insights.title: applyZoomTransform motionBlur default alignment
insights.problem: applyZoomTransform used motionBlurEnabled default true which could produce motion blur even when disabled in settings.
insights.root_cause: Default param mismatch across modules handling transforms and rendering.
insights.solution: Set motionBlurEnabled default to false in applyZoomTransform signature so motion transforms respect the disabled-by-default setting.
insights.lesson_learned: Transformation helper functions should use parameters that mirror application-level defaults to avoid silent visual discrepancies.

insights.title: Gate motion blur by motionBlurEnabled flag
insights.problem: Motion blur continued to be applied even when user toggled motion blur off (or animation used stale value).
insights.root_cause: applyZoomTransform used isPlaying and motionIntensity checks but didn't consider a motionBlurEnabled preference.
insights.solution: Added motionBlurEnabled parameter to TransformParams and used it to gate application of blurFilter and computed motionBlur amount.
insights.lesson_learned: Low-level transform functions should accept all flags that influence rendering rather than reading global state; keep transforms pure and parameterized.

src/hooks/useCameraDevices.ts.description: A React hook that enumerates video input devices when enabled, exposes the device list, selected device id, loading/error state, and handles dynamic device changes. It chooses a sensible default selection and updates when devices are added/removed via the MediaDevices devicechange event.

insights.title: Resilient selected device handling and removal when devices unplug
insights.problem: If the previously selected camera was unplugged, the hook could leave selectedDeviceId pointing to a stale id or cause wrong behavior.
insights.root_cause: Effect depended on selectedDeviceId and used closures; it didn't robustly fall back to an available device when the selected ID disappeared.
insights.solution: Use a ref to track selectedDeviceId within effect and, when loading devices, pick first available device if current selected ID is missing. Remove selectedDeviceId from effect deps to avoid unnecessary re-runs; register devicechange handler to reload devices.
insights.lesson_learned: When reacting to device lists, don't rely solely on state captured by closure — use refs or event-driven updates and always validate that selected IDs are still present in the new list.

insights.title: Set error state when enumerateDevices rejects
insights.problem: Enumeration failures (permission denied or other) weren't surfaced properly to consumers.
insights.root_cause: Previous tests and code paths assumed enumerateDevices resolves; actual rejection paths weren't asserted/handled.
insights.solution: Catch enumeration errors, set error state string, set devices to empty and isLoading to false. Tests were added to assert this behavior.
insights.lesson_learned: Always handle navigator.mediaDevices errors and expose understandable error information to the UI. Add tests covering rejection paths.

insights.title: Enumerate camera devices with permission re-request if labels are empty
insights.problem: Device labels can be empty until camera permission is granted, making it hard to display user-friendly names.
insights.root_cause: Browser privacy model hides device labels without user permission; simply calling enumerateDevices() can return unlabeled devices.
insights.solution: Added useCameraDevices hook which enumerates devices, detects missing labels and (when enabled) requests a temporary getUserMedia({video:true}) to obtain labels, stops tracks immediately, and re-enumerates. Also listens to devicechange and cleans up event listeners on unmount.

insights.title: Avoid stale selectedDeviceId on mount
insights.problem: Selected device id might remain unset if not handled correctly after enumeration.
insights.root_cause: Selected device state needed initialization after devices are loaded.
insights.solution: Set selectedDeviceId to the first discovered device when none was set yet.

test_functions: useCameraDevices
should request permission if labels are empty
should set first device as default
should list video input devices

insights.title: platformUtils refactor: synchronous -> asynchronous APIs
insights.problem: formatShortcut/isMac/getModifierKey/getShiftKey were synchronous utilities relying on navigator, not accurate in Electron. Changing them to async breaks many callers expecting sync strings.
insights.root_cause: Need for accurate platform detection in renderer required IPC to main via electronAPI.getPlatform; that is async and prompted changing utilities to async.
insights.solution: Added getPlatform() (with caching) that invokes window.electronAPI.getPlatform(); converted isMac/getModifierKey/getShiftKey/formatShortcut to async functions that await platform. Provided a navigator-based fallback for dev.
insights.lesson_learned: Converting widely used sync utils into async is a breaking change — update all call sites (components, tests) to await or handle promises. Prefer incremental approach: add new async helpers and keep legacy sync helpers until all consumers are ported.

insights.title: Cache platform result in renderer
insights.problem: Repeated IPC calls for platform detection degrade performance.
insights.root_cause: Each call previously would invoke IPC.
insights.solution: Introduced cachedPlatform variable to memoize platform after first IPC call.
insights.lesson_learned: Cache stable environment values retrieved from main to avoid unnecessary IPC overhead.

insights.title: Platform-aware keyboard shortcut formatting utility

insights.root_cause: Different places rendered modifier keys with hardcoded symbols.
insights.solution: Add formatShortcut/isMac/getModifierKey/getShiftKey helpers and replace hardcoded snippets with formatShortcut([...]).
insights.lesson_learned: Encapsulate platform specifics for UI display (modifier symbols) in a small util so all components render consistently.

insights.title: Move arrow icons to reusable SVGs and streamline figure rendering
insights.problem: Annotation overlay used React icon libraries which are not deterministic for export and caused duplication of icon-to-export logic.
insights.root_cause: UI-only icons can't be easily reproduced in export renderer; different implementations led to visual mismatch.
insights.solution: Introduced ArrowSvgs and getArrowComponent usage; simplified figure rendering to use arrow SVG components and consolidated figure types.
insights.lesson_learned: For visuals that must be exported, prefer deterministic, self-contained rendering primitives (inline SVG or canvas) rather than external icon libraries.

insights.title: Prevent click event after dragging an annotation
insights.problem: Click handler would fire immediately after a drag due to click events being emitted after drag stop, causing accidental selection toggles.
insights.root_cause: No differentiation between click and drag end; no isDragging flag.
insights.solution: Added isDraggingRef, set onDragStart/onDragStop with a short debounce to suppress click events that follow drag, and use pointer-events logic for selected vs non-selected items.
insights.lesson_learned: Distinguish user interactions (drag vs click) with state flags to prevent accidental click handlers firing post-drag.

insights.title: Support zIndex boost for selected annotation
insights.problem: Overlapping annotations made selection/editing difficult because stacking order was static.
insights.root_cause: No runtime z-index boost for selected item.
insights.solution: Added zIndex prop and isSelectedBoost flag that increases z-index when selected so the item is easier to drag/edit.
insights.lesson_learned: Expose stacking order (zIndex) in annotation model and temporarily raise z-index for focused/selected elements to avoid hit-test friction.

insights.solution: Key list by i18nKey and render localized labels via t(i18nKey, { defaultValue: label }).

insights.title: Conflict resolution UI when reassigning shortcuts

insights.solution: Show amber conflict banner with Swap and Cancel options; prevent assigning keys reserved by FIXED_SHORTCUTS; persist changes only after user saves.
insights.lesson_learned: Provide clear UX for conflict resolution (swap or cancel) instead of silently overriding; validate against fixed/reserved shortcuts and show informative errors.

insights.title: Configurable shortcuts dialog with capture mode

insights.solution: Implemented dialog that captures keydown events in capture mode, updates draft config, persists via ShortcutsContext.persistShortcuts and supports Reset to defaults. Capturing ignores pure modifier keys and uses escape to cancel.
insights.lesson_learned: Capture mode should prevent default/propagation, ignore modifier-only events, and provide a clear cancel UX (Esc). Persist changes explicitly rather than instantly to allow preview/reset.

insights.title: Fix audio desync & preserve pitch under speed regions
insights.problem: Audio would desynchronize or sound incorrect (pitch-shifted) when speedRegions were applied during exports.
insights.root_cause: Audio export pipeline previously demuxed/decoded chunks directly and attempted naive timestamp remapping; it didn't support pitch-preserving speed changes.
insights.solution: Introduce two-mode AudioProcessor: a trimmed-only fast path and a speed-aware timeline rendering path (renderPitchPreservedTimelineAudio) that uses an AudioElement + MediaRecorder via an AudioContext route to render pitch-preserved audio with playbackRate changes, then demux/re-mux the resulting audio blob into final muxer. Also fixed various decoding loops to ensure reader.cancel() is called and variable renaming fixes.
insights.lesson_learned: Pitch-preserving audio speed edits require actual playback/rendering (or sophisticated time-domain algorithms). For fidelity prefer timeline-rendered audio recorded from the platform's media pipeline, then re-demux for muxing.

insights.title: Add AudioProcessor: decode, trim-adjust, re-encode, and mux audio
insights.problem: Export pipeline previously lacked robust audio processing that respects trim regions and re-encodes to a muxable codec.
insights.root_cause: Audio track handling was missing; exporting video-only left out audio muxing and timestamp adjustments required by trims/speed changes.
insights.solution: Introduce AudioProcessor that decodes source audio (AudioDecoder), skips trimmed regions, computes trim offset timestamps, re-encodes (AudioEncoder -> Opus), and feeds encoded chunks to VideoMuxer; includes isConfigSupported checks and cancellation support.
insights.lesson_learned: Audio processing in a streaming/export pipeline must rebase timestamps for trims, confirm codec support, and avoid leaking memory by closing AudioData. Use encode/decode support checks and a cancel flag for long-running tasks.

insights.title: Clip annotation text to annotation box and implement proper word-wrapping
insights.problem: Rendered annotation text could overflow the annotation bounding box and did not wrap words the same way as the editor (visual mismatch).

insights.title: Handle Playwright page context termination when HUD closes
insights.problem: HUD window closes faster after switchToEditor, terminating the Playwright page context; hudWindow.evaluate could throw when the underlying page is closed.
insights.root_cause: evaluate() awaited resolution while switchToEditor triggered window close concurrently.
insights.solution: Wrapped the evaluate call in a try/catch around the outer context so expected page-close errors are caught and treated as expected behavior.
insights.Lesson Learned: E2E tests that control application windows must tolerate page/context termination when lifecycle actions close windows; catch expected errors and document them.

insights.title: Force software WebGL (SwiftShader) in CI for stable WebGL framebuffers
insights.problem: Headless CI environments failed to create valid WebGL framebuffers, causing PixiJS pixel reads to fail and GIF export to hang.
insights.root_cause: No GPU in CI; hardware WebGL unavailable or unreliable.
insights.solution: Add --enable-unsafe-swiftshader to the Chromium launch args in the e2e test to force SwiftShader software GL.
insights.Lesson Learned: CI headless browsers may need software GL flags for WebGL-dependent rendering tests; include launcher args in test harness.

insights.title: E2E test: GIF export from loaded video
insights.problem: Need an automated e2e test that validates full export pipeline end-to-end (renderer + main).
insights.root_cause: No E2E coverage existed for the export flow which previously broke across packaging modes.
insights.solution: Add Playwright test that launches Electron (dist-electron/main.js), intercepts save-exported-video IPC to capture exported buffer, triggers setCurrentVideoPath then switchToEditor flow, selects GIF, waits for completion and asserts the file is a valid GIF.
insights.lesson_learned: E2E tests for export pipelines should capture main-process IPC and verify binary outputs. Tests must set HEADLESS env handling and rebuild renderer prior to electron launch.

key_behaviors: enables fast, native-like demuxing of media streams
used by media export/decoding pipelines in the renderer

src/components/video-editor/VideoEditor..short_description: Main React component for the video editor UI: load/save project, manage editor state, playback controls, and export workflow.
src/components/video-editor/VideoEditor..description:
VideoEditor is the central renderer-side component that orchestrates the editor experience: it loads a video (or a recording session), initializes editor state (undoable and non-undoable), wires the preview/playback component, exposes handlers for timeline regions (zoom/trim/speed/annotation), and implements the export/save project flows. It exists to coordinate user interactions (adding/editing/removing timeline regions, settings changes, playback control) with persistence and main-process actions via window.electronAPI (open/save project, save exports, load current session/video, set unsaved changes flag). The component also bridges the UI and exporter pipeline by preparing Export settings and assembling a Project snapshot that is persisted or exported.

Design choices reflected in the file: (1) separation of undoable editor state via useEditorHistory (pushState/updateState/commitState) keeps interactive drags from spamming history; (2) non-undoable state is kept in independent useState hooks for selection, playback, and paths; (3) many derived values are memoized (currentProjectMedia, project snapshot) to keep serialization/persistence consistent; (4) effects coordinate IPC requests (load initial data, fetch telemetry) and propagate unsaved changes to the main process using window.electronAPI.setHasUnsavedChanges. The file is intentionally defensive: it validates and normalizes project payloads before applying them and guards async IPC calls with try/catch to surface localized errors.

VideoEditor is tightly coupled to VideoPlayback (preview & container refs), SettingsPanel (prop drilling for many editor flags), TimelineEditor (region editing), and exporter modules (VideoExporter/GifExporter via config prepared here). Changes to export settings, region types, or media schema will require updates across these modules; the commit history shows multiple co-changes (webcam support, cursorTelemetry propagation, motion blur flag, trim/speed regions and exporter plumbing).

key_constructs.name: VideoEditor
key_constructs.purpose: Default-exported React component that composes the editor UI, holds editor state, handles persistence and export flows.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the root component for the editor; agents editing or wiring UI behavior should start here to understand how state is created, mutated, and synchronized with the main process or exporter. Many handlers used by child components originate in this function.

key_constructs.name: applyLoadedProject
key_constructs.purpose: Validate/normalize a loaded project and apply its media and editor state to the component (including pushing to undo history).
key_constructs.reasoning: Project load normalization and ID derivation live here; edits that change project schema, media shape, or editor defaults must preserve the validation/normalization and next-id computation performed by this function.

key_constructs.name: currentProjectMedia
key_constructs.purpose: Memoized ProjectMedia resolved from videoPath/videoSourcePath and optional webcam paths; used to build project payloads and for exporter inputs.
key_constructs.reasoning: This represents the authoritative media model used for saving and exporting projects; code that creates project payloads must use the same resolution logic to avoid diverging file path formats.

key_constructs.name: saveProject
key_constructs.purpose: Serializes the current project editor state + media into a file via window.electronAPI.saveProjectFile and updates local path/snapshot state.
key_constructs.reasoning: This handles the save flow (including Save As) and sets lastSavedSnapshot; it is called by main-process save-before-close hooks and menu handlers, so its return value and side-effects (setting currentProjectPath, lastSavedSnapshot) are relied upon by main for lifecycle management.

key_constructs.name: hasUnsavedChanges
key_constructs.purpose: Boolean computed by comparing current project snapshot with lastSavedSnapshot using hasProjectUnsavedChanges.
key_constructs.reasoning: This value is pushed to the main process (window.electronAPI.setHasUnsavedChanges) and used for close/save prompts; keeping its computation unchanged is important for correct main/renderer lifecycle dialog behavior.

key_behaviors: loads a project or recording session on mount and initializes editor state
saves project files via Electron IPC and updates current project path
prepares and launches export pipelines (video/gif) and handles resulting file save dialogs
propagates unsaved change state to main process for window lifecycle
manages undo/redo and selection state for timeline regions

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or changing useEffect dependencies related to exporter/settings flags (e.g., motionBlurEnabled, trimRegions) or refs used by exporterRef
pitfalls.consequence: Exporter may capture stale settings resulting in exports that don't reflect current UI state (e.g., wrong motion blur, trim not applied).
pitfalls.prevention: Respect existing dependency arrays and ref usage; if adding settings, ensure effects that recreate exporter or related refs include them.

pitfalls.mistake: Treating saveResult.success as sole indicator that a file was persisted (ignoring missing result.path)
pitfalls.consequence: Code might assume a file exists and attempt to reveal it in the OS or present success messages while nothing was saved.
pitfalls.prevention: When handling save results require both success and a non-empty path before signaling the export as saved.

pitfalls.mistake: Auto-saving user preferences before they are hydrated on mount
pitfalls.consequence: Persisted preferences are overwritten with defaults on initial render.
pitfalls.prevention: Maintain the prefsHydrated guard and only autosave after it becomes true; do not remove this hydration gating.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing URL/path normalization logic or file:// handling without coordinating electron ipc handlers
pitfalls.consequence: Project load/save or recording session resolution can fail to find files or approve read permissions; main-process path approval logic expects normalized filesystem paths.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep fromFileUrl/toFileUrl conversion and ProjectMedia shape consistent with electron/ipc/handlers and recordingSession types.

pitfalls.mistake: Handling keyboard frame-step globally without excluding ARIA widgets or select/inputs/contentEditable
pitfalls.consequence: Native widget keyboard behavior is intercepted (broken sliders, spinbuttons, resizing handles).
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve existing guards that skip frame-step when target is input/select/textarea/contentEditable or inside ARIA roles that consume arrow keys.

key_sections: applyLoadedProject: validates and applies external project payloads and sets up editor/next IDs
useEffect(loadInitialData): logic for initial project/session/video load via window.electronAPI
saveProject: how project serialization and save-as flow works (and how lastSavedSnapshot is set)
export flow handlers (handleExport/handleExportSaved/unsavedExport logic): how export is started and how unsaved exported blobs are retained on dialog cancel
skip_unless_needed: Large JSX render / markup for layout and child components (unless modifying UI structure or passing props)
Detailed region CRUD handlers if only changing save/export plumbing

insights.title: Fix import order / type error and hasProjectUnsavedChanges invocation
insights.problem: Type/import ordering caused a type error after PR changes; hasProjectUnsavedChanges call split across multiple lines caused formatting issues.
insights.root_cause: Reordered imports inadvertently; createProjectSnapshot and hasProjectUnsavedChanges ordering mismatch.
insights.solution: Reordered imports to resolve type error and simplified hasProjectUnsavedChanges call to a single-line invocation.
insights.Lesson Learned: Maintain import order consistency; prefer normalized/centralized editor normalization before comparing snapshots to avoid subtle type mismatches.

insights.title: Switch 'New Recording' dialog to use startNewRecording IPC
insights.problem: Editor UI previously used clearCurrentVideoPath + switchToHud to start new recording; this was refactored to a single startNewRecording IPC.
insights.root_cause: Window/session lifecycle needed an atomic action to clear session and show HUD safely.
insights.solution: handleNewRecordingConfirm now calls window.electronAPI.startNewRecording() and handles success/error results.
insights.Lesson Learned: Encapsulate complex multi-step main-process operations behind a single IPC call to reduce race conditions between windows.

insights.title: Introduce webcamSizePreset propagation throughout editor state
insights.problem: Webcam size preset feature added and the editor needed to store/propagate webcamSizePreset to playback, exporter, settings panel.
insights.root_cause: New UI control requires editor state, persistence, and exporter plumbing.
insights.solution: Added webcamSizePreset references in editor state creation, pushes, updateState/commitState calls and passed to SettingsPanel/VideoPlayback/Exporters.
insights.Lesson Learned: Adding a UI preference often requires widespread propagation; ensure persistence and exporter usage are updated together to avoid inconsistencies.

insights.title: Persist user settings and avoid overwriting saved prefs on initial render
insights.problem: Auto-saving settings immediately on mount overwrote persisted preferences with defaults before they were loaded.
insights.root_cause: The auto-save effect ran before loadUserPreferences completed because the hydration guard used useRef in a way that didn't trigger effect dependencies correctly (race condition).
insights.solution: Introduce a hydration flag (initially implemented as useRef, later changed to useState per review) and only auto-save after prefsHydrated/prefsLoadedRef is set. Load persisted preferences once on mount and update local state, then enable auto-save effect that depends on the hydrated flag.
insights.lesson_learned: When loading persisted state asynchronously in a component, gate side-effectful auto-saves behind a hydration flag using useState (not useRef) so React dependency tracking prevents premature writes.

insights.title: Make starting a new recording robust with proper error handling and localized UI
insights.problem: Starting a new recording from the editor could fail silently and the dialog could close prematurely; messages weren't localized.
insights.root_cause: The dialog was dismissed before asynchronous IPC calls completed, and errors were not caught/reported. Static strings used instead of i18n for the dialog.
insights.solution: Wrap clearCurrentVideoPath / setCurrentRecordingSession / switchToHud calls in try/catch, only close dialog after success, log and surface an error message on failure. Replace static dialog strings with i18n keys.
insights.lesson_learned: Do not dismiss UI state before async cleanup completes; always handle IPC promise rejections and localize UI strings.

insights.title: Skip frame-step keyboard handling for ARIA widgets that own arrow keys
insights.problem: The new arrow-key frame-step feature intercepted arrow keys even when focus was on ARIA widgets such as sliders, spinbuttons, or panel resize handles, breaking native keyboard behavior.
insights.root_cause: Original guard only ignored inputs and textareas; it didn't consider select elements, contentEditable elements, or ARIA roles that consume arrow keys.
insights.solution: Expand the guard to skip frame-step when target is HTMLSelectElement, contentEditable, or within elements with roles [role="separator"], [role="slider"], [role="spinbutton"].
insights.lesson_learned: When adding global keyboard shortcuts, explicitly exclude native/form controls and ARIA widgets to avoid stealing input. Consider accessibility and role-based behaviors.

insights.title: Frame-step navigation via Arrow keys (no modifiers)
insights.problem: Users needed a way to step frame-by-frame using keyboard.
insights.root_cause: No frame-step keyboard navigation existed.
insights.solution: Add computeFrameStepTime utility (src/lib/frameStep.ts) and handle ArrowLeft/ArrowRight (no modifiers) in VideoEditor to compute new time and call handleSeek. Introduced refs for currentTime and duration to avoid stale closures.
insights.lesson_learned: When wiring keyboard-driven time-based actions, use refs to capture frequently-updated values to avoid stale state, and add unit tests for timing math.

insights.title: Thread cursorTelemetry and zoom focusMode throughout editor & exporter
insights.problem: Auto-follow zoom features needed the same cursor telemetry during playback and export; several components required changes.
insights.root_cause: Cursor telemetry and focusMode were implemented for playback but not included in export/config plumbing.
insights.solution: Add focusMode to ZoomRegion type, pass cursorTelemetry to playback components, frame renderer, gif/video exporters, and maintain smoothing logic in both playback and rendering code.
insights.lesson_learned: Features that affect both UI playback and exported output create cross-cutting changes; plan the threading of telemetry/state through all related modules to avoid visual divergence.

insights.title: Support fullscreen video player and ESC handling
insights.problem: Editor had no fullscreen mode for the video preview.
insights.root_cause: No state or container switching to show a full-viewport player.
insights.solution: Added isFullscreen state, playerContainerRef, toggleFullscreen callback, Escape key handler to exit fullscreen, and conditional container class that switches to fixed inset-0 fullscreen style. Wired PlaybackControls to toggle fullscreen.

insights.title: Guard saved export path before treating as success
insights.problem: Export saveResult could be marked success without a path present, causing downstream code to assume a path exists (e.g., notifications, reopening).
insights.root_cause: saveResult.success was being used as sole indicator, but the result shape includes both success and optional path; missing path should not be treated as a saved export.
insights.solution: Change success branch checks to require saveResult.path in addition to saveResult.success before calling handleExportSaved.

insights.title: Allow re-saving exported output if user cancels save dialog
insights.problem: When the user canceled the OS save dialog, exported data (blob/arrayBuffer) was lost and user couldn't retry without re-exporting.
insights.root_cause: Export flow immediately discarded the generated export data on dialog cancel.
insights.solution: Added unsavedExport state to hold arrayBuffer, fileName, and format when a save dialog is canceled; provided handleSaveUnsavedExport to re-open save dialog and finalize saving. Hooked SettingsPanel to render a 'Choose Save Location' CTA when unsavedExport exists.

insights.title: Support for webcam video path and session-based media model
insights.problem: Existing editor assumed a single videoPath per project; with webcam overlay support the editor needed to support optional webcamVideoPath and to load 'recording sessions' stored by the recorder.
insights.root_cause: Project data format was legacy (videoPath string) and editor state only tracked a single video path, so adding a second video required data model changes and migration logic.
insights.solution: Introduce currentProjectMedia memo derived from videoPath/webcamVideoPath and project media model; add loading from current recording session via window.electronAPI.getCurrentRecordingSession; pass webcamVideoPath to playback and exporters; update createProjectData usage to include media object.
insights.lesson_learned: Evolve project schema to explicit media object for multi-source projects and implement backward-compatible resolution for legacy videoPath fields. Prefer central media shape (ProjectMedia) to propagate into export/rendering stacks.

insights.title: PanelGroup layout restructuring
insights.problem: VideoEditor layout needed reorganization to support new right-hand settings panel and improved resizing.
insights.root_cause: Old fixed flex layout made it awkward to add new resizable settings panel.
insights.solution: Refactor markup to use PanelGroup/Panel components (split left/top/timeline/right) and add PanelResizeHandle for clearer UX.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding substantial UI features (webcam preview/settings), reorganize layout into composable panels for easier future expansions.

insights.title: Adopt undo/redo history (useEditorHistory) and move editor state to history
insights.problem: Editor state changes (sliders, padding, zoom/trim/annotation edits) were not undoable or caused noisy history entries during drags.
insights.root_cause: All editor state was stored as independent useState hooks; no centralized history or checkpointing for continuous interactions.
insights.solution: Introduce useEditorHistory hook and move undoable pieces (zoomRegions, trimRegions, speedRegions, annotationRegions, crop, wallpaper, padding, borderRadius, aspectRatio, shadow, motionBlur) into editorState managed by pushState/updateState/commitState; use pushState for discrete changes, updateState for live dragging with commitState on end. Wire undo/redo keyboard handling and shortcut UI.
insights.lesson_learned: Implement a small history abstraction with push/update/commit to avoid flooding history during interactive drags. Keep selection IDs out of undoable state to avoid surprising rollbacks.

insights.title: Sync unsaved changes to main process and respond to save-before-close
insights.problem: Main process could not prompt properly because it didn't know if editor had unsaved changes; renderer needed to perform save and notify main.
insights.root_cause: No IPC channel from renderer to main to indicate unsaved state or to respond to a save request before close.
insights.solution: Call window.electronAPI.setHasUnsavedChanges(hasUnsavedChanges) in a useEffect and register onRequestSaveBeforeClose to run saveProject(false) and return cleanup. This allows main to prompt Save & Close and wait for save-before-close-done.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep main and renderer in sync for lifecycle-sensitive state (unsaved changes) using explicit IPC and listener cleanup; ensure the renderer exposes a handler that returns a remover.

insights.title: Load cursor telemetry and add zoom suggestion hook
insights.problem: Auto-zoom suggestions needed cursor telemetry files produced during recording.
insights.root_cause: No telemetry loading existed in the editor for recorded files.
insights.solution: Add effect to call window.electronAPI.getCursorTelemetry(fromFileUrl(videoPath)) and store samples in state; wired TimelineEditor to accept cursorTelemetry and exposed onZoomSuggested callback to add suggested zoom regions.
insights.lesson_learned: Editor importing of supplemental telemetry files complements video metadata; provide robust fromFileUrl conversion for file:// urls.

insights.title: Support 'native' aspect ratio mode
insights.problem: Users wanted to export at cropped video's actual aspect ratio with zero padding.
insights.root_cause: Aspect ratio dropdown only exposed fixed ratios; native cropping requires computing ratio from crop/video dims.
insights.solution: Add 'native' to AspectRatio list and implement getNativeAspectRatioValue(videoWidth, videoHeight, cropRegion), plus wire UI to set padding to 0 when selecting native.
insights.lesson_learned: Introduce feature flag values (like 'native') carefully and ensure both preview and export logic accept native semantics.

insights.title: Add speedRegions feature and project persistence integration
insights.problem: Introduce playback speed regions and wire them through playback, timeline, exporter and settings.
insights.root_cause: New editor feature requires adding state, handlers, wiring to playback and exporter, and persistence of project state.
insights.solution: Added speedRegions state, selection handling, CRUD handlers, passed speedRegions to VideoPlayback, FrameRenderer/exporter, and SettingsPanel; added project save/load normalization and project path tracking.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding new timeline region types: (1) add typed state and defaults, (2) ensure selection interactions clear other selections, (3) propagate to playback and export pipelines, and (4) include in project save/load and effect dependency lists.

insights.title: Reset exportedFilePath timing and show 'Show in Folder' action
insights.problem: Exported file path was reset too early and user couldn't reveal file after export; no robust reveal path fallback.
insights.root_cause: State for exportedFilePath was cleared at wrong time; reveal-in-folder not implemented.
insights.solution: Keep exportedFilePath until dialog close, provide toast action and ExportDialog button that call revealInFolder with fallback handling.
insights.lesson_learned: Persist exported path until user dismisses UI; handle platform-level reveal errors and show helpful messages.

insights.title: Project load: validate and normalize project payload
insights.problem: Loading arbitrary JSON could break editor state if fields are missing or malformed.
insights.root_cause: No validation/normalization of project JSON leading to potential runtime errors or corrupt state.
insights.solution: Added validateProjectData and normalizeProjectEditor to sanitize ranges, clamp numbers, fill defaults, and compute next IDs. Also update UI state robustly.
insights.lesson_learned: Always validate and normalize external inputs (project files) before applying to app state. Compute next IDs to avoid collisions.

insights.title: Motion blur default synchronized with SettingsPanel
insights.problem: VideoEditor had motionBlurEnabled default true, inconsistent with the intended default behavior.
insights.root_cause: State initialization in VideoEditor did not match SettingsPanel defaults and exporter defaults.
insights.solution: Set useState(false) for motionBlurEnabled in VideoEditor so UI state and settings panel default match.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep component-level initial state aligned with settings defaults and downstream export/rendering defaults to avoid surprises.

insights.title: Remove duplicate semicolon in useEffect cleanup
insights.problem: Minor lint/style issue: stray extra semicolon after useEffect.
insights.root_cause: Typo left extra semicolon.
insights.solution: Removed extra semicolon.
insights.lesson_learned: Small stylistic issues are fixed during routine cleanup; linting/formatter (biome) helps catch these.

insights.title: Add exportQuality state and size/bitrate selection
insights.problem: Export previously always used source resolution/bitrate heuristics; there was no UI-driven quality preset.
insights.root_cause: No typed quality setting to control export resolution/bitrate.
insights.solution: Added exportQuality state, passed to SettingsPanel, and changed export sizing/bitrate calculation: 'source' uses original, 'good'/'medium' produce targetHeight 1080/720 with bitrate mapping.
insights.lesson_learned: Expose export tuning options in UI and keep exporter logic aligned with these presets. Ensure resolution math produces even dimensions for codecs.

insights.title: Avoid small off-by-one / even-dimension issues in export dimensions
insights.problem: Codec encoders (AV1/VP9) often require even dimensions; previous rounding sometimes left odd sizes.
insights.root_cause: Export dimension calculations didn't consistently enforce even numbers.
insights.solution: Ensure exportWidth/exportHeight are even (Math.floor(.../2)*2) and iterate to find dimensions matching requested aspect ratio when needed.
insights.lesson_learned: Always produce encoder-friendly dimensions (even numbers) when computing scaled export sizes; test against multiple aspect ratios.

insights.title: Annotations: store type-specific fields and wire exporter preview dimensions
insights.problem: Annotation content was shared via a single 'content' field resulting in content loss when switching types; export renderer had no preview dimensions for correct scaling.
insights.root_cause: Single 'content' field tried to represent text, image data, and other payloads; exporter lacked knowledge of preview container size for consistent scaling.
insights.solution: Store textContent/imageContent per annotation, initialize DEFAULT_FIGURE_DATA for figure annotations, pass previewWidth/previewHeight to VideoExporter, and include annotationRegions in export config.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep structured per-type storage for rich annotation types so switching types doesn't lose user-entered data; exporter needs preview metrics to render overlays accurately.

insights.title: Remove noisy console.log debugging statements
insights.problem: Numerous console.log statements scattered in VideoEditor created noisy output.
insights.root_cause: Temporary debug logs were left in production code.
insights.solution: Removed many console.log calls throughout region add/change/delete handlers.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid leaving verbose debug logs in code; prefer structured, named logs where needed.

insights.title: Stale closure for motion blur and export dependencies
insights.problem: A useEffect that (re)creates/tears down exporterRef depended on a subset of UI flags; toggling motion blur could produce stale exporter state leading to exports with old settings.
insights.root_cause: motionBlurEnabled (new feature) wasn't included in the dependency array for the effect that resets exporterRef, causing closures to capture outdated values.
insights.solution: Added motionBlurEnabled and trimRegions to the dependency array so exporter is recreated when these settings change.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding UI flags that influence export/render behavior, ensure all such flags are included in effect dependencies or accessed via refs to avoid stale closures.

insights.title: Trim integration in editor -> exporter path
insights.problem: Trim regions (new feature) needed to be surfaced into export pipeline and UI flows.
insights.root_cause: Trim data was only in the timeline UI and not passed into exporter or playback components.
insights.solution: Added trimRegions state, selection handlers, wired trimRegions into VideoPlayback and VideoExporter config, and added UI callbacks (onTrimAdded, onTrimSpanChange, onTrimDelete).
insights.lesson_learned: Feature additions frequently require plumbing through multiple layers (UI state -> playback -> exporter); plan the data model early and add tests that exercise the full flow.

insights.title: Export aspect resolution / bitrate calculation fixed
insights.problem: Export dimensions and bitrate were computed using source video width/height directly, producing incorrect aspect-cropped exports and possibly odd encoder configs.
insights.root_cause: Export used raw videoWidth/videoHeight rather than a target aspect ratio and even dimensions; bitrate decisions used wrong pixel count.
insights.solution: Compute an exportWidth/exportHeight that conforms to target 16:9 aspect ratio, ensure even dimensions, and compute totalPixels from export resolution before choosing bitrate.
insights.lesson_learned: Export resolution must be normalized (aspect ratio + even dimensions) before downstream steps (encoder config, bitrate calculation). Keep explicit rounding to even numbers to satisfy many encoders.

src/components/video-editor/VideoPlaybac.short_description: Preview component that renders the video + webcam overlay using PixiJS, handles per-frame transforms (zoom/focus), motion blur, trims, speed regions and user interactions.
src/components/video-editor/VideoPlaybac.description:
VideoPlayback is a forwardRef React component that embeds a PixiJS Application to render the main video (and optional webcam PiP) with composite layout, zoom transforms, blur/shadow, and overlayed annotations. It synchronizes HTMLVideoElement(s) with the timeline (currentTime, isPlaying), applies speed/trim rules, and exposes imperative methods (play, pause) and refs (video element, Pixi app, containerRef) required by editor and exporter code paths. The component implements interactive behavior: dragging to change zoom focus, dragging webcam PiP position, and selecting annotations/zoom regions through pointer handlers on an overlay element. It also includes resilient readiness checks for video frames and runtime logic to avoid race conditions between PixiJS and HTMLVideo readiness.

The file is where the preview semantics live: layoutVideoContent computes sizes and base transforms using compositeLayout utilities; per-frame animation state and zoom transforms are computed via zoomTransform utilities and smoothing logic for auto-follow using cursor telemetry. Performance-sensitive flags (motion blur) are handled via refs to avoid re-render churn during per-frame operations. The component also maintains synchronization logic for a secondary webcam video element and adjusts its playbackRate and seeks to match the main video when speedRegions apply.

VideoPlayback is used by VideoEditor and FrameRenderer/FrameRenderer-like exporter logic mirrors many of its algorithms. Because playback uses PixiJS and HTMLMediaElements, changes here must respect resource lifecycles and cleanup (destroying Pixi Application, cancelling RAF loops, releasing pointer captures). Several commits fixed subtle timing, drift, and readiness issues — those areas are sensitive to change and tied to cross-file exporter behavior.

key_constructs.name: VideoPlayback
key_constructs.purpose: ForwardRef React component that renders the preview using PixiJS and exposes an imperative VideoPlaybackRef.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the entry point for preview rendering; changes here ripple into layout, exporter preview sizing, and user interactions. Agents should consult it when updating rendering behavior or props contract.

key_constructs.name: VideoPlaybackRef
key_constructs.purpose: Type describing imperative methods/refs exposed to parent: video element, pixi Application, sprite, containerRef, play/pause functions.
key_constructs.reasoning: The exporter and VideoEditor rely on these methods and refs to control playback and to read preview container dimensions; modifying the interface requires coordinated updates where it's consumed.

key_constructs.name: layoutVideoContent
key_constructs.purpose: Compute layout (stage size, base scale, offsets, webcam rect, mask) and apply it to the Pixi stage/containers; caches results into refs for per-frame transforms.
key_constructs.reasoning: This centralizes layout logic and delegates to layoutVideoContentUtil. Editors changing padding, webcam presets, mask shapes or crop behavior must keep this function consistent with computeCompositeLayout used by the exporter.

key_constructs.name: updateFocusFromClientPoint
key_constructs.purpose: Translate pointer client coordinates into normalized zoom focus and apply clamping and onZoomFocusChange callbacks.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function contains pointer-to-focus math used for interactive focus dragging. Changing coordinate math or clamping behavior requires verifying UI pointer interactions and export focus consistency.

key_constructs.name: handleWebcamPointerDown
key_constructs.purpose: Begin dragging of webcam PiP (picture-in-picture layout) and record drag offsets for later pointermove events.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is part of the PiP positioning UX; changes affect how webcamPosition updates are emitted and must preserve pointer capture/release semantics and interaction guards (e.g., disallow while playing).

key_behaviors: initializes and tears down a PixiJS Application for preview rendering
keeps main video and optional webcam element synchronized (play/pause/seek/playbackRate)
applies zoom transforms and focus smoothing (auto-follow) with configurable depth and smoothing factors
filters visible annotations and ensures selected annotation remains visible for editing
skips over trimmed regions during playback and applies speed regions to playbackRate

pitfalls.mistake: Relying on a single requestAnimationFrame or DOM read to determine video readiness
pitfalls.consequence: Pixi or frame rendering may occur before the media has valid dimensions producing blank/mis-sized frames or failed layout.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the existing RAF-loop readiness checks (videoReadyRafRef) and readyState/dimension gating before marking videoReady.

pitfalls.mistake: Using React state for per-frame or high-frequency flags like motionBlurAmount
pitfalls.consequence: Excessive re-renders or stale closure behaviour in per-frame animation loops; reduced animation performance.
pitfalls.prevention: Use refs (motionBlurAmountRef/motionBlurStateRef) for frequently-read booleans/numbers and preserve effect updates that sync them.

pitfalls.mistake: Not syncing webcam playbackRate/currentTime with speedRegions logic
pitfalls.consequence: Visual drift between screen video and webcam overlay (out-of-sync behavior), especially when speed regions change.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep webcam synchronization logic intact; when modifying playbackRate logic follow patterns used here to clamp/seek webcam element when drift > threshold.

pitfalls.mistake: Forgetting to destroy Pixi Application and cancel RAF on unmount or path change
pitfalls.consequence: Memory leaks, orphaned animation frames, or multiple audio/video resources in memory.

insights.title: Propagate webcamSizePreset to layout and renderer
insights.problem: Video playback/layout functions needed the numeric webcam size to compute webcam rendering dimensions.
insights.root_cause: Webcam size model changed to numeric percent; playback needed to accept and pass the new value into composite layout.
insights.solution: Added webcamSizePreset param in props and passed it into computeCompositeLayout and pixi frame setup; ensured cleanups and destroy semantics remained intact.
insights.Lesson Learned: When layout configuration types change, update all rendering call sites to accept new parameters to avoid mismatches between preview and exported layouts.

insights.title: Sync webcam preview playback speed with main video and speed regions
insights.problem: Webcam overlay playback could drift/be out of sync with main video especially when speedRegions are applied, causing visual desynchronization between screen and webcam overlays.
insights.root_cause: Webcam video element wasn't using speed region data or properly adjusting playbackRate/currentTime on play/pause transitions.
insights.solution: Query active speedRegion based on currentTime and set webcamVideo.playbackRate accordingly; also clamp resets and seek the webcam element when time drift > threshold; ensure pause/resume adjusts currentTime appropriately.
insights.lesson_learned: When rendering a secondary media element synchronized to a timeline with variable playback rates, replicate timeline speed decisions (speedRegions) and aggressively correct drift (thresholded seeks) to maintain visual alignment.

insights.title: Playback component motionBlur default disabled
insights.problem: VideoPlayback component default parameter for motionBlurEnabled was true which could lead to preview differences vs exporter.
insights.root_cause: Default parameter value in the playback component signature was not aligned with the settings/executor defaults.
insights.solution: Change the default parameter motionBlurEnabled = false to match SettingsPanel and exporter defaults.
insights.lesson_learned: Defaults should be aligned across playback, editor, and exporter; prefer explicit props over implicit defaults where possible.

insights.title: Robust ready-state handling for video readiness (prevent race with PixiJS)
insights.problem: Render pipeline assumed video had dimensions and frame data after a simple double requestAnimationFrame; in some environments this was not reliable, causing blank or mis-sized frames.
insights.root_cause: Relying on requestAnimationFrame twice didn't guarantee media element had data or dimensions (readyState).
insights.solution: Introduced a requestAnimationFrame loop (videoReadyRafRef) that checks video.videoWidth/videoHeight and readyState >= HAVE_CURRENT_DATA before marking video ready, with cleanup on unmount or path changes.
insights.lesson_learned: Media readiness should be detected from media properties (readyState and dimensions). Use a controlled RAF loop and cleanup to avoid leaked animation frames.

insights.title: Expose containerRef to allow VideoEditor to read preview dimensions
insights.problem: Exporter needed preview container size for proper annotation scaling but VideoPlayback didn't expose container element.
insights.root_cause: UI-only component kept internal refs.
insights.solution: Added containerRef to VideoPlaybackRef and passed containerRef to parent so exporter can query clientWidth/clientHeight.
insights.lesson_learned: When renderer/export paths require DOM metrics, expose refs via component APIs rather than querying DOM by selector.

insights.title: Filter displayed annotations to include selected annotation outside time window
insights.problem: Selected annotation could be hidden when playhead moved slightly outside its range making editing awkward.
insights.root_cause: Filtering logic only included annotations strictly active at current time.
insights.solution: When computing visible annotations, always include the selectedAnnotationId regardless of time filter.
insights.lesson_learned: For editing, prefer to show the selected object even if it momentarily falls outside its active time range to avoid surprising disappearance while editing.

insights.title: Skip playback into trimmed regions
insights.problem: While playing, the video would continue through regions that the user marked as trimmed rather than skipping them.
insights.root_cause: Time updates and seek handlers didn't consult trimRegions and could remain inside a trimmed span.
insights.solution: Added trimRegions prop and a ref (trimRegionsRef), implemented logic in event handlers to detect active trim region and skip to its end (or pause if end beyond duration).
insights.lesson_learned: Playback control logic must mirror timeline edits (like trims). Using refs to hold frequently-read flags reduces stale closure issues inside animation loops.

insights.title: Motion blur flag moved to ref for animation pipeline
insights.problem: Motion blur toggles needed to be used in animation loop and filter decisions without causing expensive re-initialization.
insights.root_cause: React state updates inside tight rendering loops cause re-renders; using state directly caused stale closure or unnecessary updates.
insights.solution: Introduce motionBlurEnabledRef updated in an effect; pass its current value into places that compute per-frame motion blur.
insights.lesson_learned: For per-frame animation filters, store frequently-read booleans in refs to avoid re-render churn and stale closure pitfalls.

insights.title: Microtask double requestAnimationFrame hack for Pixi readiness
insights.problem: Sometimes the renderer marked video ready before PixiJS or video frames were fully available, causing missing frames on first render.
insights.root_cause: Race between DOM readiness and Pixi canvas setup.
insights.solution: Wrap setVideoReady(true) in two nested requestAnimationFrame calls to delay readiness until next frame tick.
insights.lesson_learned: Rendering initialization timing can be fragile; prefer deterministic readiness signals from lower-level libraries if available. Use small delays only as last resort and document why.

electron/electron-env.d.ts.short_description: Ambient TypeScript declarations for Electron main/preload environment and window.electronAPI
electron/electron-env.d.ts.description:
This file provides ambient TypeScript declarations used by the renderer and shared code to get accurate types for the runtime environment created by the Electron main process and the preload script. It declares the NodeJS.ProcessEnv shape (a small subset used by the app: APP_ROOT and VITE_PUBLIC), typings for the global Window.electronAPI surface (the contextBridge API exposed in electron/preload.ts), and small domain types ProcessedDesktopSource and CursorTelemetryPoint used across renderer code. The primary purpose is to keep renderer TypeScript code compiled and to provide compile-time safety when calling main-side functionality through window.electronAPI.

It exists because the preload script (electron/preload.ts) exposes many functions to the renderer via contextBridge, but those are not part of the DOM or NodeJS default lib. By declaring them here, components such as the VideoEditor and hooks (useScreenRecorder, etc.) can call window.electronAPI.getSources(), storeRecordedSession(), setCurrentRecordingSession(), setLocale(), etc., with correct types. The file intentionally imports RecordingSession type references via relative import paths so the declarations align with the source types in src/lib/recordingSession. The commit history shows this file has been updated in the past when preload API was extended (e.g., startNewRecording, getPlatform) — so it must be kept synchronized with preload.ts and ipc handlers.

Because this file is an ambient declaration, changes here do not affect runtime behavior directly but will affect TypeScript checks and developer productivity. The declarations must match the actual functions exposed by electron/preload.ts and the main process handlers (electron/ipc/handlers.ts); otherwise, the renderer will have stale or incorrect type information leading to compile-time mismatch or runtime surprises for developers who rely on types.

key_constructs.name: NodeJS.ProcessEnv
key_constructs.purpose: Describes environment variables the app expects at runtime (APP_ROOT and VITE_PUBLIC).
key_constructs.reasoning: When code reads process.env.APP_ROOT or VITE_PUBLIC (e.g., main or build-time logic), TypeScript will know these keys exist and their intended use. Keep these names consistent with build scripts and vite/electron config.

key_constructs.name: Window
key_constructs.purpose: Augments the global Window with electronAPI that matches the functions exposed by preload.ts.
key_constructs.reasoning: Most renderer modules call window.electronAPI.*. Any addition/removal/shape change in preload.ts must be reflected here to keep compile-time correctness.

key_constructs.name: ProcessedDesktopSource
key_constructs.purpose: Represents a normalized desktop capture source returned by getSources (id, name, display_id, thumbnail, appIcon).
key_constructs.reasoning: Used widely in renderer components that present or select screen/app sources; declarations must match the structure produced by main/ipc handlers.

key_constructs.name: CursorTelemetryPoint
key_constructs.purpose: Represents a single cursor telemetry sample used by editor/exporter to overlay cursor movement (timeMs, cx, cy).
key_constructs.reasoning: Export and editor code rely on this shape to compute cursor-based annotations and exports; mismatches will cause type errors and subtle runtime bugs when shape assumptions change.

key_behaviors: provides compile-time typings for the electron contextBridge API
documents expected environment variables (APP_ROOT, VITE_PUBLIC)
exposes domain types used across renderer and preload like ProcessedDesktopSource and CursorTelemetryPoint

pitfalls.mistake: Modifying electron/preload.ts to add/remove methods without updating this file
pitfalls.consequence: TypeScript type mismatches in renderer (compile errors) or stale types that mislead developers about available APIs
pitfalls.prevention: Always update the ambient declarations when changing the preload/API surface; run typecheck (npx tsc --noEmit) after changes

pitfalls.mistake: Changing the import path used in type references (e.g., to RecordingSession) without ensuring the relative path resolves from this d.ts file
pitfalls.consequence: TypeScript cannot resolve referenced types, producing import errors or incorrect types in the renderer
pitfalls.prevention: Keep import paths aligned with repository layout and verify with full typecheck; prefer the same relative paths used by other declarations (commit history shows prior edits)

pitfalls.mistake: Altering APP_ROOT or VITE_PUBLIC semantics in build scripts without reflecting that in these env typings
pitfalls.consequence: Confusing assumptions in code that depends on APP_ROOT/VITE_PUBLIC leading to build/runtime path mismatches
pitfalls.prevention: When build outputs or directory structure changes, update the docstring and usages and run the build/test matrix

src/vite-env.d.ts.short_description: Renderer-side ambient types including Vite and electron API surface for in-browser development
src/vite-env.d.ts.description:
This declaration file is placed under src and is used primarily by renderer code compiled via Vite. It merges Vite client typings (/// <reference types="vite/client" />) with the application's electron API ambient definitions so that code under src can refer to window.electronAPI with correct types in both dev and production. It duplicates the electronAPI shape declared in electron/electron-env.d.ts but uses import paths relative to src (e.g., import("./lib/recordingSession")) so that TS resolution works during renderer compilation.

It exists to allow the renderer to be developed against a typed API even when running in a Vite dev server (where the electron preload may not be present). Many renderer modules (VideoEditor, hooks, exporter) rely on these types. The file therefore acts as a bridge between vite's type environment and the Electron-specific ambient declarations. As with the sibling electron-env.d.ts file, any change to the preload/exposed API or the RecordingSession shape must be mirrored here; the repository has historically required synchronous updates to both declarations (commit history demonstrates edits adding startNewRecording and getPlatform).

key_constructs.reasoning: Used by components under src (LaunchWindow, SourceSelector, VideoEditor) to type the objects returned by getSources and selectSource.

key_constructs.purpose: Shape of cursor telemetry sample used by editor/exporter.
key_constructs.reasoning: Renderer export/UI code expects consistent structure for cursor samples; changes here must mirror exporter expectations.

key_constructs.name: Window
key_constructs.purpose: Augments the window global for the renderer build with the electronAPI surface.
key_constructs.reasoning: Because this file lives in src it ensures Vite/renderer TypeScript resolves types while developing without an actual preload present.

key_behaviors: exposes electronAPI types to renderer code during Vite dev and builds
ensures import paths for referenced types resolve correctly from src
duplicates the electron-env type surface so both dev and production compiles are typed
