src/lib/exporter/frameRenderer.ts.short_description: Pixi-based offscreen renderer that composites video, webcam overlay, background, masks, blur, shadow and annotations for export frames
src/lib/exporter/frameRenderer.ts.description:
FrameRenderer is the export-side rendering implementation responsible for producing pixel-perfect frames for the export pipeline. It exists to reproduce the editor's preview visuals deterministically in an offscreen canvas: background (image/color/gradient), cropped / scaled main video texture, optional webcam overlay, rounded-corner masks, blur and motion-blur filters, drop shadows, and annotation drawing. The class uses PixiJS to perform GPU-accelerated composition of the main video content and a separate set of 2D canvases for final CPU-side compositing and deterministic readback.

The implementation is explicitly designed to be resilient across platforms. It maintains a rasterCanvas & rasterCtx to receive CPU-side ImageData (gl.readPixels fallback) so downstream code does not rely on implicit GPU->2D canvas sharing (a known failure mode on some Linux/Wayland stacks). The renderer caches layout information (layoutCache) so zoom/transform and mask geometry calculations can be consistently applied when computing camera transforms or composing shadows. It also threads cursor telemetry and smoothing state through the export pipeline to match in-editor auto-follow behavior.

key_constructs.name: FrameRenderer
key_constructs.purpose: Encapsulates all state and logic to render a single composited export frame (video + optional webcam + background + masks + shadow + annotations) to an offscreen canvas.
key_constructs.reasoning: This class centralizes GPU (PixiJS) stage composition and CPU compositing/readback so exporters (GIF/MP4) can request deterministic pixel output per frame. It stores and reuses Pixi objects, shader/filter state, layout cache and smoothing state, which is important because per-frame initialization would be expensive and platform-sensitive.

key_constructs.name: initialize
key_constructs.purpose: Creates Pixi Application, configures filters, prepares background canvas and CPU compositing canvases, and sets up mask graphics.
key_constructs.reasoning: initialize must be called before renderFrame; it constructs the WebGL-backed Pixi renderer and the separate 2D canvases used for compositing and readback. It contains compatibility guards (e.g., canvas.colorSpace try/catch) and throws if critical 2D contexts can't be acquired, so callers should await it and handle errors.

key_constructs.name: setupBackground
key_constructs.purpose: Renders the configured wallpaper (solid color, image, linear/radial gradient) into a dedicated background canvas used later during final compositing.
key_constructs.reasoning: Background rendering is done on a CPU canvas because it should not be affected by zoom transforms and must be composited deterministically. setupBackground handles cross-origin decisions, gradient parsing, image cover/center math and fallbacks on errors.

key_constructs.name: renderFrame
key_constructs.purpose: Main per-frame entry: accepts a VideoFrame (and optional webcamVideoFrame + timestamp), updates the Pixi texture, advances animation state, applies zoom/motion blur transforms, renders the Pixi stage, and delegates final compositing (shadows, webcam overlay, masks) to CPU canvases, then draws annotations.
key_constructs.reasoning: renderFrame bridges the streaming decoder output (VideoFrame) and the export pipeline. It ensures textures are replaced safely, animation smoothing is applied, and that readback path is robust (reads ImageData into a VideoFrame for the encoder). It also includes safety around encoder stalls because exporter relies on deterministic per-frame output.

key_constructs.name: updateLayout
key_constructs.purpose: Calculates layout (scale, sprite size/position, mask rect and base offsets) for the current config and caches those values in layoutCache.
key_constructs.reasoning: updateLayout mirrors editor layout computation (computeCompositeLayout) to ensure exported geometry matches the preview: cropping math, padding->viewportScale conversion, webcam size/preset handling, and mask rounding. The layoutCache is later used by applyZoomTransform and clampFocus utilities.

key_behaviors: creates an offscreen Pixi Application and stage for video composition
uploads VideoFrame content into a Pixi Texture and replaces it per frame
computes and caches layout/mask geometry to ensure export matches preview
performs robust CPU readback for cross-platform deterministic pixels
composites background, video, webcam overlay, shadow and annotations into a final canvas

pitfalls.mistake: Assume drawImage(canvas) from a WebGL-backed canvas will always return correct pixels
pitfalls.consequence: On some Linux/Wayland drivers implicit sharing fails and exported frames become green/empty.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the explicit readback path (rasterCanvas & readPixels fallback) and avoid depending on GPU->2D implicit sharing.

pitfalls.mistake: Recreate Pixi Application per frame or before calling initialize
pitfalls.consequence: Huge performance penalty and potential memory/resource leaks; code expects initialize() to be called once and reused.
pitfalls.prevention: Only call initialize once and ensure app is non-null before renderFrame; the code already throws if not initialized.

pitfalls.mistake: Destroy textures incorrectly or forget to close VideoFrame buffers
pitfalls.consequence: Memory leaks and WebCodecs issues during long exports.
pitfalls.prevention: When replacing textures, preserve pattern used in renderFrame: create new Texture.from(videoFrame), assign to sprite, then destroy oldTexture(true). Also ensure VideoFrame.close() calls are preserved by exporter loops.

pitfalls.mistake: Change layout math without verifying preview parity
pitfalls.consequence: Export visuals (crop, mask radius, webcam placement) will diverge from the editor preview leading to WYSIWYG mismatch.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep computeCompositeLayout and previewWidth/previewHeight usage consistent; changes must respect preview->export scaling and borderRadius scaling logic from commit history.

key_sections: initialize: sets up Pixi, filters, composite and raster canvases
setupBackground: understand how background rendering and cross-origin handling work
renderFrame: core per-frame flow (texture update, animation update, render, composite)
updateLayout: layout math used to position/crop video and mask
skip_unless_needed: internal helper routines not referenced by exporter (small utilities inside file)
detailed gradient parsing calls (unless debugging gradient output)

related_files.relationship: consumer - VideoExporter uses FrameRenderer to render each export frame (renderFrame) and then reads back pixels for encoding
related_files.reason_to_check: Any change to FrameRenderer's output canvas shape, pixel format, or method to acquire final canvas must be reflected in VideoExporter where ImageData is read and VideoFrame constructed.

related_files.relationship: spec reference - playback uses the same zoom/transform and smoothing utilities; FrameRenderer duplicates algorithmic behavior to ensure exported frames match preview
related_files.reason_to_check: Behavioral parity (auto-follow smoothing, motion blur, mask radius scaling) must be consistent between playback and export; changes to playback layout utilities or constants affect FrameRenderer logic.

related_files.relationship: shared layout utility - FrameRenderer calls computeCompositeLayout to compute webcam & screen rects
related_files.reason_to_check: Modifications to computeCompositeLayout or its presets impact maskRect/webcamRect used by FrameRenderer.

related_files.relationship: annotation render target - FrameRenderer invokes renderAnnotations to draw annotationRegions on the final composite
related_files.reason_to_check: If annotation API or coordinate space changes, FrameRenderer must provide appropriate previewWidth/previewHeight and scaleFactor.

data_constants_to_check: previewWidth/previewHeight usage where borderRadius scaling derives

insights.title: Pass webcamSizePreset through FrameRenderer config
insights.problem: Frame rendering previously didn't accept the new webcamSizePreset param.
insights.root_cause: Composite layout changes required exporter frame renderer to include new parameter to keep previews and export consistent.
insights.solution: Extended FrameRenderConfig to include webcamSizePreset and pass it through when computing layout in frame rendering.
insights.Lesson Learned: Ensure exporter/rendering pipeline receives the same layout configuration as the editor UI to produce WYSIWYG results.

insights.title: Workaround GPU→2D texture sharing failures on Linux/Wayland by explicit readback
insights.problem: On some Linux/Wayland setups (EGL/Ozone), drawImage(webglCanvas) fails silently, producing green/empty frames in exports.
insights.root_cause: The implicit GPU-to-2D shared-image path relied upon by drawing a WebGL canvas into a 2D canvas can be unsupported or buggy on certain drivers/OS combos; this produces invalid pixel data.
insights.solution: Add an explicit readbackVideoCanvas() that uses WebGL's gl.readPixels to copy the framebuffer into a CPU-side Uint8Array, flip rows (since readPixels is bottom-to-top), create ImageData and putImageData into a raster 2D canvas, and use that canvas for subsequent drawImage calls. Maintain a rasterCanvas & rasterCtx, and fall back to the original canvas when WebGL/gl isn't available.
insights.lesson_learned: When relying on cross-API canvas operations (WebGL→2D), provide an explicit GPU readback fallback for platforms where implicit sharing breaks. Prefer deterministic readPixels/getImageData paths for export-critical frames.

insights.title: Maintain a separate raster canvas for CPU-side image data
insights.problem: Previously the code assumed drawImage(webglCanvas) would always work; adding raster canvas centralizes CPU-side pixel operations and avoids reusing the GL canvas for 2D draws.
insights.root_cause: Mixing WebGL and 2D drawing on the same canvas leads to platform-specific implicit sharing assumptions.
insights.solution: Create a separate rasterCanvas with 2D context to receive readPixels output; use rasterCanvas as the source for composite operations.
insights.lesson_learned: Isolate GPU-backed canvases from CPU-backed canvases when you need to guarantee pixel contents across platforms; add checks and clearups to avoid leaking contexts.

insights.title: Integrate smoothing & cursor-auto-follow logic into FrameRenderer
insights.problem: Automatic zoom-follow behavior required consistent smoothing across playback and export pipelines.
insights.root_cause: Cursor telemetry and auto-follow behavior previously implemented only in playback; export pipeline needed parity to avoid visual mismatch.
insights.solution: Add smoothedAutoFocus, prevAnimationTimeMs and prevTargetProgress state to FrameRenderer and apply deadzone + time-based smoothing for auto-follow focus in the same way as playback. Accept cursorTelemetry in FrameRenderConfig.
insights.lesson_learned: When a visual feature (e.g., auto-follow) must appear the same in both UI playback and exported output, thread telemetry data through renderer/exporter modules and keep smoothing algorithms consistent.

insights.title: Render webcam overlay into final composite during export
insights.problem: Exported frames didn't composite the webcam overlay into the final render, making exported files lacking webcam overlays.
insights.root_cause: FrameRenderer composite step only drew the main video canvas; no webcamFrame handling existed.
insights.solution: Add optional webcamWidth/webcamHeight config fields, accept optional webcamFrame parameter on renderFrame, compute overlay layout via computeWebcamOverlayLayout and draw webcamFrame into composite canvas inside compositeWithShadows().
insights.lesson_learned: Export stage must mirror preview compositing logic (layout, rounded corners, shadows). Keep layout computation shared between playback and renderer utilities.

insights.title: Export clampFocusToStage uses stageSize instead of layoutCache
insights.problem: clampFocusToStage previously passed entire layoutCache to util expecting stageSize.
insights.root_cause: Mismatch between what clamp util expects and what was passed.
insights.solution: Pass this.layoutCache.stageSize to clampFocusToStageUtil.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep util function contracts clear; prefer minimal shape (stageSize) rather than full layoutCache when only a subtree is needed.

insights.title: FrameRenderer accepts speedRegions and enables antialiasing change
insights.problem: FrameRenderer didn't receive speedRegions that may be needed to render overlays tied to playback speed; antialiasing was previously disabled.
insights.root_cause: New editor concept (speed regions) wasn't passed into renderer; rendering quality settings were conservative.
insights.solution: Added speedRegions to FrameRenderConfig and enabled antialias:true and increased blur filter quality.
insights.lesson_learned: When upstream editor features affect visual output, update renderer API. Be aware that antialiasing and higher filter quality improve visuals but increase GPU/CPU cost.

insights.title: FrameRenderer motionBlur fallback default to false
insights.problem: FrameRenderer used this.config.motionBlurEnabled ?? true fallback which enabled motion blur unless explicitly set to false, causing exported frames to be blurred unexpectedly.
insights.root_cause: The exporter-level fallback default was true, opposite to the new UI default.
insights.solution: Change fallback to this.config.motionBlurEnabled ?? false so exporter respects the disabled-by-default setting.
insights.lesson_learned: Exporter modules should follow the same default configuration semantics as UI; prefer explicit false fallback if feature is opt-in.

insights.title: Border radius mismatch between preview and export
insights.problem: Exported video rendered rounded-corner masks with border radius appearing smaller than in the preview UI.
insights.root_cause: Mask corner radius was applied in export using the raw logical radius value, but export canvas size could be scaled relative to preview dimensions causing visual mismatch.
insights.solution: Scale the borderRadius by the canvas scale factor derived from export / preview dimensions and use scaledBorderRadius for the mask drawing (commit b748586).
insights.lesson_learned: Whenever rendering UI-derived pixel properties on a canvas that can be scaled for export, convert logical CSS-like values to the canvas coordinate space by applying consistent scale factors. Keep previewWidth/previewHeight available in exporter config to compute scale factors.

insights.title: Add annotation rendering hook and preview/export padding
insights.problem: Annotations were part of DOM overlay only and not rendered into export frames, causing exported videos to miss annotations.
insights.root_cause: Annotation visuals lived only in the HTML overlay / React layer; export used PixiJS canvas but didn't composite annotation artwork.
insights.solution: Added support to FrameRenderer config for annotationRegions/previewWidth/previewHeight and invoke renderAnnotations to draw them onto the export composite context after rendering the video frame.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep renderer and UI representations in sync — if UI can show a visual (annotations), the export renderer must reproduce it pixel-perfect. Add explicit data (preview dimensions, annotations) into the renderer config.

insights.title: Introduce padding export parameter and reuse in layout scaling
insights.problem: Previously export used a fixed VIEWPORT_SCALE which made preview/export sizing inconsistent with UI padding setting.
insights.root_cause: Padding was only a UI control; export used hardcoded viewport scale assumptions.
insights.solution: Added padding to renderer config, translated padding (percentage) into a paddingScale used when computing viewportWidth/height.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep UI controls (padding) reflected in export calculations; expose them in the renderer config so export visuals match preview.

insights.title: Removed stale updateConfig dead code
insights.problem: An updateConfig method existed but was removed in a later commit; keeping it may cause confusion.
insights.root_cause: Dead/unused API in the FrameRenderer class.
insights.solution: Deleted updateConfig (cleanup).
insights.lesson_learned: Remove dead public API to prevent accidental usage and reduce maintenance burden.

insights.title: Export layout alignment refactor and later manual replacement
insights.problem: Exported frames were not matching preview layout (crop/centering/scale mismatch).
insights.root_cause: Preview used layoutVideoContent utility; early refactor replaced it with a manual layout implementation. One manual change later introduced incorrect geometry/scale and removed reuse of shared layout logic.
insights.solution: Multiple iterations: first switched to using layoutVideoContent util (to keep preview and export consistent), then attempted a manual calculation to fix a regression. The final edits compute cropped video pixel extents, scale to fit a viewport, position sprite and container, update mask and cache layout info.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep layout logic for preview and export DRY — prefer reusing the same layout utility. If manual computation is necessary, validate against preview with visual tests. Ensure cameraContainer/required PIXI objects are checked consistently before layout.

insights.title: Guard against missing PIXI containers and cache consistent layout
insights.problem: updateLayout could run with missing PIXI objects and then produce no layoutCache or invalid values.
insights.root_cause: Different commits had inconsistent null checks (cameraContainer present in some checks and not others).
insights.solution: Standardized presence checks for essential objects (app, videoSprite, maskGraphics, videoContainer, and in some variants cameraContainer). Ensured layoutCache is consistently populated with stageSize, videoSize, baseScale, baseOffset, maskRect.
insights.lesson_learned: Rendering code must defensively check all runtime graphical objects before performing layout. Maintain a single source of truth for layout data and cache it for later transforms.

insights.title: Mask and scaled sprite geometry set for export
insights.problem: Export required correct mask and scaled display region; failing to set mask caused visual artifacts.
insights.root_cause: Export code didn't compute display mask based on cropped dimensions.
insights.solution: Compute croppedDisplayWidth/Height, set maskGraphics.roundRect with radius, fill mask, and set videoSprite dimensions/position to render the cropped area centered in export canvas.
insights.lesson_learned: Export pipeline needs explicit pixel math for cropping/centering; approximations produce subtle visual differences.

src/lib/exporter/videoExporter.ts.short_description: Export orchestrator: decodes source video(s), renders frames via FrameRenderer, encodes video with WebCodecs VideoEncoder, and muxes audio/video into final blob
src/lib/exporter/videoExporter.ts.description:
VideoExporter is the high-level export pipeline that orchestrates streaming decode, frame rendering, video encoding, optional audio processing and muxing into a final output blob. It was designed for long-running deterministic exports: it uses a StreamingVideoDecoder (demuxer + VideoDecoder) to decode frames in a forward pass, passes frames through a FrameRenderer instance to produce composited canvases, and uses WebCodecs VideoEncoder to encode frames while streaming encoded chunks to a VideoMuxer for final containerization.

This file implements retry logic across encoder preferences (hardware vs software), explicit backpressure based on encoder queue size, encoder stall detection and timeouts, careful resource management (closing/destroying decoders and frames), webcam decoding as a parallel stream with an AsyncVideoFrameQueue for synchronization, and audio post-processing via AudioProcessor when the source contains an audio track. The exporter is intentionally defensive against platform-specific failures observed historically (e.g., GPU shared-image failures, flawed hardware encoders on Windows) and therefore probes isConfigSupported, switches encoder modes, reads pixel buffers from canvases, and enforces timeouts when flushing encoders.

key_constructs.name: VideoExporter
key_constructs.purpose: Top-level export class that accepts export parameters and runs export() to produce a blob result.
key_constructs.reasoning: VideoExporter encapsulates lifecycle management of decoder(s), renderer, encoder and muxer. It provides cancellation, progress reporting, retry/fallback across encoder preferences and robust cleanup of resources after completion or failure.

key_constructs.name: export
key_constructs.purpose: Public method that tries encoder preferences in order and returns an ExportResult (success + blob or error).
key_constructs.reasoning: export wraps repeated export attempts with different hardwareAcceleration choices. It manages lastError and ensures cleanup between attempts. Callers (UI) rely on this method to surface failures and to receive progress callbacks.

key_constructs.name: exportWithEncoderPreference
key_constructs.purpose: Per-attempt exporter logic: initializes streaming decoders, renderer, encoder and muxer; decodes frames, renders them, encodes VideoFrames and streams encoded chunks to muxer; processes audio and finalizes output.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function contains the streaming loop and must be correct and robust: it handles webcam decoding in parallel, enforces encoder backpressure, uses ImageData buffer to construct VideoFrames (readback), ensures per-frame VideoFrame.close(), and waits on encoder.flush() and muxing promises before finalizing.

key_constructs.name: initializeEncoder
key_constructs.purpose: Configures and initializes the WebCodecs VideoEncoder with requested codec/bitrate/framerate and chosen hardwareAcceleration; sets up the output and error callbacks used to feed VideoMuxer and detect fatal errors.
key_constructs.reasoning: initializeEncoder probes VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported and configures the encoder accordingly. It captures decoderConfig.description and colorSpace on the first chunk to initialize muxer metadata. Error handling here sets fatalEncoderError and cancels decoders; changing this routine impacts encoder behavior and muxer metadata handling.

key_constructs.name: cleanup
key_constructs.purpose: Releases encoder, decoders, audio processor and muxer resources if present; used between attempts and on cancel/failure.
key_constructs.reasoning: Robust cleanup prevents resource leaks during repeated attempts or on abort. Many prior bugs in this area motivated extensive try/catch and guards in cleanup to avoid crashes while freeing platform resources.

key_behaviors: decodes source video(s) using a streaming demuxer + VideoDecoder pipeline
renders frames through FrameRenderer and creates VideoFrame from raw ImageData buffer
encodes frames with WebCodecs VideoEncoder and streams encoded chunks to VideoMuxer
processes audio track after video is encoded and adds audio into the muxer
supports cancellation and encoder preference retries (hardware/software) with timeouts

pitfalls.mistake: Assume VideoEncoder.encode() will always accept frames (no backpressure)
pitfalls.consequence: Encoder queues can grow and cause memory blowup or stalls; exporter will hang or fail.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect encodeQueueSize, use small MAX_ENCODE_QUEUE, and wait (with stall timeout) when the queue is full. Do not remove or alter the encoder stall timeout logic (ENCODER_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS).

pitfalls.mistake: Construct VideoFrame directly from an HTMLCanvasElement on all platforms
pitfalls.consequence: Implicit GPU->CPU canvas sharing can fail on some Linux drivers, producing empty or corrupted frames.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the explicit path that reads pixel data via getImageData (or readbackVideoCanvas/gl.readPixels) and creates VideoFrame from ImageData.data.buffer as used in export loop.

pitfalls.mistake: Neglect to close VideoFrame objects or fail to destroy queues on error
pitfalls.consequence: Memory leaks and hung decode/encode loops.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep per-frame try/finally that always calls videoFrame.close(), webcamFrame?.close(), and use queue.fail/close/destroy in finally blocks.

pitfalls.mistake: Remove or shorten encoder flush timeout or not await muxingPromises
pitfalls.consequence: Finalization can hang or produce incomplete files if muxing hasn't finished.
pitfalls.prevention: Ensure encoder.flush() is awaited with withTimeout and all muxingPromises are awaited before calling muxer.finalize().

pitfalls.mistake: Change mapping between effective timeline and source timeline without updating mapEffectiveToSourceTime logic
pitfalls.consequence: Trimmed or speed-changed exports will sample incorrect source frames resulting in misaligned output.
pitfalls.prevention: Any modifications to trimming/speed mapping must maintain mapEffectiveToSourceTime and getEffectiveDuration semantics used to compute totalFrames and source timestamps.

key_sections: export: high-level retry loop across encoder preferences
exportWithEncoderPreference: the decode->render->encode pipeline and webcam queue handling
initializeEncoder: how encoder output metadata is captured and how muxer first-chunk metadata is prepared
cleanup & cancel: resource teardown behavior to follow on failure
skip_unless_needed: minor logging statements and console.debug lines
detailed inner workings of StreamingVideoDecoder (inspect the decoder file if debugging decoding issues)

related_files.relationship: consumer/provider - VideoExporter creates and calls FrameRenderer.initialize/renderFrame/getCanvas to obtain the final composited canvas/image buffer for encoding
related_files.reason_to_check: If FrameRenderer changes the getCanvas API, color format, or timing semantics, VideoExporter must adjust how it reads ImageData and constructs VideoFrame objects.

related_files.relationship: collaborator - VideoExporter pushes encoded chunks to VideoMuxer; muxer.finalize() is used to produce final blob
related_files.reason_to_check: Changes in encoded chunk metadata handling (decoderConfig.description/colorSpace) require coordinating changes in how VideoExporter provides the metadata to the muxer.

related_files.relationship: collaborator - streaming decode and demux are provided by StreamingVideoDecoder; exporter relies on its decodeAll API and demuxer for audio
related_files.reason_to_check: Any changes to decodeAll semantics, timestamps reporting, or resource lifecycle will need updates in the export loop and error handling.

related_files.relationship: upstream caller - UI constructs VideoExporter and forwards configuration (zoomRegions, trimRegions, speedRegions, cursorTelemetry, etc.)
related_files.reason_to_check: Modifying exporter config parameters or the public API requires updating UI call sites and types in VideoEditor.

data_constants_to_check: ENCODER_STALL_TIMEOUT_MS and ENCODER_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS defined at top of file
this.MAX_ENCODE_QUEUE and logic that switches it based on encoder preference

insights.title: VideoExporter accepts webcamSizePreset and forwards to FrameRenderer
insights.problem: VideoExporter needed the new webcam sizing parameter to produce matching exported video.
insights.root_cause: Change in webcam sizing model requires exporters to accept and use new parameter.
insights.solution: Added webcamSizePreset to VideoExporterConfig and forwarded into frame rendering pipeline.
insights.Lesson Learned: When adding a global layout parameter, update all exporter entry points to accept and forward it.

insights.title: Avoid silent empty frames by reading raw pixels from canvas before VideoFrame creation
insights.problem: Passing an HTMLCanvasElement directly to new VideoFrame(canvas, ...) could result in empty/green frames on some Linux systems due to a failing GPU shared-image path.
insights.root_cause: The same implicit GPU→2D sharing problem: some platforms silently fail when VideoFrame is constructed from a GPU-backed canvas or when canvas-to-VideoFrame path relies on platform image sharing.
insights.solution: Read ImageData via canvas.getContext('2d').getImageData(...) and create the VideoFrame from the raw pixel buffer (imageData.data.buffer) with appropriate format, codedWidth, codedHeight. This ensures the VideoFrame is constructed from CPU-side pixel data.
insights.lesson_learned: For deterministic exports across platforms, use CPU-backed pixel buffers (getImageData or gl.readPixels) instead of relying on implicit GPU image sharing when constructing VideoFrames.

insights.title: Thread cursor telemetry through exporter to match playback behavior
insights.problem: Auto-follow zoom behavior in exported videos could differ from playback if cursor telemetry isn't passed through exporter and frame renderer.
insights.root_cause: Export pipeline didn't accept cursorTelemetry, so frame rendering lacked the runtime cursor data used by playback.
insights.solution: Extend VideoExporter config to include cursorTelemetry and pass it down to FrameRenderer so exported frames use identical focus logic.
insights.lesson_learned: Visual features dependent on runtime telemetry must be explicitly passed into export code paths; this often requires coordinated changes across exporter, renderer, and types.

insights.title: Prevent export deadlocks and handle encoder stalls/fatal errors
insights.problem: Video exports could hang indefinitely (encoder stall) or deadlock on Windows/hardware encoders; webcam decode could race and cause blocking; encoder errors were not surfaced properly leading to silent failures.
insights.root_cause: No stall detection for encoder output, no robust fallback ordering (hardware vs software) for problematic Windows encoders, and insufficient cleanup of decoding/mux tasks caused deadlocks. Encoder errors only set cancelled flag instead of failing fast and cancelling streaming loops.
insights.solution: Introduced encoder stall timeout (lastEncoderOutputAt tracking), fatalEncoderError to surface encoder errors, ENCODER_FLUSH_TIMEOUT_MS for flush timeout, explicit encoder hardware/software preference ordering (prefer-software first on Windows), getEncoderPreferences helper, withTimeout for encoder flush, reportProgress wrapper, adjust MAX_ENCODE_QUEUE behavior depending on encoder preference, and improved cleanup paths. Export retries different encoder preferences and returns meaningful errors.

insights.title: Split export flow to try encoder preferences and improve resource cleanup
insights.problem: Single export flow attempted one encoder config only and mixed setup/cleanup logic making retries hard.
insights.root_cause: All encoder initialization, decoding, rendering, and muxing lived in one large export() block without a notion of retry attempt isolation.
insights.solution: Refactored export into an outer loop selecting encoder preferences and an exportWithEncoderPreference which composes initialization, decode, and finalization, and ensures cleanup in finally blocks.

insights.title: Always release VideoFrame resources and handle webcam decode flags
insights.problem: VideoFrame objects could leak if an exception occurred mid-frame processing leading to exhausted memory or WebCodecs issues.
insights.root_cause: Frames were sometimes closed early or not in a finally block. Webcam decode produced queues that could block finally logic.
insights.solution: Wrap per-frame processing in try/finally and ensure videoFrame.close() and webcamFrame?.close() are always called. Add stopWebcamDecode flag and ensure webcam decoder is cancelled and its promise awaited in finally.

insights.title: Tear down webcam export queues and surface decode errors
insights.problem: Analogous to GIF exporter, VIDEO exporter used webcam frame queues that could remain open or not be failed correctly on errors, causing hangs or corruption during export.
insights.root_cause: webcam frame queue lifecycle was managed locally and wasn't destroyed in all error/finalization cases.
insights.solution: Introduce outer-scoped webcamFrameQueue and webcamDecodeError, finalize queue with fail/close in finally handlers and call destroy() at outer finally.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep queue lifecycle explicit, fail-then-close semantics are useful to propagate error to consumers; always destroy to free frame resources.

insights.title: Provide readEndSec to audio processing to avoid finalization stalls on Windows
insights.problem: Export finalization could stall on some platforms because audio demuxing read stream wasn't bounded to the true end, causing the underlying reader to wait or stall.
insights.root_cause: Audio pipeline read of demuxer didn't pass a safe end bound when muxing completed frames, letting reader attempt to read beyond actual data.
insights.solution: Calculate readEndSec from videoInfo and pass it to audioProcessor.process; update audio processor to accept readEndSec and read bounded streams.
insights.lesson_learned: Long-running streaming reads should be bounded by known durations to avoid platform-specific finalization stalls; pass explicit end markers where possible.

insights.title: Integrate audio processing and muxer audio flag
insights.problem: Video export pipeline needed to mux audio tracks (and optionally process audio) and coordinate with streaming decoder demuxer.
insights.root_cause: Previously muxer always initialized without audio and no audio processing step existed.
insights.solution: Initialize VideoMuxer with hasAudio flag based on streaming decoder metadata; after video muxing, invoke AudioProcessor.process(demuxer, muxer, trimRegions) to add audio chunks; cancel audioProcessor on exporter.cancel.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep audio/video muxing coordinated: check decoded metadata for hasAudio, expose demuxer to reuse streams, and cancel audio processing during abort. Update exporter callers to pass new config (speedRegions).

insights.title: Use actual encoder queue size and reduce busy-wait sleep
insights.problem: Exporter previously used an internal counter or a busy-wait loop that wasn't tied to the encoder's real queue size, causing either spinning or incorrect backpressure behavior.
insights.root_cause: Code relied on this.encodeQueue (custom counter) instead of the VideoEncoder's encodeQueueSize, and used Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 0)) which aggressively yielded CPU.
insights.solution: Check this.encoder.encodeQueueSize directly and await a short sleep (5ms) instead of a zero-delay spin; also changed VideoEncoder latencyMode to 'quality' for better throughput.
insights.lesson_learned: Prefer the encoder's own queue/metrics over custom counters. Avoid tight spin loops; use small sleeps for backpressure. Adjust latencyMode based on tradeoff of realtime vs throughput.

insights.title: Add speedRegions to export pipeline types
insights.problem: New editor feature (playback speed regions) needed to be represented during export but exporter types and frame renderer did not accept them.
insights.root_cause: Types and FrameRenderer config previously only carried zoom/trim/annotation; speedRegions were missing.
insights.solution: Added SpeedRegion type imports and threaded speedRegions through FrameRenderer, GifExporter and VideoExporter configs.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding editor state that affects export, ensure that exporter type signatures and all downstream modules accept and propagate the new data.

insights.title: Switch to streaming decode pipeline (web-demuxer + VideoDecoder)
insights.problem: Previous exporters relied on seeking an HTMLVideoElement for each frame which is extremely slow and unstable for large exports.
insights.root_cause: Per-frame seeks on an HTMLVideoElement force rebuffering and are not suitable for high frame-rate batch export.
insights.solution: Adopt StreamingVideoDecoder (web-demuxer + VideoDecoder) which demuxes in a forward pass and resamples frames to CFR. Refactored exporter to use streaming decoder APIs and removed per-frame seeking logic.
insights.lesson_learned: For exporting large numbers of frames, prefer a forward-decoding pipeline (demuxer + VideoDecoder) to avoid seeking overhead. Manage backpressure, close VideoFrames, and implement cancellation and cleanup.

insights.title: Refactor exporter to stream/parallelize encoding and muxing with encoder backpressure
insights.problem: Original exporter likely decoded/encoded frames sequentially and had visual and performance issues during export; metadata (decoderConfig description and colorSpace) handling and encoder backpressure were weak.
insights.root_cause: Tight coupling between decode/render/encode phases, no robust backpressure handling, missing immediate mux streaming and insufficient handling of decoder/encoder metadata.
insights.solution: Rewrote main loop to process frames continuously; introduced encode queue (MAX_ENCODE_QUEUE) and waiting when queue is full; capture decoderConfig.description and colorSpace from encoder output; stream encoded chunks to muxer as they arrive and collect muxing promises; ensure encoder.flush and await muxingPromises before finalizing muxer. Also added hardware-acceleration detection and fallback to software if unsupported (commit 7a7db0b).
insights.lesson_learned: Video export pipelines must treat decode, render and encode as pipelined stages with explicit backpressure. Use encoder output metadata to configure muxer. Always ensure encoder.flush() completes and wait for any async muxing operations before finalizing output. Log both hardware/software selection for debugging. Be careful when changing the pipeline — test on low-memory and variable hardware to avoid stalls.

insights.title: Avoid seek race conditions and ensure first-frame readiness
insights.problem: Seeking and reading frames from a video element can race with setting currentTime; first frames may not be ready.
insights.root_cause: Code previously set videoElement.currentTime then awaited 'seeked' listener added after setting currentTime or didn't correctly wait for the first frame to be painted.
insights.solution: Attach 'seeked' listener (seekedPromise) before setting currentTime to avoid missing the event; for the first frame use requestVideoFrameCallback to ensure frame readiness (commit 7a7db0b).
insights.lesson_learned: When programmatically seeking an HTMLVideoElement, attach event handlers before changing currentTime; consider requestVideoFrameCallback for frame-accurate readiness. Not doing so can cause missed events and corrupted frames.

insights.title: Ensure encoder state checked and warn if not ready
insights.problem: Encoder might not be configured at encode time, potentially causing dropped frames or exceptions.
insights.root_cause: Encoder state transitions can be async and the code assumed encoder would be configured always when encoding.
insights.solution: Add checks for encoder && encoder.state === 'configured' before calling encode and log a warning when encoder not ready (commit 7a7db0b).
insights.lesson_learned: Validate API object readiness before calling methods that assume configured state and surface clear logs to help debug encoding stalls.

insights.title: Capture and use encoder decoderConfig metadata in muxer
insights.problem: Muxer didn't receive codec description/colorSpace until too late.
insights.root_cause: Encoder output chunks contain decoderConfig metadata; code needs to extract and pass it to muxer as soon as available.
insights.solution: On first chunk, capture description and colorSpace and pass them to muxer before streaming frames (commit 7a7db0b).
insights.lesson_learned: When working with low-level media APIs, encoder outputs often carry essential metadata for muxers. Capture this metadata early and use it to initialize muxer state.

insights.title: Set cancel flag on encoder error
insights.problem: Encoder errors previously may not have been propagated correctly to stop the export pipeline.
insights.root_cause: No consistent canceled state was set when encoder errored.
insights.solution: In encoder.error handler set this.cancelled = true and log error (commit 7a7db0b).
insights.lesson_learned: When async worker components fail (encoder, muxer), set an explicit cancellation flag and ensure other pipeline loops check it to exit gracefully.

insights.title: Reduce seek bottleneck and pipeline decode/render/encode
insights.problem: Export loop previously performed synchronous seeks and waited per-frame (requestVideoFrameCallback / seek races), causing a CPU/GPU bottleneck and poor throughput.
insights.root_cause: Per-frame sequential seeking + waiting serialized the decode/render/encode pipeline. Relying on requestVideoFrameCallback and not decoding ahead caused stalls and underutilized hardware encoders.
insights.solution: Introduced a decode-ahead pipeline (DECODE_AHEAD), a frameQueue to overlap decode/render/encode, attach 'seeked' listeners before changing currentTime to avoid race conditions, cap encoder queue with MAX_ENCODE_QUEUE, and parallelize muxing writes.
insights.lesson_learned: When extracting frames from a media element for bulk export, avoid synchronous per-frame seeks. Pre-decode ahead and overlap pipeline stages. Always attach event listeners before changing currentTime to avoid missed events/races.

insights.title: Fix seek race and first-frame readiness
insights.problem: Export could miss 'seeked' or render wrong frames due to attaching seek listeners AFTER setting currentTime or relying on requestVideoFrameCallback for the first frame.
insights.root_cause: Race between setting video.currentTime and listening for the 'seeked' event; first-frame readiness also relied on requestVideoFrameCallback which is not sufficient in all environments.
insights.solution: Attach 'seeked' listener before setting currentTime; for first frame, explicitly wait for loadeddata if needed and use seeked event. Use a decode queue to ensure frames are available before rendering.
insights.lesson_learned: Event listener ordering matters for media seeking. Always set up listeners before triggering the state change that emits those events.

insights.title: Improve logging and encoder metadata capture
insights.problem: Hard-to-read logs and inconsistent handling of encoder chunk metadata (decoderConfig.description/colorSpace).
insights.root_cause: Encoder output handling was capturing metadata into local variables and had inconsistent variable names; logs were terse/unnamespaced.
insights.solution: Unified metadata capture into class fields (this.videoDescription / this.videoColorSpace), added namespaced console messages, and ensured muxing uses captured metadata when sending first chunk.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep encoder/muxer metadata managed on the exporter instance so parallel tasks can reliably read them; consistent logs help debugging long-running exports.

insights.title: VideoEncoder config support check tightened
insights.problem: Fallback path for unsupported encoders previously logged ambiguous messages and could throw different error texts.
insights.root_cause: Previous code used hardwareSupport variable names and different error messages; behavior on unsupported encoders could be unclear.
insights.solution: Normalized support check using 'support', prefer-hardware path, fallback to 'prefer-software' and throw 'Video encoding not supported' if still unsupported.
insights.lesson_learned: When using platform capabilities (VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported) ensure clear fallback semantics — callers may need to handle the 'not supported' error consistently.

insights.title: Trim integration — map effective timeline to source time
insights.problem: When exporting with trim regions, frames were being sampled using the effective timeline (post-trim) as if source time matched effective time, producing misaligned frames.
insights.root_cause: Export loop iterated effective frames (excluding trimmed durations) but used naive frame index -> source time calculation.
insights.solution: Added getEffectiveDuration to compute duration excluding trims; computed totalFrames from effective duration; introduced mapEffectiveToSourceTime to translate an effective-time offset to the corresponding source-time (by adding back durations of trimmed segments before that point); used mapped sourceTime when seeking and rendering frames.
insights.lesson_learned: When supporting time-mapping features (trim, speed changes), separate effective timeline from source timeline and implement deterministic mapping functions. Tests should validate frame-level alignment across trims.

insights.title: Seek race fix: attach seeked listener before setting currentTime
insights.problem: Seeking during export could miss the 'seeked' / ready event leading to waiting forever or sampling an old frame.
insights.root_cause: The code set videoElement.currentTime before adding an awaited seeked listener, creating a race where the event could fire before the listener was registered.
insights.solution: Attach a once seeked listener promise before setting currentTime and await it after setting currentTime. Also handle first-frame readiness separately via requestVideoFrameCallback.
insights.lesson_learned: With asynchronous DOM media APIs, always attach event listeners before triggering the event-producing action to avoid race conditions.

insights.title: VideoEncoder support checking and hardware/software fallback
insights.problem: Initializing encoder could fail on systems without hardware support or with incompatible configs.
insights.root_cause: Previously code attempted to configure encoder and relied on try/catch fallback; didn't explicitly query support and could report poor errors.
insights.solution: Use VideoEncoder.isConfigSupported to detect hardware support and choose between hardware acceleration and software (prefer-software) explicitly, with clear logging and error throw if neither supported.
insights.lesson_learned: Probing platform support before configuring hardware-accelerated encoders provides clearer fallback paths and earlier, actionable errors. Log and set cancellation on encoder errors.

insights.title: Encoder error handling and cancellation
insights.problem: Encoder errors were logged but export continued or left internal state inconsistent.
insights.root_cause: Encoder's error callback didn't set state to cancel or stop export loop.
insights.solution: On encoder error, set this.cancelled = true and add clearer error logging; also warn when encoder not ready in encode queue path.
insights.lesson_learned: Long-running export pipelines must be defensive: abort on encoder failure and surface errors to UI; add logs to help debugging mid-export failures.

insights.title: Codec level change to avc1.640033 (level 5.1) and software fallback
insights.problem: Codec baseline changed to a higher profile; if system doesn't support it, exports could fail.
insights.root_cause: Commit switches default codec to a higher profile string (avc1.640033) and relies on isConfigSupported fallback behavior.
insights.solution: Default codec changed and code now probes support and falls back to software encoder; throw a clear error if encoding not supported.
insights.lesson_learned: Changing default codec/profile is potentially breaking for older machines; always probe support and expose fallback paths. Document changes in release notes.

electron/ipc/handlers.ts.short_description: Main-process IPC handlers for filesystem, recording session, project persistence, cursor telemetry and OS interactions
electron/ipc/handlers.ts.description:
This file centralizes registration of ipcMain handlers that implement the app's main-process responsibilities exposed to the renderer via the preload contextBridge. It exists to: (1) validate and gate all filesystem reads/writes that originate from renderer requests; (2) maintain ephemeral application state (selected source, current project path, current recording session, current video path); (3) sample and persist cursor telemetry during recordings; and (4) wrap OS-level interactions (dialogs, shell, systemPreferences) with structured results for the renderer.

Design decisions visible in the code: explicit approval model for user-selected filesystem paths (approvedPaths + approveFilePath) and tight normalization/validation of incoming path-like inputs to prevent traversal or arbitrary file access. Recording session concepts are first-class (RecordingSession model used across handlers) and sessions are persisted to a per-recording manifest next to video files. Cursor telemetry is sampled via a timed loop using screen.getCursorScreenPoint and normalized to display bounds; samples are rotated/limited to a maximum and moved to a pending buffer to be persisted when recordings are saved. The file implements many small, single-purpose helpers (normalizeVideoSourcePath, isPathAllowed, approveReadableVideoPath, resolveRecordingOutputPath, getApprovedProjectSession, loadRecordedSessionForVideoPath) to centralize security and path validation logic.

This file is tightly coupled to preload.ts (which exposes these handlers to the renderer) and to src/lib/recordingSession.ts (type normalization). Many UI flows in the editor and HUD depend on the structured return values and error/cancel semantics implemented here (e.g., saving/loading projects, exporting video/gif, selecting a current video). The registerIpcHandlers function is the registration entry point used by the main application bootstrap (electron/main.ts) and accepts callbacks and window factory functions to integrate with the rest of the main process (createEditorWindow, switchToHud, etc.).

key_constructs.name: PROJECT_FILE_EXTENSION
key_constructs.purpose: Default extension for saved project files (openscreen)
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to enforce consistent project file naming and to guide save/load dialogs and validation

insights.title: Prevent path traversal and unauthorized file reads via IPC
insights.problem: IPC handlers allowed arbitrary file paths (project/video imports and read-binary-file) which could be used to read or write files outside application data directories or accept dangerous file names.
insights.root_cause: Handlers accepted raw paths/filenames from the renderer without canonicalization, extension checks, or a whitelist of allowed directories. Recording output filenames were used directly with path.join, allowing traversal or nested paths.
insights.solution: Added approval flow and validation helpers: approvedPaths set, normalizeVideoSourcePath usage, isPathWithinDir/isPathAllowed, allowed video extension whitelist, approveReadableVideoPath, getApprovedProjectSession, and resolveRecordingOutputPath that rejects traversal/nested paths. All relevant handlers now check allowed status before reading/writing.
insights.Lesson Learned: Always canonicalize and validate filesystem paths crossing the renderer<->main IPC boundary. Maintain an explicit approval list for user-picked files and enforce extension/dir constraints for imports and output filenames.

insights.title: Normalize and reject unapproved current video path
insights.problem: set-current-video-path accepted arbitrary paths and created a current recording session with an unnormalized path.
insights.root_cause: Missing normalization and allowed-path check when setting current video path.
insights.solution: Normalize path with normalizeVideoSourcePath and require isPathAllowed before restoring/creating session; return failure if not approved.
insights.Lesson Learned: Normalize inputs and gate session state changes on prior approval/validation when bridging renderer-provided file paths.

insights.title: Project load now validates referenced media paths
insights.problem: Loading a project directly set the current recording session from project JSON without validating referenced media paths (screen/webcam).
insights.root_cause: Project files could reference arbitrary file paths; no validation before using them in session state.
insights.solution: Introduced getApprovedProjectSession(project) to validate and approve referenced screen/webcam paths before setting current session state.
insights.Lesson Learned: When importing structured data that references external files, validate and approve those file references before trusting them in app state.

insights.title: Register switch-to-hud IPC handler
insights.problem: Main process needed handler to accept renderer requests to switch to the HUD.
insights.root_cause: No IPC route existed for 'switch-to-hud'.
insights.solution: Add ipcMain.handle('switch-to-hud', ...) to call switchToHud wrapper if provided to registerIpcHandlers.
insights.lesson_learned: Adding renderer-to-main navigation actions requires plumbing through the ipc handlers registration and main initialization.

insights.title: Restore recorded session metadata when opening individual video file (webcam sessions)
insights.problem: When setting current video path (e.g., loading a webcam or screen video), the app lost associated recording session metadata (webcam pairing, timestamps), making it impossible to resume editing with webcam context.
insights.root_cause: set-current-video-path simply normalized the passed path and set partial session state, but did not attempt to load an associated session manifest (recording session JSON) that could live alongside video files. Webcams were saved as separate files with '-webcam' suffix, so matching logic and manifest lookup was missing.
insights.solution: Added helper getSessionManifestPathForVideo() and loadRecordedSessionForVideoPath() to try to find and restore the RecordingSession manifest based on the selected video. When a manifest is found, restore full session state (normalize paths); otherwise fall back to minimal session creation. This preserves webcam-screen link and metadata.

insights.title: Add camera permission request and recording session persistence APIs
insights.problem: Renderer needed to request platform camera permissions and persist an entire recording session (screen + optional webcam) instead of only single video files.
insights.root_cause: Previous main IPC surface only supported storing a single recorded video path and lacked explicit session management or camera permission handling.
insights.solution: Added 'request-camera-access' handler (macOS specific askForMediaAccess flow), introduced storeRecordedSession which writes screen + optional webcam binary files, writes cursor telemetry, creates a session manifest, and sets the current recording session. Added 'set-current-recording-session' and 'get-current-recording-session' handlers and updated get-recorded-video-path to prefer the current session.
insights.lesson_learned: IPC surfaces should model higher-level domain objects (recording session) when adding features that logically span multiple artifacts. Use explicit session manifests to keep editor state consistent. Handle platform-specific permission flows in main process.

insights.title: Read binary files through main process for local sources
insights.problem: Renderer's fetch-based reading couldn't access local file:// sources in packaged app; export pipeline needed raw bytes for local files.
insights.root_cause: Browser context cannot reliably read local files via fetch/file:// in all packaging modes; node fs can but renderer didn't expose handler.
insights.solution: Added IPC handler read-binary-file that normalizes path and returns ArrayBuffer for local files, used by streaming decoder to support local sources.
insights.lesson_learned: When code needs binary access to local files in an Electron app, prefer main-process read via fs and expose a safe IPC wrapper that normalizes/validates paths.

insights.title: Capture and persist cursor telemetry during recording
insights.problem: Need cursor telemetry for zoom suggestions; no mechanism existed to sample cursor during recording and persist it alongside recorded video.
insights.root_cause: Main process recorded videos but cursor sampling was not recorded or persisted.
insights.solution: Add sampling loop: on set-recording-state true start sampling screen.getCursorScreenPoint at fixed interval, normalize to selected display bounds, store activeCursorSamples and move them to pendingCursorSamples on stop; when saving video write pendingCursorSamples to videoPath.cursor.json; add ipc handler get-cursor-telemetry to read file and return sanitized sorted samples.
insights.lesson_learned: Sampling must be bounded (max samples), normalized to display coordinates, robust to selectedSource/display id differences, and persisted atomically; handle ENOENT gracefully when telemetry absent.

insights.title: Project file save/load IPC handlers
insights.problem: Editor needed ability to persist and restore project state to disk.
insights.root_cause: No IPC endpoints existed for saving/loading editor projects.
insights.solution: Added save-project-file and load-project-file handlers that implement safe naming, showSaveDialog/showOpenDialog flows, read/write JSON, and return structured success/error/cancelled payloads.
insights.lesson_learned: IPC handlers should return structured results and handle cancel flows explicitly. When writing files, sanitize suggested names and support overwriting existing project paths without prompting.

insights.title: Shortcuts persistence IPC handlers
insights.problem: Shortcuts config needed to be persisted between runs.
insights.root_cause: No read/write IPC endpoints for shortcuts configuration.
insights.solution: Added get-shortcuts and save-shortcuts handlers to read/write a JSON shortcuts file in userData.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep small config files near app.getPath('userData') and return clear error objects on failure.

insights.title: Reveal-in-folder IPC handler with fallback
insights.problem: Users wanted a quick way to show exported files in the OS file manager; shell.showItemInFolder can throw in some edge cases (file moved).
insights.root_cause: shell.showItemInFolder may throw or fail if file path is invalid or file moved; there was no fallback.
insights.solution: Added reveal-in-folder handler that calls shell.showItemInFolder and falls back to shell.openPath(dir) if revealing fails. Returns structured success and message/error information.
insights.lesson_learned: Wrap OS interactions in try/catch and provide graceful fallbacks; return useful messages for UI to display.

insights.title: save-exported-video dialog uses correct parent window and file filters for GIF
insights.problem: Save dialog for exported files didn't set file filters based on extension and in earlier versions didn't pass a parent window, which could cause focus issues or incorrect file type suggestion.
insights.root_cause: The save dialog call used a static MP4 filter and omitted passing mainWindow in some code paths.
insights.solution: Determine isGif from fileName extension, set filters accordingly, and pass mainWindow to dialog.showSaveDialog(mainWindow || undefined, ...).
insights.lesson_learned: Always set dialog filters to match file type being saved and pass the parent window where possible to ensure correct window modality/focus. When adding new export formats, update main-process handlers to support the new MIME/extension filters.

insights.title: Expose platform via IPC for renderer
insights.problem: Renderer code used navigator.platform for platform detection which fails in production Electron renderer and makes consistent shortcuts formatting hard.
insights.root_cause: Renderer cannot reliably detect host OS for formatting keyboard shortcuts when it runs in Electron context and navigator may be different.
insights.solution: Registered ipcMain.handle('get-platform', () => process.platform) so preload can expose getPlatform to renderer (commit f34bd19).
insights.lesson_learned: For platform-specific behavior in renderer, prefer a single source of truth from main process via IPC. Remember to cache results in renderer to avoid repeated IPC roundtrips.

insights.title: Open video picker and persist current video path in main process
insights.problem: Renderer needed to let user pick an arbitrary video from disk and then open it in editor.
insights.root_cause: No handler existed to showOpenDialog for video file selection nor to persist a current video path between windows.
insights.solution: Added open-video-file-picker handler that uses dialog.showOpenDialog with filters; added set/get/clear handlers for currentVideoPath stored in main process memory.
insights.lesson_learned: Main process is the right place to manage ephemeral app state that crosses windows. IPC handlers should validate results (cancellation) and return structured responses (success/cancelled/message).

insights.title: Save dialog integration for exports and cancelled flow handling
insights.problem: Export previously wrote directly to downloads without user choice; failures were not surfaced uniformly.
insights.root_cause: Exporter used app.getPath('downloads') implicitly; no save dialog to choose destination.
insights.solution: Use dialog.showSaveDialog to let user pick destination; return cancelled flag when user cancels and propagate it back to renderer; return errors with message and error string.
insights.lesson_learned: Long-running user actions like export should always involve explicit user confirmation for save path; propagate cancellation so UI can show appropriate notification.

electron/preload.ts.short_description: ContextBridge exposing typed electronAPI methods to renderer for IPC communication
electron/preload.ts.description:
This file defines the secure renderer-facing API surface by using contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('electronAPI', {...}). It exists to provide a minimal, typed wrapper around ipcRenderer.invoke/send/on calls so renderer code can perform operations that require main-process privileges (filesystem, dialogs, OS interactions, recording lifecycle) without access to Node APIs. The shape of the exposed API corresponds closely to ipcMain handlers registered in electron/ipc/handlers.ts.

Design choices: the API uses Promise-returning invoke calls for request/response flows and uses ipcRenderer.send for fire-and-forget events (e.g., HUD hide/close). Event listeners are exposed as functions that attach ipcRenderer.on and return a cleanup function which removes the listener to prevent leaks. Types for RecordingSession and StoreRecordedSessionInput are imported to provide TypeScript safety. The exposed method names and their signatures form a contract between renderer and main; they must remain synchronized with handlers.ts and electron-env.d.ts to avoid runtime type mismatches in production (context-isolated) builds.

src/components/video-editor/SettingsPane.short_description: React settings sidebar for the video editor exposing UI to control wallpaper, crop, webcam, export and visual settings
src/components/video-editor/SettingsPane.description:
SettingsPanel.tsx implements the right-hand settings sidebar used by the VideoEditor. It centralizes a large number of UI controls that map editor state to user interactions: wallpaper selection (bundled and user-uploaded), background color/gradient, crop controls and aspect presets, shadow/blur/motion-blur sliders and commits, border radius and padding sliders, webcam layout/size controls, export format/quality/GIF options, annotation controls, and playback speed controls. The component is a presentational/controller component that receives many props (handlers and values) from its parent (VideoEditor) and raises events such as on*Change and on*Commit so the parent can apply live preview and finalize state changes into the editor history.

The file exists because the editor's many knobs needed one cohesive UI with consistent commit semantics: some controls update preview continuously (onChange) while others expose on*Commit callbacks to avoid creating many history entries during a drag (commit pattern introduced in commit history). It uses helper modules like getAssetPath (to resolve packaged wallpaper assets), exporter constants (GIF presets/frame rates), and internal types (AnnotationRegion, CropRegion, PlaybackSpeed, ZoomDepth, ZoomFocusMode, etc.). The component also contains several important small helper components and constants used by the UI: CustomSpeedInput (text input that pairs with preset speed buttons), wallpaper asset lists, and GRADIENTS presets.

Design decisions visible in the code: (1) separation of continuous change handlers and commit handlers for sliders (shadow, padding, borderRadius, webcam size) so parent can implement live preview + a single commit to history; (2) fallback for asset resolution using getAssetPath with a try/catch that falls back to static relative paths; (3) only allows JPG/JPEG user-uploaded wallpaper images, converting them to a data URL and storing in local state for selection; (4) crop math uses normalized (0..1) crop region but exposes numeric pixel inputs to users and carefully clamps values with minimum percentages (min 0.05) and aspect-lock behavior. The component is deliberately defensive about video dimensions (defaulting to 1920x1080) and guards many handlers on presence of callbacks/props.

This file is tightly coupled to VideoEditor (provides/consumes many props) and VideoPlayback (many same props forwarded) — when editing SettingsPanel, ensure the prop contract matches the parent/consumer expectations (names, semantics, especially commit callbacks). Several behaviors are driven by UX decisions and earlier commits (unsaved export handling, motion blur default semantics, webcam size commit pattern) that must be respected when changing code.

key_constructs.name: CustomSpeedInput
key_constructs.purpose: A small controlled input allowing the user to type a custom playback speed; integrates with preset detection and validation.
key_constructs.reasoning: CustomSpeedInput implements local draft state and focus-aware syncing so typed values don't immediately overwrite preset-driven values; it also validates against MAX_PLAYBACK_SPEED and calls onError when exceeded. An agent modifying parent props or speed presets must keep this input's focus/draft logic and validation constraints in mind.

key_constructs.purpose: Number of bundled wallpaper images shipped with the app.
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to generate WALLPAPER_RELATIVE; changing it requires updating shipped assets and related indexing.

key_constructs.name: WALLPAPER_RELATIVE
key_constructs.purpose: Relative paths for bundled wallpaper assets used to resolve actual URLs via getAssetPath.
key_constructs.reasoning: The array is resolved with getAssetPath on mount. Any changes to asset paths or count must be synchronized with packaging and getAssetPath behavior.

key_constructs.name: GRADIENTS
key_constructs.purpose: List of CSS background gradient strings exposed as background choices in the UI.
key_constructs.reasoning: These strings are used directly in inline styles. Altering them changes background visuals and may affect tests or snapshot comparisons.

key_constructs.name: ZOOM_DEPTH_OPTIONS
key_constructs.purpose: Preset zoom depth options (depth numeric + display label) used in the Zoom controls portion of the settings panel.
key_constructs.reasoning: Controls what discrete zoom depths are available in the UI; other parts of the app (VideoPlayback, exporter) expect zoom depth semantics to match these values.

key_constructs.name: SettingsPanel
key_constructs.purpose: Main exported React component that renders the entire settings panel and calls back to parent handlers.
key_constructs.reasoning: SettingsPanel is the single UI surface for many editor features. It accepts a large props object — agents editing this file must preserve prop names and commit semantics so parent VideoEditor continues to work without breaking undo/redo, export, or playback preview.

key_constructs.name: handleCropNumericChange
key_constructs.purpose: Converts numeric pixel inputs into normalized cropRegion values, clamps minima/maxima, and respects crop aspect-lock behavior.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function contains the conversion and clamping logic that ensures crop values remain valid and consistent with VideoPlayback's crop expectations. Alterations must maintain rounding, min/ max and aspect-lock behavior.

key_constructs.name: applyCropAspectPreset
key_constructs.purpose: Applies an aspect ratio preset (e.g., '16:9') to the current crop region, computing which dimension to change and enabling locked-aspect mode.
key_constructs.reasoning: It uses video dimensions and existing crop region to compute a new width or height. Changes here will affect how cropping behaves when users pick a preset; keep the same calculation approach to avoid regressions.

key_constructs.name: getCropPixelValue
key_constructs.purpose: Reads a cropRegion field and converts it into rounded pixel units for display in numeric inputs.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function must be consistent with handleCropNumericChange's inverse math; rounding and video dimensions matter for exact numeric consistency visible to users.

key_constructs.name: handleImageUpload
key_constructs.purpose: Handles user-uploaded wallpaper images: validates file type (JPG/JPEG), reads file as DataURL, stores it in local state and triggers onWallpaperChange.
key_constructs.reasoning: This enforces JPG-only uploads, uses FileReader to create a data URL, and clears the input after handling so same file can be reselected. Changing validation or storage approach will affect the wallpaper selection UX and may need corresponding changes in VideoEditor/E2E tests.

key_constructs.name: handleRemoveCustomImage
key_constructs.purpose: Removes a user-uploaded custom wallpaper from local state and clears selection if it was selected.
key_constructs.reasoning: This handler also stops event propagation and ensures UI doesn't retain a deleted wallpaper as selected. Preserving event.stopPropagation semantics is important to avoid unintended parent click handlers running.

key_behaviors: renders wallpaper selection and resolves bundled asset paths
accepts and validates user-uploaded JPEG wallpapers and stores them as data URLs
converts between pixel inputs and normalized crop coordinates and applies aspect presets
applies live-change handlers and separate commit handlers for slider interactions
exposes export format and GIF-specific options and surfaces unsaved export re-save action

pitfalls.mistake: Change prop names or remove on*Commit handlers (e.g., onShadowCommit, onPaddingCommit) without updating parent
pitfalls.consequence: Editor history commit semantics will break; dragging sliders could produce many undo entries or fail to persist final value correctly.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the existing on*Change/on*Commit contract; if renaming, change callers in VideoEditor and related exports simultaneously.

pitfalls.mistake: Assume getAssetPath always resolves successfully and remove the fallback to relative paths
pitfalls.consequence: When packaged assets fail to resolve (development or unusual packaging), wallpaperPaths may become empty and UI will lack bundled wallpapers.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the try/catch fallback that maps WALLPAPER_RELATIVE to '/{p}' or ensure packaging guarantees asset resolution.

pitfalls.mistake: Allow image types other than JPG/JPEG in handleImageUpload or change validation silently
pitfalls.consequence: Uploaded images might be large, unsupported, or cause downstream code assumptions to fail (tests or UX expecting jpg-only).
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the existing validation for 'image/jpeg'/'image/jpg' and toast error messages when invalid.

pitfalls.mistake: Modify the crop normalization logic (min 0.05, clamping) without aligning VideoPlayback and exporter calculations
pitfalls.consequence: The editor preview (crop numeric inputs) and the actual exported/canvas rendering could diverge, producing unexpected crops.
pitfalls.prevention: If altering crop constraints, cross-check VideoPlayback crop usage and exporter rendering math to keep behavior consistent.

pitfalls.mistake: Change CustomSpeedInput draft/focus behavior or MAX_PLAYBACK_SPEED validation without updating callers/tests
pitfalls.consequence: Edge cases where the draft value does not reflect external preset changes or silent acceptance of invalid speeds can occur, confusing users.
pitfalls.prevention: Maintain focus-aware draft syncing and use SPEED_OPTIONS/MAX_PLAYBACK_SPEED constants consistently; if changing, update VideoEditor and tests.

key_sections: CustomSpeedInput: handles custom numeric speed input with focus/draft behaviour and validation
Wallpaper constants (WALLPAPER_RELATIVE & GRADIENTS): how bundled backgrounds are provided and resolved
Crop helpers (handleCropNumericChange, applyCropAspectPreset, getCropPixelValue): conversion and clamping logic between pixels and normalized crop values
Image upload/remove handlers (handleImageUpload, handleRemoveCustomImage): validation and storage approach for custom wallpapers
Slider commit wiring: look for on*Change vs on*Commit usage patterns (shadow, padding, border radius, webcam size)
skip_unless_needed: Large JSX markup of UI sections (scroll lists of palette/gradient wallpapers) if only behavior/handlers are being changed

related_files.reason_to_check: Ensure prop names, default values, and commit semantics remain compatible with VideoEditor’s useEditorHistory integration.

related_files.relationship: Consumer of many of the same visual props (cropRegion, shadowIntensity, showBlur, motionBlurAmount, borderRadius, padding, webcam settings). SettingsPanel changes to how these props are produced should be validated against VideoPlayback rendering.
related_files.reason_to_check: To verify preview matches UI changes and exported output, check VideoPlayback uses the same units/normalization.

related_files.relationship: Utility that resolves packaged asset paths used by SettingsPanel to load bundled wallpapers.
related_files.reason_to_check: If changing how assets are resolved or asset locations are modified, update getAssetPath usage and fallback behavior.

related_files.relationship: Export pipeline that consumes editor/export settings (motion blur, shadow intensity, padding, webcam sizing) when producing final output.
related_files.reason_to_check: If SettingsPanel changes default values or semantics of export-related props, ensure exporter interprets them the same way.
