insights.title: Add webcam size UI (slider) and propagate commit events
insights.problem: Users needed fine-grained control of webcam size in picture-in-picture layout.
insights.root_cause: Previous presets were coarse or missing; UI didn't expose percentage control.
insights.solution: Added a slider UI in SettingsPanel rendered when picture-in-picture layout is active; introduced onWebcamSizePresetChange and onWebcamSizePresetCommit props to support live-change and commit semantics.
insights.Lesson Learned: For UX sliders that control exportable layout, separate onValueChange (live preview) from onValueCommit (persist/serialize) so exporters/state commits occur only on user end-of-interaction.

insights.title: Expose unsaved export re-save button in settings
insights.problem: No UI to re-save previously generated export when user canceled the save dialog.
insights.root_cause: Export unsaved data was tracked in VideoEditor but not surfaced in SettingsPanel.
insights.solution: Added unsavedExport prop and onSaveUnsavedExport callback and rendered a prominent 'Choose Save Location' button when unsavedExport exists.

insights.title: Expose on*Commit callbacks for sliders to support history commit
insights.problem: Slider interactions created multiple undo entries while dragging.
insights.root_cause: Change handlers were called continuously without a commit hook to consolidate state into a single history entry.
insights.solution: Add onShadowCommit, onBorderRadiusCommit, onPaddingCommit and wire them to commitState in editor so updateState can be used for live changes and commitState called on commit.
insights.lesson_learned: When integrating a history system, UI controls should expose commit/finalize hooks so transient changes don't bloat history.

insights.title: Playback speed controls and project save/load buttons
insights.problem: Users need UI to configure speed regions and to trigger project save/load from the settings sidebar.
insights.root_cause: Settings panel lacked controls for new speed regions and in-editor quick project actions.
insights.solution: Added Playback Speed section with SPEED_OPTIONS buttons, added Load/Save Project buttons with callbacks.
insights.lesson_learned: New timeline region types should have clear UI affordances in settings; disable actions when nothing selected.

insights.title: Motion blur default changed to disabled
insights.problem: Motion blur was enabled by default across editor UI and export rendering which produced unexpected blur for users who didn't opt in.
insights.root_cause: Default props and state values for motion blur were true in multiple places (SettingsPanel prop default, VideoEditor state, playback transform signature), and FrameRenderer fallback also defaulted to true leading to mismatched behavior.
insights.solution: Change default motionBlurEnabled to false in SettingsPanel, VideoEditor, VideoPlayback/zoomTransform signatures, and use config.motionBlurEnabled ?? false in FrameRenderer so exporter honors false by default.
insights.lesson_learned: Default feature flags must be consistent across UI, playback, and exporter layers. Centralize and document defaults to prevent mismatches between editor preview and actual export.

insights.title: Settings panel layout and export format UI additions
insights.problem: Settings panel tabs and export UI cramped or lacked format controls for new GIF feature.
insights.root_cause: Earlier layouts used flexible zero heights that caused scroll/overflow issues for some content (image selection and settings tabs). GIF export feature required UI to select formats/options.
insights.solution: Adjust Tabs container min-height / scrollable region sizes (min-h and max-h adjustments), introduce Format selection UI and GIF option controls, and add small layout tweaks (grid column counts) where GIF options changed grid widths.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding a new feature that affects UI density (GIF options), review layout constraints and scrolling areas. Use explicit min/max heights for predictable cross-platform layout.

insights.title: Switch Export Quality select to segmented button group and spacing tweaks
insights.problem: Small UI inconsistencies in spacing, heights and the export quality select control.
insights.root_cause: UX iteration: designer prefer button group to select.
insights.solution: Replaced <select> with a 3-button segmented group bound to ExportQuality type, adjusted paddings and spacing, and propagated exportQuality prop into SettingsPanel.
insights.lesson_learned: When swapping form controls, ensure type bindings follow through into parent and export logic. Update className/cell spacing consistently.

insights.title: Settings layout / spacing cleanup and addition of aspect ratio/padding controls
insights.problem: Multiple small layout changes to match updated design (rounded paddings, smaller heights).
insights.root_cause: UX polish.
insights.solution: Adjusted classNames, reduced heights, added Aspect Ratio selector and Padding / Roundness sliders in different commits; added handlers for new props (onBorderRadiusChange, onPaddingChange).
insights.lesson_learned: UI changes often require matching prop plumbing in parent components. Keep SettingsPanel props typed and minimal for required features.

insights.title: Disable source selection when recording (LaunchWindow interaction)
insights.problem: Users could open source selector while recording which could interfere with capture.
insights.root_cause: LaunchWindow actions were not gated by recording state.
insights.solution: Disabled the source/project selection buttons while recording (propagate recording state to LaunchWindow).
insights.lesson_learned: Guard UI actions that affect ongoing system-level tasks (recording) to prevent user actions from interrupting background processes.

insights.title: Expose motionBlurEnabled and shadowIntensity controls
insights.problem: Users needed UI to control motion blur and adjust shadow intensity; these needed to be passed to playback and exporter.
insights.root_cause: Initial UI only exposed boolean drop-shadow toggle and blur; shadow strength and motion blur were not surfaced.
insights.solution: Added a motion blur Switch and slider-based shadowIntensity control; hooked them to parent VideoEditor via props (motionBlurEnabled, onMotionBlurChange, shadowIntensity, onShadowChange).
insights.lesson_learned: When adding renderer-facing visual toggles, ensure consistent naming and numeric range (0-1 for intensity) and flow through both preview and export code paths.

electron/main.ts.short_description: Electron main process: app lifecycle, window & tray management, IPC registration, permissions, and recordings dir bootstrapping
electron/main.ts.description:
This file is the Electron main process entry for the desktop app. It exists to initialize application-level resources (tray, menus, recordings directory), create and switch between different BrowserWindow types (HUD overlay vs editor vs source selector), register permission handlers, and wire up IPC by calling registerIpcHandlers. It centralizes platform-specific behavior (macOS audio permission workaround, microphone permission prompting on macOS) and manages the authoritative mainWindow/sourceSelectorWindow/tray references and related state such as selectedSourceName and editorHasUnsavedChanges.

Design decisions visible here: window lifecycle is centrally managed in main to avoid race conditions between multiple windows; menu actions are robust to missing editor windows by creating the editor window and waiting for did-finish-load before sending IPC; close flows use an isForceClosing guard and a captured-window forceCloseEditorWindow helper to avoid races with asynchronous renderer save flows. The file also exposes a constant RECORDINGS_DIR and computes key filesystem paths (MAIN_DIST, RENDERER_DIST, process.env.VITE_PUBLIC) used by other native code paths (tray icon loading, persistence operations). Localization is reflected into menu labels via mainT and setMainLocale, and set-locale is handled through an ipcMain.handle call.

key_constructs.name: RECORDINGS_DIR
key_constructs.purpose: Holds the path where recordings are persisted under the app's userData directory
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the authoritative path used by the main process for file persistence; other parts of the app expect recordings to be saved here, so edits must preserve its semantics and location.

key_constructs.name: ensureRecordingsDir
key_constructs.purpose: Creates the RECORDINGS_DIR (recursive) at startup and logs path/errors
key_constructs.reasoning: Called during app.whenReady to guarantee the recordings directory exists. An agent modifying startup flow should keep this call or provide an equivalent to avoid missing directories and runtime file write errors.

key_constructs.name: VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL
key_constructs.purpose: Reads process.env['VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL'] to detect dev server mode
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to determine where static assets are loaded from (public vs built dist). Changing surrounding logic affects asset resolution and the tray icon path resolution via process.env.VITE_PUBLIC.

key_constructs.name: MAIN_DIST
key_constructs.purpose: Path to the built electron distribution (dist-electron)
key_constructs.reasoning: Exposed for other build/runtime resolution logic; keep correct app root semantics when changing packaging or directory layout.

key_constructs.name: RENDERER_DIST
key_constructs.purpose: Path to the built renderer distribution (dist)
key_constructs.reasoning: Used for locating render assets in production; altering it impacts getTrayIcon and any code that loads renderer files from disk.

key_constructs.name: createWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Creates the default HUD overlay window by delegating to createHudOverlayWindow and storing reference in mainWindow
key_constructs.reasoning: A small factory wrapper to centralize initial HUD creation — other flows rely on createWindow to set mainWindow into a known HUD state.

key_constructs.name: showMainWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Shows, restores and focuses existing mainWindow or creates a new HUD overlay if none exists
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by tray and other user actions to reveal the HUD; must preserve existing window behavior (restore if minimized) and ensure focus, so any change should keep these stepping behaviors.

key_constructs.name: isEditorWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Checks whether a BrowserWindow's webContents URL identifies it as the editor (via query param windowType=editor)
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by menu actions to decide whether to send editor-specific IPC; relies on URL matching convention used when creating windows — keep the URL contract in sync with windows factory.

key_constructs.name: sendEditorMenuAction
key_constructs.purpose: Sends a menu action IPC (load/save/save-as) to the focused editor window, creating an editor window if needed and deferring until did-finish-load
key_constructs.reasoning: Implements robust menu->renderer dispatch. It captures the case where no editor is focused by creating one and deferring the send after did-finish-load. Any edits must preserve the did-finish-load deferral to avoid lost IPC messages.

key_constructs.name: setupApplicationMenu
key_constructs.purpose: Builds and installs the application menu (File/Edit/View/Window), pulling localized labels via mainT
key_constructs.reasoning: Centralizes menu construction and uses localization; menu item click handlers rely on sendEditorMenuAction and other main-level functions — changing menu structure affects UX and IPC flows.

key_constructs.name: createTray
key_constructs.purpose: Instantiates the Tray object with the default icon and binds click/double-click to showMainWindow
key_constructs.reasoning: Tray is created lazily and mutated by updateTrayMenu; code that touches tray lifecycle must avoid re-creating or leaking native Tray objects.

key_constructs.name: getTrayIcon
key_constructs.purpose: Loads a nativeImage from the public or dist path and resizes it for the tray
key_constructs.reasoning: Resolves icons according to process.env.VITE_PUBLIC or RENDERER_DIST. Changes to asset layout or naming must keep this resolution correct; resizing parameters are set to small dimensions expected by native trays.

key_constructs.name: updateTrayMenu
key_constructs.purpose: Updates tray icon, tooltip and context menu based on whether the app is currently recording and which source is selected
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by IPC handlers (via registerIpcHandlers callback) to reflect recording state in the system tray. It mutates tray image, tooltip and context menu; preserve the selectedSourceName usage and localized labels.

key_constructs.name: forceCloseEditorWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Safely force-closes a captured editor window instance while avoiding race conditions with global mainWindow state
key_constructs.reasoning: Implements a captured-window close via setImmediate with isForceClosing guards to avoid races where mainWindow changes during async save flow. Do not replace with immediate mainWindow.close() calls without considering concurrency.

key_constructs.name: createEditorWindowWrapper
key_constructs.purpose: Closes any existing mainWindow and opens a new editor window; wires up unsaved-changes close handling
key_constructs.reasoning: Sets up mainWindow as editor with close handler that prompts for saving; it toggles and respects isForceClosing and editorHasUnsavedChanges. Retains the modal flow of sending 'request-save-before-close' and awaiting 'save-before-close-done' IPC before force-closing.

key_constructs.name: createSourceSelectorWindowWrapper
key_constructs.purpose: Creates a source selector window and clears the reference on close
key_constructs.reasoning: A thin wrapper to ensure single instance and proper lifecycle for the source selector; other code expects an available reference callback for registerIpcHandlers.

key_behaviors: boots recordings directory at startup
creates and shows HUD/editor/source-selector windows
manages tray icon, tooltip and context menu (including recording state)
intercepts editor close to prompt for unsaved changes and coordinate save-before-close
registers session permission handlers and requests microphone access on macOS
routes menu actions to editor, creating it if missing

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or altering the isForceClosing guard or the captured-window logic in forceCloseEditorWindow
pitfalls.consequence: Can cause race conditions where mainWindow changes during async save-before-close flows, leading to windows not closing or unexpected app state
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the captured-window pattern (capture specific window to close, set isForceClosing around close, clear after) and avoid relying solely on global mainWindow at time of async callbacks

pitfalls.mistake: Sending IPC to a newly-created window immediately instead of waiting for did-finish-load
pitfalls.consequence: Renderer may not receive the IPC message (or message is ignored) leading to lost menu actions or failed save/load behavior
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the did-finish-load deferral in sendEditorMenuAction when creating an editor window

pitfalls.mistake: Changing the list of permissions allowed in session.setPermissionCheckHandler / setPermissionRequestHandler without including camera/video/audio names
pitfalls.consequence: getUserMedia and other media APIs could be silently blocked in-app on some platforms, causing recording/camera features to fail
pitfalls.prevention: Ensure allowed array includes 'media', 'audioCapture', 'microphone', 'videoCapture', and 'camera' where required

pitfalls.mistake: Altering RECORDINGS_DIR path semantics or removing ensureRecordingsDir call
pitfalls.consequence: File writes may fail at runtime (missing directory) or recordings saved to unexpected locations
pitfalls.prevention: Retain or replace with equivalent initialization guaranteeing recordings directory exists under app.getPath('userData')

pitfalls.mistake: Recreating the native Tray object repeatedly instead of reusing and mutating it
pitfalls.consequence: Possible UI flicker, resource leaks or inconsistent native behavior across platforms
pitfalls.prevention: Use createTray + updateTrayMenu pattern where tray is created once and updated in-place

key_sections: registerIpcHandlers(...) call: shows how main communicates state to IPC handlers and how callbacks are used to update tray/mainWindow
createEditorWindowWrapper: contains unsaved-changes dialog flow and save-before-close coordination
sendEditorMenuAction: shows robust menu->editor window dispatch (including did-finish-load deferral)
updateTrayMenu: how recording state and selectedSourceName affect tray icon/menu
skip_unless_needed: VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL / path constants block (only relevant if changing build/packaging layout)
mac-specific commandLine appendSwitch near top unless working with mac audio permissions

tests.example_command: npm run test && npm run test:browser:install && npm run test:browser

related_files.relationship: Register & implement IPC handlers that the renderer calls; registerIpcHandlers is invoked from app.whenReady here and receives callbacks that update main state (createEditorWindowWrapper, updateTrayMenu, etc.)
related_files.reason_to_check: If you change callback signatures, window lifecycle, or IPC channel names here, update handler registration and payload expectations in the IPC handlers module

related_files.relationship: Factory functions for createEditorWindow, createHudOverlayWindow and createSourceSelectorWindow are implemented here and are used by this main process file to create windows
related_files.reason_to_check: URL conventions (e.g., query param windowType=editor), webPreferences (e.g., backgroundThrottling), and preload script paths are coupled between these files

related_files.relationship: ContextBridge surface exposed to renderer; renderer uses window.electronAPI functions that trigger main-side IPC handlers registered by registerIpcHandlers
related_files.reason_to_check: If you change IPC channel names, signatures, or behavior in main.ts, ensure preload and renderer consumers and tests are updated

related_files.relationship: Renderer hook that orchestrates recording and calls electronAPI to store sessions; main updates tray via callbacks supplied to registerIpcHandlers
related_files.reason_to_check: Changes to how recording state is reported to main (e.g., different IPC events or payload shapes) must be kept consistent between renderer and main

tests_to_run: npm run test:browser:install && npm run test:browser
data_constants_to_check: RECORDINGS_DIR (this file) - path and creation logic

insights.title: Add switchToHud application flow and wrapper to re-open HUD
insights.problem: Editor needed a way to close and switch back to HUD with correct window lifecycle handling.
insights.root_cause: Window lifecycle and isForceClosing flag needed to be handled to avoid unexpected app exit or duplicate windows.
insights.solution: Implement switchToHudWrapper that closes the mainWindow with isForceClosing toggle and then calls showMainWindow to open HUD; pass wrapper into registerIpcHandlers.
insights.lesson_learned: Window navigation from renderer to main must carefully manage mainWindow references and force-close flags to avoid inconsistent state.

insights.title: Allow video/camera permission checks in session handlers
insights.problem: Camera permission checks were not included in the session's allowed permission list, causing getUserMedia for camera to potentially be blocked when used inside the app context.
insights.root_cause: session.defaultSession permission check/ request handler didn't include 'videoCapture'/'camera'.
insights.solution: Added 'videoCapture' and 'camera' to allowed permission arrays in setPermissionCheckHandler and setPermissionRequestHandler.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding new hardware features (camera), ensure Electron session permission handlers are updated to avoid silent permission rejections.

insights.title: Graceful forced-close when saving before close
insights.problem: When the editor requested save-before-close the previous close flow set a global force-flag and immediately closed the window; this could interact poorly with async save handler and leave inconsistent state.
insights.root_cause: Close flow didn't capture which window to close (mainWindow could change) and relied on global isForceClosing set/unset inline.
insights.solution: Introduce forceCloseEditorWindow helper that captures the specific window, sets isForceClosing, closes inside setImmediate and clears the flag; use the captured window when handling user's Save & Close choice.
insights.lesson_learned: UI close flows that rely on inter-window async communication should capture the specific window instance to close and avoid racing with global mutable window variables.

insights.title: Unsaved changes prompt on editor window close
insights.problem: Closing editor window lost unsaved user edits.
insights.root_cause: Main process closed window without querying renderer about unsaved state.
insights.solution: Track editorHasUnsavedChanges via ipcMain event 'set-has-unsaved-changes'; intercept mainWindow.on('close') to show a dialog offering Save & Close (sends request-save-before-close to renderer), Discard & Close, or Cancel; use isForceClosing guard to avoid reentrancy.
insights.lesson_learned: Coordinate unsaved state between renderer and main with explicit IPC channels; guard close/force-close cycles to avoid infinite loops.

insights.title: Application menu actions for project save/load (+ Save As)
insights.problem: Editor menu needed to trigger save/load project commands and create editor window if not focused.
insights.root_cause: Menu actions previously didn't ensure the editor window was present or expose Save As.
insights.solution: Added sendEditorMenuAction helper that ensures editor window exists and queues a did-finish-load send; added Save Project As menu item and hookup.
insights.lesson_learned: Menu actions should be resilient to app state (e.g., create target window if missing) and must use did-finish-load before sending IPC to newly-created windows.

insights.title: Dynamic tray icon & menu updates while recording
insights.problem: Tray menu always showed static options and icon; UX required different controls while recording (Stop Recording) vs idle (Open / Quit).
insights.root_cause: Tray logic previously created/destroyed or used static icon and menu without reflecting recording state.
insights.solution: Introduced getTrayIcon helper, createTray, and updateTrayMenu(recording:boolean) to switch icon, tooltip, and menu template based on recording state; keep tray persistent instead of destroying it (commit 81b59ca).
insights.lesson_learned: Centralize tray state updates in a small API (createTray, updateTrayMenu) and call updateTrayMenu when recording state changes. Keep tray alive and mutate icon/menu to avoid flicker and race conditions from re-creating native objects.

insights.title: hud overlay close event platform check removed so close works on Windows
insights.problem: Close/hide event handler only quit the app on macOS (process.platform === 'darwin'), so Windows close button did nothing.
insights.root_cause: An explicit platform guard prevented the hud-overlay-close handler from quitting the app on non-macOS platforms (commit 8cbdcf2).
insights.solution: Removed platform check; hud-overlay-close now triggers app.quit() on all platforms so close button works everywhere.
insights.lesson_learned: Platform-specific guards for simple lifecycle events can silently disable behavior on other platforms. When changing app lifecycle behavior, test on all supported OSes.

insights.title: Tooltips and menu reflect recording source name
insights.problem: Tray tooltip didn't show the recording source name while recording.
insights.root_cause: tray.setToolTip used a static string previously.
insights.solution: updateTrayMenu now sets tooltips to include selectedSourceName when recording.
insights.lesson_learned: Small UX improvements like dynamic tooltips improve clarity for recording sessions. Keep selectedSourceName as a module-level variable updated by IPC.

insights.title: HUD overlay hide/close IPC & macOS quit behavior
insights.problem: HUD overlay needed hide and close actions; on macOS closing the overlay should quit the app when requested.
insights.root_cause: Main didn't listen to hud-overlay-close/hide events and didn't keep HUD window reference to minimize/hide.
insights.solution: Added ipcMain listeners for hud-overlay-hide and hud-overlay-close, kept hudOverlayWindow reference and minimized on hide; on macOS hud-overlay-close triggers app.quit().
insights.lesson_learned: When creating transient windows (HUD), main should keep a window reference to allow programmatic minimize/close. Be cautious with platform-specific quit semantics.

insights.title: Disable background throttling for editor window
insights.problem: Renderer was being throttled in background which could affect export or playback tasks.
insights.root_cause: BrowserWindow webPreferences default allowed background throttling.
insights.solution: Set backgroundThrottling: false in createEditorWindow webPreferences.
insights.lesson_learned: For apps that perform CPU-intensive or time-sensitive background work (encoding), disable backgroundThrottling for windows involved in processing.

src/hooks/useScreenRecorder.ts.short_description: A React hook that manages screen/webcam/microphone recording lifecycle, media mixing, and persistence.
src/hooks/useScreenRecorder.ts.description:
This file implements a single exported React hook, useScreenRecorder, which encapsulates all client-side logic for starting, stopping, pausing, restarting, and finalizing screen recordings. It coordinates multiple MediaStreams and MediaRecorders (screen and optional webcam), merges audio tracks when both system audio and microphone are present (via an AudioContext), chooses codecs/bitrates, enforces codec alignment for dimensions, and persists completed recordings by calling into the main process through window.electronAPI (storeRecordedSession, setCurrentRecordingSession / setCurrentVideoPath, switchToEditor, setRecordingState).

The hook was designed to support modern app behaviors: high target frame rates (60fps), multiple recording sources (screen and webcam), microphone and system audio mixing, restart and cancel/discard semantics, and safe finalization that avoids double-saving. It models each recorder as a RecorderHandle (created by createRecorderHandle) containing a MediaRecorder and a promise for the final Blob so finalization (async conversion/fix-up) can be done reliably after stop. Several idempotency and coordination primitives are used: refs for recordingId, finalizingRecordingId, discardRecordingId, allowAutoFinalize, restarting, accumulatedDurationMs and segmentStartedAt to maintain accurate durations across pause/resume.

Because this hook directly uses browser MediaDevices APIs and Electron IPC (window.electronAPI.*), it must handle platform permission failures, fallbacks, and partial capture (e.g., system audio unavailable). The hook surfaces state and setters for external UI: recording/paused booleans, elapsedSeconds, microphone/webcam toggles and device IDs, and an async setWebcamEnabled that pre-flights camera permission via requestCameraAccess and shows user-visible errors using sonner toast.

From commit history, this file contains many fixes and features: robust finalizeRecording as a single async path, explicit cancel/discard semantics, restart semantics that wait for old recorder termination, and careful chunking/timeslice handling for MediaRecorder. These historical changes mean the hook relies on carefully ordered flags and event-driven coordination; edits must respect those ordering assumptions and the reasoning behind the idempotency tokens.

key_constructs.name: createRecorderHandle
key_constructs.purpose: Create a MediaRecorder wrapper that accumulates chunks and exposes a promise which resolves to the final Blob when the recorder stops.
key_constructs.reasoning: Finalization logic in finalizeRecording depends on being able to await the final Blob for a recorder without race conditions. This function ensures chunk collection, ondataavailable behavior, error handling, and that recorder.start(RECORDER_TIMESLICE_MS) is invoked consistently.

key_constructs.name: useScreenRecorder
key_constructs.purpose: A React hook that exposes recording state and controls to UI components and contains all recording lifecycle logic.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the module's public API: components call this hook to start/stop recordings, toggle mic/webcam/system audio, and receive elapsed time and paused/recording flags. Any external changes must preserve the hook's exported shape and semantics because UI components depend on these state setters and async return values.

key_constructs.name: selectMimeType
key_constructs.purpose: Select the best supported WebM/codec mime type on the current platform using MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported.
key_constructs.reasoning: Codec selection affects the produced Blob type and set of supported recording constraints. Consumers depend on it for consistent mimeType passed to MediaRecorder; changing the order or types can affect compatibility and downstream export logic.

key_constructs.name: computeBitrate
key_constructs.purpose: Compute an integer video bitrate based on resolution and optional high-frame-rate boost.
key_constructs.reasoning: Bitrate computation is used to set recorder options (if supported) and determines recording quality/size. It relies on constants like FOUR_K_PIXELS and HIGH_FRAME_RATE_THRESHOLD; preserving this function ensures stable heuristics used throughout the codebase and tests/CI that tune constants accordingly.

key_constructs.name: teardownMedia
key_constructs.purpose: Stop and null out all MediaStream refs and close any AudioContext used for mixing.
key_constructs.reasoning: Proper resource cleanup is crucial to avoid retained tracks, dangling permission prompts, and leaking AudioContext resources. finalizeRecording and the effect cleanup call this; edits must preserve the guarantee that tracks and contexts are stopped/closed and references nulled.

key_constructs.name: setWebcamEnabled
key_constructs.purpose: Async setter that requests camera access preflight and toggles webcamEnabled state, returning false and showing toasts if access is denied.
key_constructs.reasoning: UI toggles use this to avoid starting webcam capture without permission. It relies on requestCameraAccess to check platform-specific permission flows (e.g., macOS). Changes must keep the preflight behavior and error reporting consistent with UX assumptions.

key_constructs.name: finalizeRecording
key_constructs.purpose: Single async finalization path that takes recorder handles, awaits recorded Blobs, fixes WebM durations, calls window.electronAPI.storeRecordedSession, sets current session/path, and switches to editor.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function centralizes persistence and transforms (fixWebmDuration) and includes idempotency checks using finalizingRecordingId and discardRecordingId. It must remain a single coordinated path to avoid doubled saves or lost recordings.

key_constructs.name: stopRecording
key_constructs.purpose: A ref to a function that triggers finalizeRecording for the current recorders and stops both screen and webcam MediaRecorders safely.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function is called from UI, tray events, and restart/cancel flows. It must remain tolerant to invalid states (null recorders) and guard against recorder.stop throwing. The useRef indirection is deliberate to allow stable callback references for event subscriptions.

key_constructs.name: startRecording
key_constructs.purpose: Orchestrates getting selected source from electronAPI, obtaining MediaStreams for screen/system audio/mic/webcam, merging audio tracks, applying constraints, creating recorder handles, and starting timers/state for a new recording.
key_constructs.reasoning: Start flow contains many try/catch branches and fallbacks for permission failures and device capability limitations. It sets up stream refs, recorder handles, applyConstraints attempts, and allowAutoFinalize semantics. Changes should preserve the error-handling, fallback paths, and order of side effects (e.g., setRecording, setElapsedSeconds, window.electronAPI.setRecordingState).

key_behaviors: starts and stops screen recordings with optional webcam and microphone
merges system audio and microphone via an AudioContext destination
finalizes recordings by fixing WebM duration and persisting via electronAPI
supports cancel/discard and restart flows with idempotent finalization

pitfalls.mistake: Assume MediaRecorder.onstop has already delivered final chunks immediately after calling stop()
pitfalls.consequence: Starting a new recorder too early can cause chunk interleaving or lost data during restart. This hook waits for stop events and uses recordedBlobPromise to avoid races.
pitfalls.prevention: Wait for the recorder's recordedBlobPromise or stop event before creating a new recorder; preserve restarting/discard flags and recordedBlob promise semantics.

pitfalls.mistake: Remove or change idempotency refs (finalizingRecordingId, discardRecordingId, allowAutoFinalize)
pitfalls.consequence: Can cause duplicate saves, accidental persistence of discarded recordings, or lost recordings when finalization races with cancels.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep idempotency tokens and checks intact when modifying finalizeRecording/stop/cancel logic.

pitfalls.mistake: Change media dimension handling without honoring CODEC_ALIGNMENT or failing to fallback on applyConstraints errors
pitfalls.consequence: Recordings may use odd dimensions incompatible with some encoders, or start may throw if applyConstraints is assumed to always succeed.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect CODEC_ALIGNMENT rounding and surround applyConstraints calls with try/catch and graceful fallbacks.

pitfalls.mistake: Assume system audio is always available or that getUserMedia audio requests will always succeed
pitfalls.consequence: Start recording may fail or leave partial streams; users will see confusing behavior without explicit toasts and fallback to audio:false.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve existing try/catch and toast error messages for permission denial and fallback paths as currently implemented.

pitfalls.mistake: Stop or null out streams inconsistently in error paths
pitfalls.consequence: Leaked MediaStream tracks, retained camera/microphone permissions, or AudioContext leaks.
pitfalls.prevention: Use teardownMedia consistently in all error/cleanup branches; ensure streams are stopped and refs nulled.

key_sections: createRecorderHandle: understand how recorder results are awaited
selectMimeType & computeBitrate: codec/quality decisions used when creating recorders
startRecording: main orchestration for getUserMedia, stream composition, and recorder creation
finalizeRecording: persistence and post-processing (fixWebmDuration, electronAPI.storeRecordedSession)
skip_unless_needed: top-level constant blocks (tuning knobs) unless you are changing bitrate/size heuristics
toast text keys and i18n lookups unless modifying user-visible messages

related_files.relationship: Uses the window.electronAPI IPC functions (getSelectedSource, storeRecordedSession, setCurrentRecordingSession/setCurrentVideoPath, switchToEditor, setRecordingState) that this hook calls to persist recordings and change app state.
related_files.reason_to_check: If you change arguments or return types of electronAPI methods, update usages here accordingly (file name, session object shape).

related_files.relationship: Defines the RecordingSession type/shape that storeRecordedSession returns and that this hook sets via window.electronAPI.setCurrentRecordingSession.
related_files.reason_to_check: When changing the structure of persisted session objects or file naming conventions check finalizeRecording's calls that build fileName and createdAt.

related_files.relationship: The editor consumes the session/path that this hook sets via electronAPI.switchToEditor and setCurrentRecordingSession/setCurrentVideoPath to open the recording for editing.
related_files.reason_to_check: Any changes to how sessions are stored/passed (session vs path) will affect editor load behavior.

related_files.relationship: Used by setWebcamEnabled to preflight camera permissions; platform-specific permission flow implementations live here.
related_files.reason_to_check: If requestCameraAccess interface changes, setWebcamEnabled should be updated to match new return shape or semantics.

tests_to_run: npm run test:browser (if touching browser-specific flows and MediaRecorder wrappers)

insights.title: Fix auto-finalize duration calculation after pause/resume
insights.problem: getRecordingDurationMs computed segmentDuration conditionally using recorder.state which produced incorrect durations after pause/resume.
insights.root_cause: Duration relied on recorder.state instead of tracking segmentStartedAt, causing false 0 segments when state transitions occurred.
insights.solution: Simplified segment duration computation to use segmentStartedAt.current === null ? 0 : Date.now() - segmentStartedAt.current, ensuring continuity across pause/resume.
insights.Lesson Learned: When measuring durations across pause/resume, rely on stable timestamp bookkeeping (segmentStartedAt/accumulated) rather than ephemeral external state.

insights.title: Restore cancelRecording and ensure discard logic
insights.problem: Need a way to cancel a recording (discard) and prevent auto-finalize.
insights.root_cause: Cancel logic previously removed or missing; auto-finalize could run unexpectedly.
insights.solution: Reintroduced cancelRecording that sets discardRecordingId and allowAutoFinalize flag, then calls stopRecording.
insights.Lesson Learned: Provide explicit cancel/discard APIs and update auto-finalize/commit flags consistently when aborting a recording.

insights.title: Add Cancel Recording action that discards current recording
insights.problem: Users needed a way to cancel an in-progress recording and ensure it isn't auto-finalized or persisted.
insights.root_cause: No clear cancel path; stopping a recording normally would finalize or persist it.
insights.solution: Add cancelRecording which marks the current recordingId as discarded (discardRecordingId), sets allowAutoFinalize to false, and stops the recorder via stopRecording.current(). Export/save paths check discardRecordingId to avoid finalizing.
insights.lesson_learned: When implementing cancel semantics, ensure flags clearly indicate discard intent to downstream finalizers; stop operations should consult those flags.

insights.title: Support webcam device selection and pass-through
insights.problem: Recording hooks did not expose or use a webcamDeviceId, making webcam selection and persistence impossible.
insights.root_cause: useScreenRecorder only tracked microphoneDeviceId; webcam device selection and getUserMedia options were not wired.
insights.solution: Added webcamDeviceId state and setter, propagated it into the getUserMedia call for webcam (deviceId exact constraint), and returned setters to outer components.

insights.title: Prevent concurrent restarts during restartRecording
insights.problem: Restarting recording could race: multiple restarts could be triggered concurrently leading to inconsistent media recorder states or lost recordings.
insights.root_cause: restartRecording did not guard against an already-in-progress restart and used mediaRecorder.current which could change during the sequence.
insights.solution: Added restarting ref guard to early-return if a restart is already in progress; captured the recorder reference at start and listened for its 'stop' event to wait for full stop before starting a new recording; ensure restarting flag cleared in finally.

insights.title: Reset webcam state when camera access is denied
insights.problem: If the user denied camera permission, webcam stream tracks might remain or webcamEnabled remained true leading to inconsistent UI/state.
insights.root_cause: On getUserMedia error the code logged but didn't stop/clear existing webcam stream or update webcamEnabled state.
insights.solution: Stop and clear existing webcamStream tracks, null the stream ref, and set webcamEnabledState(false) so UI and recording logic correctly reflect that webcam cannot be used.

insights.title: Finalize externally stopped recordings reliably
insights.problem: If a MediaRecorder was stopped externally (e.g., OS-level stop), the app didn't reliably finalize and persist the recording session. This resulted in lost recordings or inconsistent UI state.
insights.root_cause: Finalization logic was tied to the stop handler and the main stop function lacked idempotency and coordination for externally triggered stops and async persistence tasks.
insights.solution: Extract finalizeRecording as a reusable async function that captures the active recorder handles and recording id, guards against duplicate finalization with finalizingRecordingId, and is invoked both from stop button and recorder 'stop' event. Added allowAutoFinalize flag to opt-in auto-finalization only when appropriate.
insights.lesson_learned: Recording lifecycle must separate: (1) immediate recorder stop, (2) single finalization flow that persists data. Guard with an idempotency token to prevent double finalization.

insights.title: Add webcam support and asynchronous webcam toggle with permission preflight
insights.problem: Support for recording webcam overlay required probing camera permission and orchestrating an additional MediaRecorder; errors and permission-denied states needed to be surfaced without breaking screen recording.
insights.root_cause: Original recorder code assumed a single MediaRecorder stream and synchronous behavior; adding webcam required parallel recorder handles, separate streams, and lifecycle management.
insights.solution: Introduce RecorderHandle wrapper (createRecorderHandle), separate screenRecorder and webcamRecorder handles, webcamStream and webcamStream acquisition with preflight permissions via window.electronAPI.requestCameraAccess, and teardownMedia to stop and null streams. Persist session as screen + optional webcam via window.electronAPI.storeRecordedSession. Ensure finalization handles both recorder outputs.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding simultaneous recording sources, model each as its own recorder handle with promise-based completion. Use preflight permission checks on platforms that require them (macOS). Persist a combined session object rather than a single video path.

insights.title: Async restart recording to avoid chunk race
insights.problem: Restarting a recording immediately could race with the old recorder's onstop handler and its chunk handling, causing discard/new-session interleaving.
insights.root_cause: restartRecording called stop/start back-to-back without waiting for the previous recorder to emit 'stop' and finish delivering its final chunks.
insights.solution: Make restartRecording async: set discard flag, call stopRecording.current(), then wait for the old recorder's 'stop' event before calling startRecording().
insights.lesson_learned: When reusing mutable recorder instances or resources, wait for their termination events before creating new ones to avoid overlapping state and data races.

insights.title: Add microphone capture and merge with screen stream
insights.problem: Recording previously lacked an integrated microphone option with device selection and graceful permission handling.
insights.root_cause: Screen-only recording didn't support adding a mic track and handling permission denial cleanly.
insights.solution: Add microphoneEnabled state, request microphone stream with specific deviceId constraints, combine microphone audio track with screen's video track into a new MediaStream for MediaRecorder, add error toasts for permission denial, and stop/cleanup mic and screen streams on stop.
insights.lesson_learned: When merging multiple MediaStreams: create a new MediaStream and add tracks intentionally; always stop and null out intermediate streams; expose microphone state at hook level for UI.

insights.title: Better permission error reporting
insights.problem: Errors starting recording could be opaque; permission denied cases needed clear user feedback.
insights.root_cause: Generic catch did not distinguish NotAllowedError/Permission denied.
insights.solution: Inspect error message and show descriptive toast messages for permission denial vs other errors; ensure streams are cleaned up on failure.
insights.lesson_learned: Differentiate permission errors and provide actionable feedback; always clean up resources in error paths.

insights.title: Replace magic numbers with named constants and codec alignment
insights.problem: Hard-coded magic numbers (frame rates, bitrates, default sizes) made the recorder code harder to reason about and adjust.
insights.root_cause: Configuration values were embedded inline which made tuning/maintenance error prone.
insights.solution: Introduced named constants for target frame rate, resolutions, bitrates, codec alignment, recorder timeslice, and more. Ensured width/height rounding uses CODEC_ALIGNMENT and fallback defaults.
insights.lesson_learned: Centralize tuning knobs and codec constraints (e.g., width must be divisible by 2) to avoid ad-hoc fixes. Use constants to document intent (e.g., HIGH_FRAME_RATE_BOOST).

insights.title: Improve codec selection and bitrate computation for screen recording
insights.problem: Previous implementation used a static set of codecs, a hardcoded bitrate heuristic, and didn't attempt to lock constraints gracefully.
insights.root_cause: Naive recording defaults could either overshoot or underutilize device capabilities and didn't attempt to apply constraints safely.
insights.solution: Added selectMimeType preference list using MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported, computeBitrate(width,height) heuristic with highFrameRate boost, attempted applyConstraints with try/catch and fallback, ensured even dimensions, and logged recording config.
insights.lesson_learned: Media capture constraints should be attempted but not assumed — applyConstraints can fail and must be handled. Use MediaRecorder.isTypeSupported to pick the best codec available. Keep dimensions even for many codecs.

insights.title: Avoid large timeslices and clear chunks promptly
insights.problem: Large ondataavailable timeslices can affect latency; chunks array memory needs timely clearing.
insights.root_cause: recorder.start(5000) produced large blob creation latency; clearing chunks only after sending caused memory retention.
insights.solution: Switched to recorder.start(1000) (smaller timeslice) and clear chunks immediately after manifesting blob. Also return path via electronAPI.setCurrentVideoPath when available.
insights.lesson_learned: Recording timeslice affects latency and memory — choose a balance (1s here). Free chunk buffers early to reduce memory pressure.

src/components/launch/LaunchWindow.tsx.short_description: React HUD / launcher UI for starting/stopping recordings, selecting devices and switching to the editor.
src/components/launch/LaunchWindow.tsx.description:
This component renders the floating HUD/launch window used when starting and controlling screen recordings. It centralizes device selection (microphone, webcam), system-audio toggle, source selection, recording controls (record/pause/resume/stop/restart/cancel), language selector, and quick actions (open video file, open project, hide/close HUD). The file exists to provide the immediate recording controls presented in a small overlay window that is viewport-fixed (never clipped) so the user can manage recording state without switching to the full editor.

LaunchWindow is implemented as a single React function component that composes several custom hooks (useScreenRecorder, useMicrophoneDevices, useCameraDevices, useAudioLevelMeter) and i18n helpers (useI18n/useScopedT). The component uses local state for transient UI interactions (hover/focus expansion of device panels, whether a source has been selected) and many small handler functions which call window.electronAPI methods (openSourceSelector, openVideoFilePicker, loadProjectFile, setCurrentVideoPath, switchToEditor, hudOverlayHide/Close). The component's layout is purposely fixed to viewport coordinates and uses CSS helper class constants for consistent HUD button groups and behavior.

Design decisions reflected in the file: (1) Accessibility — the code preserves keyboard focus targets even when camera devices are unavailable (sr-only select fallback) and uses visually-hidden fallbacks; (2) Graceful electron integration — guards against the absence of window.electronAPI so the UI can render in non-Electron/dev contexts; (3) Non-blocking device toggles — toggling webcam/mic/system audio is performed via state setters and hooks that handle permission preflight elsewhere (useScreenRecorder/useCameraDevices) rather than blocking the UI during recording. The commit history shows attention to edge-cases: ensuring the device-selector panels are never clipped, adding cancel recording, enabling toggles while recording, and ensuring consistent badge heights.

key_constructs.name: LaunchWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Main React component that renders the HUD/launch UI for recording and device selection.
key_constructs.reasoning: All UI sections (language switcher, device panels, HUD bar, action handlers) are composed inside this function; changes to recording flows, device toggles or electron IPC calls must be made here or in the hooks it consumes.

key_constructs.name: ICON_CONFIG
key_constructs.purpose: Configuration map that declares which icon component and size to use for each HUD symbol.
key_constructs.reasoning: Centralizes icon selection and sizing so UI buttons use consistent icons. An agent editing visuals must respect these keys (they're used by getIcon).

key_constructs.name: getIcon
key_constructs.purpose: Helper that returns a React icon element from ICON_CONFIG by name.
key_constructs.reasoning: Used throughout the JSX to render icons; modifying the signature requires updating all call sites.

key_constructs.name: hudGroupClasses
key_constructs.purpose: CSS utility string for the button group container styling (used for hover states and rounded grouping).
key_constructs.reasoning: Used repeatedly to ensure visual consistency; experiments with layout or transitions should consider this shared class.

key_constructs.name: hudIconBtnClasses
key_constructs.purpose: CSS utility string for individual icon button styling inside the HUD.
key_constructs.reasoning: Shared styling for interactive buttons; used by many elements and impacts hover/active visuals.

key_constructs.name: windowBtnClasses
key_constructs.purpose: CSS utility string for the top-right window control buttons (minimize/close style).
key_constructs.reasoning: Separates 'window controls' style from HUD icons; keep consistent when adding new window-level actions.

key_constructs.name: openSourceSelector
key_constructs.purpose: Event handler that calls window.electronAPI.openSourceSelector() to open native source picker.
key_constructs.reasoning: Simple wrapper around a preload IPC call; the component relies on preload/main to implement this IPC identity and behavior.

key_constructs.name: openVideoFile
key_constructs.purpose: Asynchronous handler that opens native file picker via electronAPI, sets the chosen video path and switches to editor.
key_constructs.reasoning: Chains multiple electronAPI calls (openVideoFilePicker -> setCurrentVideoPath -> switchToEditor); changes must preserve order and handle canceled/failed results.

key_constructs.name: openProjectFile
key_constructs.purpose: Async handler that loads a project file via electronAPI and switches to the editor on success.
key_constructs.reasoning: Relies on electronAPI.loadProjectFile contract (result.canceled, result.success); editors will expect the current project to be loaded on switchToEditor.

key_constructs.name: sendHudOverlayHide
key_constructs.purpose: Calls electronAPI.hudOverlayHide to hide the HUD overlay (if available).
key_constructs.reasoning: A small wrapper used by window controls; preload and main must implement this IPC id for behavior to work.

key_constructs.name: sendHudOverlayClose
key_constructs.purpose: Calls electronAPI.hudOverlayClose to close the HUD overlay window (if available).
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by top-right close control; preserve the IPC identity and guard for absence of electronAPI.

key_constructs.name: toggleMicrophone
key_constructs.purpose: Toggles microphone enabled state but only when not recording (UI guard).
key_constructs.reasoning: The function intentionally prevents enabling/disabling microphone during recording at the UI level (per current logic) — note the commit history where this behavior was refined; editing it requires awareness of the underlying hook behavior (useScreenRecorder) and the intent to block/allow toggles while recording.

key_behaviors: renders floating HUD with recording controls and device selectors
queries and displays selected screen/source periodically
toggles system audio, microphone and webcam states
starts/stops/pauses/resumes/restarts/cancels recordings via useScreenRecorder
opens video files or project files and switches to the editor via electronAPI

pitfalls.mistake: Assume window.electronAPI is always present and synchronous
pitfalls.consequence: Runtime exceptions in non-Electron contexts (vite dev or browser tests) or broken behavior if IPC contract differs
pitfalls.prevention: Continue to guard calls with if (window.electronAPI) and preserve the existing async flow and result checks (result.canceled, result.success).

pitfalls.mistake: Remove the sr-only select fallback when webcamExpanded and no camera devices
pitfalls.consequence: Keyboard and assistive technology users would lose a focusable element, breaking accessibility (regression referenced in commit history).
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the invisible/select fallback so there is always at least one focusable element in the expanded webcam area.

pitfalls.mistake: Change the setInterval polling of getSelectedSource (500ms) without clearing on unmount
pitfalls.consequence: Leaked intervals that keep accessing electronAPI after component unmount, causing unexpected IPC calls or memory leaks.
pitfalls.prevention: If changing polling frequency or strategy, ensure the interval is cleared on unmount and consider replacing with an event-based IPC if main can emit updates.

pitfalls.mistake: Modify toggleMicrophone or webcam toggle semantics without coordinating with useScreenRecorder
pitfalls.consequence: UX regressions where toggles are disabled or cause errors during recording; underlying hook may expect toggles to be async and handle permissions.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the hook contracts: toggles call setters and the hooks perform permission/preflight and state changes.

pitfalls.mistake: Alter the order of IPC calls in openVideoFile (setCurrentVideoPath before switchToEditor or not handling canceled result)
pitfalls.consequence: Editor may open without an active file or with stale state; user flow could break.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the order: open picker -> check canceled -> setCurrentVideoPath -> switchToEditor; guard on result.success and result.path.

key_sections: Hooks usage at top (useScreenRecorder, useMicrophoneDevices, useCameraDevices, useAudioLevelMeter): these provide the core data and side-effects for recording and device selection
Event handler definitions (openVideoFile, openProjectFile, openSourceSelector, sendHudOverlayHide/Close): these map UI actions to electronAPI or recorder hooks
JSX structure: Language switcher (top-left), Device selectors (bottom above HUD), HUD bar (main controls) — important for layout/positioning changes
skip_unless_needed: ICON_CONFIG and small CSS class constants (hudGroupClasses, hudIconBtnClasses) — only edit if changing iconography or shared styles
Dev-only requestCameraAccess effect (runs only in DEV)

insights.title: Ensure a focusable element exists when webcam panel is expanded but no devices are present
insights.problem: When webcam panel was expanded and there were no camera devices (loading/error/empty), keyboard users had no focusable element in that region.
insights.root_cause: Conditional rendering hid the select element when expanded; no sr-only fallback was present.
insights.solution: Render an sr-only <select> when webcamExpanded and cameraDevices.length === 0 so keyboard users always have a focusable element.
insights.lesson_learned: Maintain accessible focus targets even in empty/error states; assistive and keyboard users rely on predictable focusable elements.

insights.title: Add Cancel Recording button to HUD
insights.problem: HUD lacked an explicit cancel action to discard an in-progress recording.
insights.root_cause: Only stop/restart actions existed previously.
insights.solution: Add a Cancel button in UI and wire it to cancelRecording from useScreenRecorder; add i18n keys for the tooltip/label.
insights.lesson_learned: Provide explicit destructive/cancel actions in recording UIs and ensure localization is updated.

insights.title: HUD / device selector clipping and unstable layout
insights.problem: Device selector panels and HUD were clipped or shifted when the window content used full-height (h-full) and absolute positioning inside a non-flex container; hover expansion caused layout shifts and clipping.
insights.root_cause: Incorrect positioning semantics combined with container sizing: absolute children were constrained by a parent that didn't span the viewport; inconsistent use of absolute vs fixed positioning and missing flex container for the transparent Electron window resulted in clipping and unexpected layout behavior.
insights.solution: Switched container to a layout that ensures full viewport coverage and consistent HUD placement: restored a flex parent for transparent Electron window, moved selectors and HUD to fixed positioning in later tweaks so they are viewport-relative (never clipped), and anchored device selectors above the HUD. Also standardized bottom offsets (e.g. bottom-[60px]) and added electron drag/no-drag classes.

insights.title: Introduce interactive hover-expanded device selector UI
insights.problem: Previously no webcam selector; mic selector had limited UX and could cause layout jumps when expanded.
insights.root_cause: Device selector UI needed to show a summary label and expand on hover; previous structure used fixed large paddings and absolute widths which caused inconsistent rendering.
insights.solution: Added state for hover (isMicHovered/isWebcamHovered), controlled width transitions (style width change), truncate label when collapsed, and a nicer select UI when expanded. Reworked internal elements (min-w-0, flex-1, smaller text sizes) to avoid overflow and truncation issues.

insights.title: Inconsistent badge heights
insights.problem: Badges/selectors used min-h-[36px] in some places and different sizing elsewhere, causing misaligned badges when hovered/expanded.
insights.root_cause: Mix of min-height and explicit height created inconsistent visual heights across similar components.
insights.solution: Enforce identical badge height using h-[36px] (and earlier used min-h-[36px]) across both mic and webcam selectors to ensure consistent baseline height.

insights.title: Allow toggling webcam while recording (intentional change/unintended blocking)
insights.problem: The webcam toggle button was previously disabled while a recording was active, blocking the user from enabling/disabling the webcam during an ongoing recording.
insights.root_cause: UI logic disabled the toggle (disabled={recording}) and guarded onClick with an if (!recording) branch, preventing state changes while recording even when backing systems support it.
insights.solution: Removed the disabled prop and the early-recording guard; moved camera permission probe and checks into useScreenRecorder so the toggle can be async and safe while recording.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid coupling UI interactivity to recording state when underlying recorder APIs and preflight checks can handle dynamic changes. Prefer asynchronous toggles that perform permission preflight and surface failure via toast/errors.

insights.title: Revamped HUD UI, microphone controls and project open
insights.problem: HUD needed improved layout and microphone UX; also provide Open Project action from HUD.
insights.root_cause: HUD lacked UI for mic device selection, level meter, and project open; some icons inconsistent.
insights.solution: Large UI refactor: new groups, icon buttons, mic select, AudioLevelMeter, Open Project button which calls electronAPI.loadProjectFile() then switchToEditor(), toggleMicrophone logic that sets microphoneEnabled only when not recording.
insights.lesson_learned: UI changes interact with recording state; guard interactions (e.g. disable mic/device change while recording) and ensure API calls exist in preload/main.

insights.title: Refined launch hud style and reduced blur
insights.problem: HUD bar styles were hard-coded inline and blur/saturation were high.
insights.root_cause: Styling lived inline and was inconsistent.
insights.solution: Added .hudBar to CSS and adjusted background gradient/backdropFilter values to reduce blur and saturation; minor layout tweaks.
insights.lesson_learned: Consolidate shared visual styles into CSS classes instead of inline styles for maintainability.

insights.title: Use ContentClamp for truncated source labels
insights.problem: Manual truncate helper duplicated where source name is shown in the launch window.
insights.root_cause: Ad-hoc truncation function in LaunchWindow instead of reusing common component.
insights.solution: Replaced truncateText with <ContentClamp truncateLength={6}>{selectedSource}</ContentClamp> and adjusted styling (commit 16752a7).
insights.lesson_learned: Centralizing small UI utilities (truncation + hover full-text) avoids duplication and ensures consistent behavior across UIs.

insights.title: HUD overlay UX improvements: elapsed timer, hide/close buttons, open file flow
insights.problem: HUD was minimal — no elapsed time or quick hide/close. Users also needed to load arbitrary video files.
insights.root_cause: Launch HUD originally had minimal controls; open-file flow wasn't integrated.
insights.solution: Show elapsed recording timer, expose hide and close buttons that use electronAPI.hudOverlayHide/hudOverlayClose, add openVideoFile using electronAPI.openVideoFilePicker to set current video path and switch to editor.
insights.lesson_learned: Small HUD improvements improve operability. Keep renderer -> main IPC ids consistent and update preload and main handlers together.

src/App.tsx.short_description: Root React component that picks which UI window to render and initializes fonts/backgrounds.
src/App.tsx.description:
This file exports the default React component App which is the renderer entry UI for the application. Its primary responsibility is to detect the type of window the current renderer instance is supposed to act as (via the windowType query parameter) and render the corresponding React subtree: hud-overlay (LaunchWindow), source-selector (SourceSelector), editor (VideoEditor wrapped in ShortcutsProvider plus ShortcutsConfigDialog), or a fallback placeholder. It also performs initialization side effects on mount: reading the query parameter, setting the document/background transparency when appropriate, and triggering custom font loading.

App exists to centralize renderer-level bootstrapping logic (which UI root to render and small DOM-level side effects) so the rest of the UI components can assume the right context. It intentionally manipulates document.body, document.documentElement, and the element with id 'root' to ensure transparent backgrounds for overlay windows (hud-overlay and source-selector) — an important cross-cutting concern for Electron overlay/frameless windows. It also ensures custom fonts are requested to be loaded at app startup by invoking loadAllCustomFonts and logs errors without failing the mount.

The component composes higher-order context/providers used by the rest of the UI: TooltipProvider (wraps everything) and a Toaster component (global UI feedback). For the editor windowType it provides a ShortcutsProvider around VideoEditor and renders ShortcutsConfigDialog as a sibling so keyboard shortcuts and configuration UI are available when running the editor. Because this file contains lightweight orchestration and DOM-level manipulations, changes here can affect several major behaviors (window appearance, font availability, and global providers) across renderer windows.

key_constructs.name: App
key_constructs.purpose: Default-exported React component that selects and renders the window-specific UI and performs startup side effects.
key_constructs.reasoning: App is the renderer entry point for the Vite/Electron renderer. It reads the windowType param once on mount, applies transparency for overlay windows, triggers font loading, and composes global providers (TooltipProvider and Toaster). Any edits that change the mount-time behavior, provider composition, or the windowType switch affect which root component is loaded for each Electron window type.

key_constructs.name: content
key_constructs.purpose: A self-invoking switch expression that returns the appropriate React subtree for the resolved windowType.
key_constructs.reasoning: This local constant encapsulates the decision logic for which UI to render. It centralizes mapping windowType -> component, so an agent editing this file must preserve the mappings for 'hud-overlay', 'source-selector', and 'editor' and understand that the editor case relies on ShortcutsProvider context and ShortcutsConfigDialog being rendered together.

key_behaviors: reads windowType from URL query on mount
sets transparent backgrounds for hud-overlay and source-selector windows
loads custom application fonts on initialization
renders root UI subtree based on windowType and provides global UI providers

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or changing the transparent-background DOM manipulations for 'hud-overlay' or 'source-selector'.
pitfalls.consequence: Overlay or source selector windows that expect transparency in Electron (frameless/overlay) may render with opaque background, breaking visual integration or hit-testing expectations.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the existing document/body/root style changes intact for the two overlay window types, or ensure an equivalent mechanism is implemented in Electron main or CSS before modifying.

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming document.getElementById('root') always exists and mutating it without checks.
pitfalls.consequence: In test environments (jsdom) or non-standard bootstraps the root element may be absent and calls will be no-ops; conversely, removing the null-safe access may cause runtime errors.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the optional chaining used when accessing 'root' (?.) and preserve the order of manipulations to avoid false assumptions.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering provider composition (removing TooltipProvider or Toaster) or changing their placement relative to content.
pitfalls.consequence: Global UI behaviors (toasts, tooltips) relied upon by many components will break or change; tests or UI flows expecting those providers may fail silently.
pitfalls.prevention: Retain TooltipProvider wrapping and Toaster rendering at root, or ensure consumers are updated accordingly if the composition changes.

pitfalls.mistake: Removing the catch() around loadAllCustomFonts or allowing failures to bubble up.
pitfalls.consequence: Font-loading failures could cause unhandled promise rejections or prevent the component from mounting cleanly in environments where font loading isn't supported.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the error handling behavior: load fonts, log failures, but do not block component rendering.

key_sections: useEffect: reads the windowType query param, sets transparency for overlay windows, triggers loadAllCustomFonts
content switch: maps windowType strings to UI components (hud-overlay, source-selector, editor, default)
return JSX: shows how TooltipProvider and Toaster are composed around the chosen content
skip_unless_needed: default fallback JSX (simple placeholder) — only relevant when windowType is missing

related_files.relationship: Used as the HUD overlay root when windowType === 'hud-overlay'.
related_files.reason_to_check: If the overlay's mounting/props expectations change (e.g., requires a provider), App's composition or background logic may need updating.

related_files.relationship: Rendered when windowType === 'source-selector'.
related_files.reason_to_check: Source selector UI may rely on transparent background or global providers; changes to its root expectations could require App adjustments.

related_files.relationship: Rendered when windowType === 'editor' and wrapped by ShortcutsProvider.
related_files.reason_to_check: Editor relies on ShortcutsProvider context and presence of ShortcutsConfigDialog; altering either component's API or context contract may require edits in App.

related_files.relationship: ShortcutsProvider used to wrap the editor subtree; provides keyboard shortcut context.
related_files.reason_to_check: If the context provider API changes or requires different placement, App must be updated to preserve keyboard shortcut behavior.

related_files.relationship: Defines loadAllCustomFonts which App invokes at startup.
related_files.reason_to_check: Changes in font loading behavior, return value, or error semantics affect how App should call and handle promises from this module.

npm run dev to visually validate overlay and editor windows in dev

electron/windows.ts.short_description: Factory functions to create and configure Electron BrowserWindow instances (HUD, editor, source selector).
electron/windows.ts.description:
This module centralizes creation and configuration of three kinds of Electron BrowserWindow instances used by the main process: the HUD overlay (createHudOverlayWindow), the main editor (createEditorWindow), and the source-selector modal (createSourceSelectorWindow). It computes placement and sizes (using screen.getPrimaryDisplay()), constructs the windows with explicit webPreferences (preload, contextIsolation, nodeIntegration disabled, backgroundThrottling set), attaches a did-finish-load hook to send a heartbeat message to the renderer, and loads either the dev URL (VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL) or the built index.html with a query parameter windowType so the renderer can adapt UI per window type.

The file also keeps a module-scoped handle hudOverlayWindow so the main process can respond to an ipcMain event ('hud-overlay-hide') and minimize the HUD when requested by the renderer. The module respects a HEADLESS environment flag to hide windows in CI/headless runs and uses RENDERER_DIST derived from APP_ROOT to find built assets. Several implementation details are important to other parts of the app: the query parameter names (?windowType=...) are part of the contract with renderer code (renderer reads windowType to render different UI); the webPreferences settings (preload path, backgroundThrottling=false, contextIsolation) are intentionally set for security and UX (e.g., to keep recording active while window backgrounded); and the HUD window geometry (width, height, min/max bounds) must stay in sync with HUD renderer layout to avoid clipping.

The module is used by the main process (electron/main.ts) and must remain compatible with how the renderer expects to be launched. Environment variables (VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL and HEADLESS) affect behavior and are used by test/CI flows. The commit history shows repeated adjustments to HUD geometry and a cautionary change around Mac-specific option application (conditional object spread), so edits must respect both cross-platform differences and previously observed pitfalls.

key_constructs.name: __dirname
key_constructs.purpose: Module-local directory path computed from import.meta.url; used to build paths for preload and dist files.
key_constructs.reasoning: __dirname is used as the base for APP_ROOT and to locate preload.mjs. Any changes to how files are packaged or where preload is emitted should keep this path logic consistent.

key_constructs.name: APP_ROOT
key_constructs.purpose: Root directory of the electron package (one level up from this file).
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to compute RENDERER_DIST; changing packaging layout or moving files requires updating APP_ROOT or its usages.

key_constructs.name: VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL
key_constructs.purpose: Environment variable that, when set, causes windows to load the Vite dev server URL instead of built files.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the dev/prod switch used by the main process. Tests and local dev flow depend on this variable being present or absent.

key_constructs.name: RENDERER_DIST
key_constructs.purpose: Filesystem path to the built renderer assets (index.html) used in production mode.
key_constructs.reasoning: Used in loadFile calls. If the build output location changes, this constant must be kept aligned.

key_constructs.name: HEADLESS
key_constructs.purpose: Boolean flag derived from process.env to decide whether to show windows (used for CI/headless scenarios).
key_constructs.reasoning: Controls the show property on BrowserWindow instances; tests and CI rely on HEADLESS to avoid creating visible windows.

key_constructs.name: hudOverlayWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Module-scoped reference to the current HUD overlay BrowserWindow instance (or null).
key_constructs.reasoning: Maintaining this reference enables IPC-driven operations (ipcMain listener for 'hud-overlay-hide') and ensures closed event clears the reference. Multiple HUD calls should not leak references.

key_constructs.name: createHudOverlayWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Creates and returns the HUD overlay BrowserWindow positioned at the bottom-center of the primary display.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the main entry point for HUD lifecycle. It sets fixed sizes (width/height/min/max), transparency, alwaysOnTop, skipTaskbar, backgroundThrottling=false, preloads the renderer preload script, and loads the renderer with windowType=hud-overlay.

key_constructs.name: createEditorWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Creates and returns the main editor BrowserWindow, applies macOS-specific title bar options, and maximizes the window by default.
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to open the editor UI. It includes a conditional spread for Mac-only options, sets webPreferences (note webSecurity disabled here), and loads the renderer with windowType=editor.

key_constructs.name: createSourceSelectorWindow
key_constructs.purpose: Creates a centered modal BrowserWindow used to select capture sources (screens/windows).
key_constructs.reasoning: This window is modal-style (frame: false, transparent) sized to contain source selection UI and loads renderer with windowType=source-selector.

key_behaviors: creates HUD overlay window positioned bottom-center on primary display
creates maximized editor window with macOS-specific options when on darwin
creates centered source selector window
listens to 'hud-overlay-hide' IPC and minimizes HUD if present
loads dev server URL when VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL is set or built index.html otherwise

pitfalls.mistake: Modify or remove the hudOverlayWindow module-scoped reference or its closed handler
pitfalls.consequence: Renderer requests to minimize/hide the HUD (via 'hud-overlay-hide') will fail; references may leak and subsequent createHudOverlayWindow calls may leave orphaned windows.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep hudOverlayWindow reference assignment and win.on('closed') clearing behavior intact.

pitfalls.mistake: Change the URL query parameter key or values (windowType) used in win.loadURL/loadFile
pitfalls.consequence: Renderer code that checks windowType to decide which UI to render (HUD vs editor vs source selector) will not receive expected value, causing wrong UI to show or runtime errors.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the '?windowType=...' query convention or update the renderer to match any change.

pitfalls.mistake: Use the ...(isMac && {...}) object-spread pattern or otherwise spread a boolean into window options without ensuring an object
pitfalls.consequence: Spreading a non-object into an object literal is fragile and has been recorded in commit history as a breaking change; depending on runtime it may throw or lead to unexpected options being set, causing window creation issues on non-mac platforms.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect platform branching semantics; ensure only objects are spread into BrowserWindow options.

pitfalls.mistake: Remove or change webPreferences.backgroundThrottling setting
pitfalls.consequence: Renderer may be background-throttled during recording, leading to dropped frames or audio desync during long recordings.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep backgroundThrottling:false for windows that participate in recording flows (HUD/editor) unless the renderer is updated to handle throttling.

pitfalls.mistake: Change HUD width/height/min/max bounds without updating renderer HUD layout
pitfalls.consequence: HUD UI could be clipped, overflow, or misaligned relative to native window bounds (past issues in commit history demonstrate this).
pitfalls.prevention: Keep window geometry in sync with renderer HUD CSS/layout; verify visually or via renderer tests after changes.

key_sections: createHudOverlayWindow: positioning, size consts, special window flags (transparent, alwaysOnTop, skipTaskbar, backgroundThrottling)
createEditorWindow: macOS conditional options, maximize behavior, webPreferences differences (webSecurity:false)
createSourceSelectorWindow: dimensions and centering logic
skip_unless_needed: the top-of-file constants (__dirname, APP_ROOT, RENDERER_DIST) are straightforward path setup
ipcMain.on('hud-overlay-hide') wiring unless modifying HUD control behavior

tests.example_command: npm run test (or npm run test:browser for renderer/browser tests)

related_files.reason_to_check: If the preload file name or location changes (preload.mjs), update path joins here and ensure webPreferences.preload points to correct built script.

related_files.relationship: Main process will call these factory functions to create windows and wire lifecycle/menu/tray behavior
related_files.reason_to_check: If caller expectations change (e.g., new return semantics, need to hold references externally), adjust create* functions accordingly.

related_files.relationship: Renderer reads windowType query parameter and adapts which UI is rendered; these functions must keep query param contract
related_files.reason_to_check: Any change to query naming or expected windowType values must be mirrored by renderer code.
