Start the app in dev mode (VITE_DEV_SERVER_URL set) and verify each window type renders

insights.title: HUD overlay window height must match UI
insights.problem: The HUD window size (height/width/min/max) did not match new device selector UI and caused clipping or overflow of the selector panels.
insights.root_cause: UI changes to add device panels increased the required overlay height; the BrowserWindow bounds in createHudOverlayWindow were not updated to match resulting UI.
insights.solution: Increased windowWidth to 600 and windowHeight to 200 when device selector UI was added; later reduced height to 160 for updated UI. Kept min/max sizes consistent with new dimensions.

insights.title: Increase HUD overlay height for updated UI
insights.problem: Revamped HUD requires more vertical space.
insights.root_cause: HUD module added mic panel and extra controls; previous window size too small.
insights.solution: Change default and min/max heights from 100 to 155.
insights.lesson_learned: UI changes often require synchronized native window size updates; keep window factory in sync with renderer layout.

insights.title: Conditional object spread for platform-specific window options
insights.problem: Added isMac boolean and used ...(isMac && { titleBarStyle: 'hiddenInset', trafficLightPosition: ... }) pattern to apply Mac-only options (commit ebb1d29).
insights.root_cause: Desire to have macOS-specific traffic light placement and titleBarStyle set only on Mac.
insights.solution: Inserted conditional spread using isMac variable.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid using ...(condition && {...}) object spread pattern because spreading a boolean (false) into an object literal causes runtime errors on non-objects. Use ...(isMac ? {...} : {}) or build the options object conditionally to be safe across platforms.

insights.title: Keep hudOverlayWindow reference and adjust geometry
insights.problem: Needed to allow hide/minimize from renderer and better HUD positioning.
insights.root_cause: HUD window was created without persistent reference and had fixed small size anchored to bottom-right.
insights.solution: Store hudOverlayWindow in module scope, respond to ipc messages to minimize, change size and center-bottom positioning, and handle closed event to clear reference.
insights.lesson_learned: Windows that need remote control should be tracked in main process; position calculations should use display.workArea to support multiple screen setups.

vite.config.ts.short_description: Vite build configuration that wires React and Electron entry points and controls bundling/minification.
vite.config.ts.description:
This file is the primary Vite configuration for the project and exists to coordinate how the renderer (React) and Electron (main + preload) code are built. It composes plugins (React and vite-plugin-electron/simple), maps the Electron main and preload entrypoints, and controls production bundling behavior (minifier options, chunk splitting, target). The electron plugin configuration is central: it declares the Electron main entry (electron/main.ts) and the preload input (electron/preload.ts) so the build produces the separate artifacts (dist and dist-electron) the Electron app expects at runtime.

The build section is tuned for this app's runtime characteristics: target: 'esnext' (no transpilation down from modern JS), minification via terser with console statements removed and some functions treated as pure, and manualChunks to force certain third-party libraries into named bundles (pixi, react-vendor, video-processing). The configuration also contains a conditional around the renderer plugin to work around a known plugin issue when NODE_ENV === 'test' (the plugin is set to undefined in that case). The alias '@' -> src/ is set here to support source imports across the codebase and must remain consistent with TypeScript/IDE path mapping if present elsewhere.

When editing or adding build behavior, respect the explicit entrypoints for Electron (main/preload), the special-case for test environment, and the chunking/minifier choices that reflect runtime and debugging tradeoffs. Changes here directly affect produced artifacts that the Electron main process and tests rely on (dist-electron, preload bundles, renderer index), so any edit requires re-building and verifying the Electron runtime and browser-based tests (Playwright/Vitest) as appropriate.

key_constructs.name: defineConfig
key_constructs.purpose: Wraps and exports the Vite configuration object; standard Vite export helper.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the entry point Vite expects; modifications inside its returned object are the canonical Vite configuration used for dev and build. An agent editing configuration values should start here to understand overall structure.

key_constructs.name: electron
key_constructs.purpose: The vite-plugin-electron/simple plugin factory used to wire Electron main/preload builds into Vite.
key_constructs.reasoning: This plugin maps Electron-specific entrypoints and adjusts behavior for renderer/main/preload. Changing its options affects where the Electron build output is produced and how the preload script is bundled which the main process expects at runtime.

key_constructs.name: react
key_constructs.purpose: The @vitejs/plugin-react plugin instance to enable JSX/React support in Vite builds.
key_constructs.reasoning: This plugin applies transforms necessary for React source files. Removing or misconfiguring it will break renderer builds and hot-reload in dev.

key_constructs.name: manualChunks
key_constructs.purpose: Rollup output option object mapping module names to manual chunk groups.
key_constructs.reasoning: This controls code splitting for large vendor libraries (pixi.js, react/react-dom, video-processing libs). It is referenced by Rollup during production bundling and affects caching, chunk names, and bundle sizes; altering entries changes how third-party code is grouped.

key_behaviors: declares electron main entry for separate build output
declares preload input path used in preload bundle
configures React plugin for renderer transforms
applies terser minification and removes console/debug statements
forces manual chunking for large third-party libs
provides alias '@' -> src for module resolution

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or changing the electron plugin entries (main/preload) without updating consumers
pitfalls.consequence: Electron runtime will not find expected built artifacts (dist-electron or preload bundle), causing the app to fail at startup or tests that launch the built main to fail.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the entry paths consistent with electron/main.ts and electron/preload.ts and re-run full build + Electron startup tests after edits.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing NODE_ENV conditional handling for renderer to always enable the renderer option
pitfalls.consequence: Known plugin issue referenced in comment may reappear during test runs (test run failures/instability).
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the existing special-case when NODE_ENV === 'test' and validate tests when changing this logic.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering terserOptions (drop_console, pure_funcs) or removing them without verifying behavior
pitfalls.consequence: Console-side effects used for debugging or functional behavior could be removed, and production bundles may behave differently; unit/e2e tests that rely on console side effects/logs may change.
pitfalls.prevention: If modifying minifier options, run production build and the browser/e2e test suite to verify no regressions.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing manualChunks mapping or chunkSizeWarningLimit without verifying bundle size
pitfalls.consequence: Unexpectedly large chunks, worse caching, or exceeding Electron packaging expectations (and larger installers).
pitfalls.prevention: When modifying chunking, run a production build and inspect bundle outputs and sizes; verify startup performance and CI build steps.

resolve.alias: '@' path alias used throughout the codebase
build: target, minification (terserOptions), rollupOptions.manualChunks, and chunkSizeWarningLimit

minor plugin internals not configured here

src/components/video-editor/timeline/Tim.short_description: React timeline editor for video projects: renders rows (zoom/trim/annotation/speed), handles interactions, keyboard shortcuts and zoom suggestions
src/components/video-editor/timeline/Tim.description:
This file implements the timeline UI within the video editor. It composes a dnd-timeline-backed canvas and renders multiple rows of time-based regions (zoom, trim, annotation, and speed). The component is responsible for: mapping time <-> pixels, computing axis scales and grid, providing a draggable playhead that supports snapping to keyframes, adding/deleting/updating timeline regions with overlap and neighbor-aware clamping rules, handling a number of keyboard shortcuts (including cycling overlapping annotations with Tab/Shift+Tab), and exposing a Suggest action that runs telemetry analysis to provide candidate zoom regions. It integrates small helper components (Item, Row, TimelineWrapper, KeyframeMarkers) and utility functions (zoomSuggestionUtils) to implement behavior.

Why it exists: the editor needs a compact, interactive timeline to author and manipulate temporal regions over a recording. By centralizing rendering, interaction handling, keyboard shortcuts and temporal utilities in this component, the rest of the editor (playback, export, preview) can rely on a consistent timeline model and a single source of truth for region operations.

How it fits in the system: TimelineEditor is used by the VideoEditor UI. It receives props describing the current recording (videoDuration, currentTime, keyframes/cursor telemetry) and callback props to mutate domain regions (onZoomAdded, onTrimAdded, onAnnotationAdded, onSpeedAdded, and span-change/delete/select callbacks). It uses dnd-timeline's context (useTimelineContext) for value-to-pixel conversions and visible range state. It also uses app-level contexts such as ShortcutsContext and I18nContext. The component relies on a number of constants (min item duration, default duration calculation, axis scale candidates) and contains logic to adapt rendering density/durations across very different video lengths and zoom levels.

key_constructs.name: TimelineEditorProps
key_constructs.purpose: TypeScript interface declaring the props the TimelineEditor expects
key_constructs.reasoning: Defines the contract between the timeline and the parent editor: which callbacks and region lists must be provided, and which are optional. When changing interaction patterns or adding/removing region types, update this interface and callers accordingly.

key_constructs.name: SCALE_CANDIDATES
key_constructs.purpose: List of time interval/grid density candidates used to choose axis markers depending on visible range
key_constructs.reasoning: Axis density is determined from this canonical list. Any change to axis behavior should respect these candidates and their target marker computation (TARGET_MARKER_COUNT).

key_constructs.name: calculateAxisScale
key_constructs.purpose: Choose a meaningful interval and grid spacing for the timeline axis based on visible milliseconds
key_constructs.reasoning: This function is central to how major/minor tick spacing adapts on zoom/pan; changes affect marker density and label formatting downstream (formatTimeLabel).

key_constructs.name: calculateTimelineScale
key_constructs.purpose: Return minItemDurationMs, defaultItemDurationMs, and minVisibleRangeMs based on total video duration
key_constructs.reasoning: Provides conservative defaults for placing new regions and minimum zoom levels; modifications change default placement/precision throughout the timeline.

key_constructs.name: createInitialRange
key_constructs.purpose: Create the initial visible range for the timeline (falling back to a constant range when duration is unknown)
key_constructs.reasoning: Used on initialization to avoid degenerate ranges when duration is zero; keep behavior consistent to avoid rendering errors when videoDuration is not yet known.

key_constructs.name: clampVisibleRange
key_constructs.purpose: Clamp a candidate visible range to the total timeline duration and preserve span if possible
key_constructs.reasoning: Ensures zoom/pan operations never move the visible window outside the media duration. Important when programmatically changing ranges or when dragging the playhead off-edge and asking the timeline to recenter.

key_constructs.name: normalizeWheelDelta
key_constructs.purpose: Convert wheel event delta values from different deltaMode units to pixels using page size as reference
key_constructs.reasoning: Wheel delta units differ between browsers/OS/hardware; normalization preserves consistent zoom/pan sensitivity. Do not remove or change constants without confirming cross-platform behavior.

key_constructs.name: formatTimeLabel
key_constructs.purpose: Format a time value into a readable axis label depending on interval granularity
key_constructs.reasoning: Main used by the axis to display major marker labels. Label precision is based on intervalMs; changing this logic impacts visual layout and readability.

key_constructs.name: formatPlayheadTime
key_constructs.purpose: Format a time for the playhead tooltip (human readable, with tenths of seconds when short)
key_constructs.reasoning: Used in the draggable playhead preview; keep consistent with other time formatting logic so users see expected precision.

key_constructs.name: PlaybackCursor
key_constructs.purpose: React sub-component rendering the draggable playhead and implementing drag-to-seek with optional snapping to keyframes and auto-panning when dragging outside the timeline
key_constructs.reasoning: Encapsulates playhead-specific interactions and uses timeline context functions (valueToPixels/pixelsToValue) and the visible range to convert pointer movement into seeks or range shifts. It relies on keyboard/mouse event handling and should be kept in sync with timeline range/clamping logic.

key_constructs.name: TimelineAxis
key_constructs.purpose: React sub-component rendering the timeline top axis: major markers, minor ticks and labels
key_constructs.reasoning: Computes major and minor ticks using calculateAxisScale and formatTimeLabel. Changes here affect visual density, minor tick placement, and the set of labels shown.

key_constructs.name: TARGET_MARKER_COUNT
key_constructs.purpose: Target number of axis markers used by calculateAxisScale to pick candidate intervals
key_constructs.reasoning: Controls how aggressively the axis algorithm chooses marker spacing; altering it changes the user's perception of zoom levels and clutter.

key_constructs.name: ZOOM_ROW_ID
key_constructs.purpose: Row id string used to identify the zoom row in the timeline
key_constructs.reasoning: Identifiers are used when creating TimelineRenderItem objects and when deciding which set of regions to check for overlaps. When adding or renaming rows, update references across the file.

key_constructs.name: TRIM_ROW_ID
key_constructs.purpose: Row id string used to identify the trim row in the timeline
key_constructs.reasoning: Same reasoning as ZOOM_ROW_ID for trims.

key_constructs.name: ANNOTATION_ROW_ID
key_constructs.purpose: Row id string used to identify the annotation row in the timeline
key_constructs.reasoning: Used for mapping annotation regions and keyboard cycling logic.

key_constructs.name: SPEED_ROW_ID
key_constructs.purpose: Row id string used to identify the speed row in the timeline
key_constructs.reasoning: Added as part of the speed regions feature; overlap and placement must be handled per-row.

key_constructs.name: FALLBACK_RANGE_MS
key_constructs.purpose: Fallback visible range duration used when video duration is unknown
key_constructs.reasoning: Avoids zero-length ranges during initialization; altering it changes default zoom-in behavior for unknown-duration sessions.

key_constructs.name: handleSuggestZooms
key_constructs.purpose: Load and normalize cursor telemetry, detect dwell candidates, de-duplicate and space them, then call onZoomSuggested for each candidate
key_constructs.reasoning: Implements the telemetry-driven zoom suggestion algorithm described in commit insights. Editing this function must respect normalization, filtering thresholds, overlap checks and spacing constants (SUGGESTION_SPACING_MS). It communicates user feedback via toasts when no telemetry or no candidates are found.

key_constructs.name: matchesShortcut
key_constructs.purpose: Used to match keyboard events against the user-configured shortcut bindings
key_constructs.reasoning: Used throughout key handlers to respect configurable shortcuts instead of hard-coded key checks. When modifying keyboard handling, prefer matchesShortcut to preserve user configuration behavior.

key_behaviors: renders timeline axis and grid depending on visible range
adds/edits/deletes zoom, trim, annotation and speed regions
supports keyboard shortcuts for adding/deleting/cycling regions
suggests zoom regions using cursor telemetry analysis
drag-to-seek via draggable playhead with snapping to keyframes

pitfalls.mistake: Treating formatShortcut as synchronous
pitfalls.consequence: UI may attempt to use a string that must be awaited; causes incorrect shortcut badges or runtime promise objects in UI
pitfalls.prevention: Respect that formatShortcut is async and use effect hooks/state to await results (the component currently does this)

pitfalls.mistake: Applying overlap checks globally instead of per-row
pitfalls.consequence: New regions of one type could incorrectly be blocked by regions from another type (e.g., trim vs zoom), breaking expected placement behavior
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve per-row overlap logic and make sure hasOverlap checks the correct region set for the given variant/row id

pitfalls.mistake: Changing axis scale candidates or TARGET_MARKER_COUNT without testing wide ranges
pitfalls.consequence: Axis labels could become too dense or too sparse for very short or very long videos, affecting UX
pitfalls.prevention: If changing SCALE_CANDIDATES or TARGET_MARKER_COUNT, test videos spanning milliseconds to hours and observe rendered ticks

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or altering clampVisibleRange behavior
pitfalls.consequence: Visible range or dragging operations could produce ranges outside valid bounds resulting in rendering or calculation errors
pitfalls.prevention: Maintain clamping logic and test zoom/pan near 0 and near total duration

pitfalls.mistake: Modifying wheel delta normalization without cross-platform testing
pitfalls.consequence: Scroll/zoom sensitivity may feel broken across devices/browsers
pitfalls.prevention: Retain normalizeWheelDelta behavior or validate on devices that produce DOM_DELTA_LINE and DOM_DELTA_PAGE modes

insights.title: Cursor-telemetry driven zoom suggestion algorithm
insights.problem: Users need fast way to add zooms at cursor dwell moments in recordings.
insights.root_cause: No automated analysis of cursor dwell points existed.
insights.solution: Add handleSuggestZooms which loads normalized cursor samples, detects dwell runs (thresholds for min/max duration and move distance), computes average focus (cx,cy) and strength, filters out overlaps and enforces spacing, then calls onZoomSuggested to add zoom regions. Adds a Suggest button to UI.
insights.lesson_learned: Telemetry-driven suggestions require cleanliness: sample normalization, filtering for minimal samples, guarding against overlap with existing regions, and spacing constraints to avoid overcrowding UX. Provide user feedback (toasts) when no telemetry or no candidates found.

insights.title: Make single-letter shortcuts respect modifiers (speed 's' now configurable)
insights.problem: Previously speed shortcut handling was hard-coded and didn't respect configurable bindings.
insights.root_cause: Shortcuts configuration added addSpeed but timeline still used hard-coded key checks.
insights.solution: Use matchesShortcut(e, keyShortcuts.addSpeed, isMac) to detect speed shortcut; only use bare-letter handlers when no modifiers present.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding configurable shortcuts, replace hard-coded key checks with centralized matching logic to avoid divergence.

insights.title: Add speed row, keyboard shortcut and neighbor-safe region placement
insights.problem: Timeline lacked speed row and handling for speed region overlaps; keyboard shortcuts needed to work with user-configured bindings.
insights.root_cause: New speed region type required timeline rendering, overlap checking, and keyboard hooks.
insights.solution: Added SPEED_ROW, rendered speed items, added onSpeedAdded/onSpeedSpanChange/onSpeedDelete handlers, integrated matchesShortcut use for configurable shortcuts, added keyboard 'S' to add speed, and neighbor-clamping logic to allow clamping into neighbor gaps.
insights.lesson_learned: When extending timeline types, update render pipeline, overlap checks, keyboard bindings and ensure consistent clamping/placement behavior. Use refs to avoid effects re-firing too often.

insights.title: Use centralized ASPECT_RATIOS constant instead of inline arrays
insights.problem: UI used an inline casted array of aspect-ratio strings which could diverge from the type declarations and lead to runtime/compile-time inconsistencies.
insights.root_cause: Aspect ratio options were maintained locally inside the component rather than referencing a single source of truth.
insights.solution: Import ASPECT_RATIOS from aspectRatioUtils and iterate over that list for the dropdown menu.
insights.lesson_learned: Reference canonical constants from UI components to avoid drift between types and displayed options; keep UI options derived from types/constants where possible.

insights.title: UI toolbar extended with help component
insights.problem: Timeline toolbar lacked a contextual help trigger for trimming.
insights.root_cause: UX gap; no place to explain trimming semantics inline.
insights.solution: Inserted TutorialHelp component in toolbar (commit 175bb36).
insights.lesson_learned: Keep toolbar code modular so features like help, shortcuts, and settings can be inserted without large rewrites (use small separators, consistent flex layout).

insights.title: Timeline uses async keyboard shortcut formatting
insights.problem: platformUtils.formatShortcut was changed from sync -> async, requiring components to await results.
insights.root_cause: platform detection moved to an IPC-backed getPlatform and formatShortcut was refactored to call it (commit f34bd19).
insights.solution: TimelineEditor now uses useEffect to call formatShortcut(...) and stores values in state so UI renders the formatted shortcut once available.
insights.lesson_learned: Converting a widely-used utility from sync to async is a breaking change — you must update all callers to await the value or to handle promise resolution (use effects). Prefer adding a new async API rather than changing sync signature when many call sites expect sync strings.

insights.title: Draggable playhead and pixel↔time mapping for seeking
insights.problem: Playhead was not draggable; seeking relied on clicks only.
insights.root_cause: Timeline library used valueToPixels but didn't expose reverse mapping for drag operations.
insights.solution: PlaybackCursor uses pixelsToValue for dragging mapping; Timeline passes timelineRef into PlaybackCursor so drag mouse positions are converted to time and onSeek is invoked. Also clamps values and supports pointer outside timeline.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding drag interactions, ensure you have both forward (valueToPixels) and reverse (pixelsToValue) transforms and handle clamping and edge cases for pointer positions outside the element bounds.

insights.title: Cycle overlapping annotations using Tab (and Shift+Tab)
insights.problem: When multiple annotations overlap at the playhead, selecting one was awkward and required careful clicking.
insights.root_cause: No keyboard-driven cycling or deterministic ordering of overlapping annotations existed.
insights.solution: Added Tab/Shift+Tab handler that filters annotations active at current time, sorts by zIndex, and either selects first or cycles to next/previous depending on shift key. Also added click-cycling when clicking a selected annotation to move to next overlapping.
insights.lesson_learned: Provide keyboard shortcuts for cycling overlapping objects; base cycling order on zIndex for predictability. Prevent default Tab behavior in canvas/editor contexts while preserving input fields.

insights.title: Add aspect ratio dropdown in timeline header
insights.problem: Aspect ratio selection needed a more discoverable place near timeline controls.
insights.root_cause: Aspect ratio controls were only in SettingsPanel previously.
insights.solution: Inserted a DropdownMenu to select aspect ratio and show current label via getAspectRatioLabel.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep common export/preview controls near timeline area for faster iteration.

insights.title: Platform-aware shortcut display integration
insights.problem: Keyboard shortcut badges were hardcoded for macOS symbols.
insights.root_cause: Hardcoded shortcut strings did not adapt to Windows/Linux.
insights.solution: Use formatShortcut from utils/platformUtils to render OS-appropriate modifier names/symbols.
insights.lesson_learned: Centralize presentation logic for keyboard shortcuts to ensure cross-platform consistency.

insights.title: Timeline: add trim row and keybindings (T/Z/F)
insights.problem: Timeline needed support for two separate types of items (zoom and trim) and keyboard shortcuts to add/delete them.
insights.root_cause: The existing timeline assumed a single row of zoom items which made extending to trims awkward.
insights.solution: Added separate row IDs for zoom and trim, modified item model to include variant, introduced onTrimAdded/onTrimSpanChange/onTrimDelete callbacks, added keyboard handling for 'T' and 'Z', and unified item span change handler to call correct callback depending on item id.
insights.lesson_learned: When a timeline supports multiple item types, explicitly model rows and variants. Centralize key handling and item change logic, and be careful to prevent cross-type collisions (overlap checks per-row).

insights.title: Snap/overlap logic per item type and clamp trim ranges
insights.problem: New trims/zooms could overlap or be placed out-of-bounds, producing invalid spans.
insights.root_cause: Overlap checks only considered zoom regions; trim additions required separate overlap logic and clamping.
insights.solution: Modified hasOverlap to check against the appropriate region set (zoomRegions or trimRegions) and added clamping/normalization for trim start/end to safe min/max bounds and total duration.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding multiple item types to a timeline, overlap and snapping logic must be per-type. Use normalization/clamping to defend against invalid persisted values.

vitest.config.ts.short_description: Vitest configuration that sets test environment, file globs, and a resolve alias for the test runner.
vitest.config.ts.description:
This file exports the Vitest configuration for the repository using defineConfig from 'vitest/config'. It centralizes test-runner settings used by the project's unit and DOM-based tests. The configuration explicitly sets globals to true, selects the 'jsdom' environment (a change noted in the commit history to accommodate React hook tests that access navigator.mediaDevices), and defines the set of test file globs the runner will pick up (src/**/*.{test,spec}.{js,mjs,cjs,ts,mts,cts,jsx,tsx}).

In addition to test settings, this file configures the resolver alias '@' to point to the project's src directory using node:path.resolve. This alias is important for keeping import paths short and consistent across source code and tests; it must remain in sync with other resolvers (for example, Vite and TypeScript path mappings) to avoid module resolution discrepancies. The file is intentionally minimal: it contains an import of node:path for a cross-platform path resolution, then a single default export of defineConfig with two top-level options: test and resolve.

This configuration sits at the intersection between test authoring and module resolution. Tests that rely on DOM APIs (React component tests, hooks accessing window/navigator/mediaDevices, etc.) depend on the environment being jsdom, and many tests depend on the alias '@' to import project modules. Changes to this file directly affect which files are discovered as tests and how module paths are resolved during test runs.

key_constructs.name: defineConfig
key_constructs.purpose: Wraps and returns the Vitest configuration object with typings and validation for the test runner.
key_constructs.reasoning: This imported helper is used as the top-level export to provide a typed configuration to Vitest. When editing the configuration, preserve the defineConfig call so Vitest receives a properly structured config and tooling maintains type hints for the config properties.

key_behaviors: sets the test environment to jsdom for DOM APIs
enables global test helpers by setting globals: true
discovers test files using the specified include glob
creates a resolve alias '@' mapping to the src directory

pitfalls.mistake: Changing environment from 'jsdom' to 'node' or another environment without checking tests
pitfalls.consequence: DOM-based tests (React components, hooks using navigator.mediaDevices, window/document APIs) will fail or throw because those globals are not provided.
pitfalls.prevention: Run the project's test suite (vitest) after any environment change and verify tests that rely on browser APIs still pass. Note the commit that explicitly switched environment to 'jsdom' to support navigator.mediaDevices.

pitfalls.mistake: Modifying the include glob and inadvertently excluding supported test file extensions or test locations
pitfalls.consequence: Existing tests may no longer be picked up by Vitest, leading to silent test omissions in CI and local runs.
pitfalls.prevention: When changing include patterns, run npx vitest --run to confirm all intended tests are discovered; compare counts against CI runs.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing the alias '@' target or its resolution approach without updating Vite/TypeScript configs
pitfalls.consequence: Imports using '@/...' will resolve differently between dev/build/test environments, causing module resolution errors or type errors.
pitfalls.prevention: Ensure aliases remain in sync with vite.config.ts and tsconfig.json paths; verify both test and build runs after changes.

pitfalls.mistake: Using a relative path string instead of path.resolve with __dirname
pitfalls.consequence: Cross-platform path resolution issues (especially in Windows) or incorrect directory resolution in executors running from different CWDs.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the node:path.resolve(__dirname, 'src') pattern to produce an absolute path for the alias.

resolve.alias: shows alias mapping '@' -> src and how imports will be resolved under tests
skip_unless_needed: the import of node:path — trivial but keep because it ensures cross-platform resolution

vitest.browser.config.ts.short_description: Vitest configuration for running browser-mode tests with Playwright/Chromium and WebGL support.
vitest.browser.config.ts.description:
This file exports a Vitest configuration tailored for tests that must run inside a real browser environment (Chromium via Playwright). It exists because some test suites in this repository (notably those exercising the video/GIF export pipeline, WebGL/WASM-based libraries, and media decoding) require a true browser and GPU emulation to behave like a user environment. The defineConfig call sets up test discovery (src/**/*.browser.test.{ts,tsx}), a Playwright provider with specific launch args to enable SwiftShader software GL, headless Chromium instances, extended timeouts for slow export/codec operations, and an assetsInclude rule so test imports of .webm files work as URL assets.

The design choices in this config reflect CI and platform constraints: tests run headless (CI compatible), but Chromium is launched with --enable-unsafe-swiftshader and --use-gl=swiftshader so Pixi.js and other WebGL consumers run on CI machines that lack a GPU driver. The config also creates a module alias '@' resolved to src/ to match the codebase's import style in tests. The extended testTimeout and hookTimeout values recognize that media processing, WASM initialization, or Playwright startup can be slower than normal unit tests.

This file interops with other parts of the system in three specific ways: (1) tests matching the include glob will expect browser APIs and likely import assets (.webm) which assetsInclude allows; (2) the Playwright provider launch args must be consistent with expectations in exporter tests that rely on software GL/WebGL behavior; and (3) the alias must match other build/test configs (vite/tsconfig) to avoid import resolution mismatches. The commit history indicates this file was added specifically to enable real-browser export tests that previously could not be exercised in pure unit-mode Vitest runs.

key_constructs.name: defineConfig
key_constructs.purpose: Wraps and returns a Vitest configuration object; used as the export for Vitest to load.
key_constructs.reasoning: When an agent modifies the exported configuration object, it must keep this top-level defineConfig call and its shape; Vitest expects a configuration object returned here and altering the wrapper semantics may change how Vitest reads the file.

key_constructs.name: playwright
key_constructs.purpose: Factory from @vitest/browser-playwright providing a Playwright-based provider for Vitest browser mode.
key_constructs.reasoning: The playwright provider is the mechanism that spawns Chromium with custom launch options. Any edits to browser startup flags or provider configuration must be made through this symbol to preserve the Playwright integration used by browser-mode tests.

key_constructs.name: path
key_constructs.purpose: Node path module imported as node:path used to resolve the '@' alias to the repository's src directory.
key_constructs.reasoning: The alias resolution here must match other build/test configs. If path resolution changes, ensure the alias remains consistent with vite/tsconfig aliases to avoid broken imports in tests.

key_behaviors: runs browser-mode tests using Playwright/Chromium
launches Chromium with SwiftShader software GL for WebGL in headless CI
treats .webm files as importable assets
creates a module alias '@' pointing to src/

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or changing the --enable-unsafe-swiftshader / --use-gl=swiftshader args
pitfalls.consequence: WebGL-dependent tests (e.g., ones using Pixi.js or WASM that expect a GL context) may fail in headless CI environments without GPU drivers.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve or replace with an equivalent software GL strategy; validate GL-dependent tests in CI after any change.

pitfalls.mistake: Turning off headless or changing instances/browsers without updating CI expectations
pitfalls.consequence: Tests may behave differently locally vs CI or the CI job may fail if a non-headless setup requires a display or different browser binaries.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep headless:true for CI runs or update CI job setup and playwright install steps to match any browser changes.

pitfalls.mistake: Removing assetsInclude for '**/*.webm' or changing the pattern
pitfalls.consequence: Tests that import .webm assets (as URLs) will fail to resolve imports or treat them incorrectly, breaking media/export tests.
pitfalls.prevention: Maintain the assetsInclude entry or update tests and build config consistently when changing asset handling.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing the resolve.alias entry for '@' without synchronizing vite/tsconfig
pitfalls.consequence: Module resolution may break in tests, causing import errors that are not directly related to test logic.
pitfalls.prevention: Ensure alias changes are mirrored in vite.config.ts and tsconfig.json (paths) and run browser tests to validate.

pitfalls.mistake: Reducing testTimeout/hookTimeout values arbitrarily
pitfalls.consequence: Long-running media export or WASM initialization tests may become flaky/timeout in CI.
pitfalls.prevention: Retain or cautiously adjust timeouts and run the full browser test suite to verify stability.

test.testTimeout / hookTimeout: extended times for heavy media tests
resolve.alias: ensures '@' resolves to src/ for test imports
assetsInclude: makes .webm importable within tests

related_files.reason_to_check: If you change include patterns, provider args, headless mode, timeouts, or assets handling, re-run or update these tests.

insights.problem: Exporter behavior (GIF/MP4 generation) depends on real browser/WebGL; unit-mode tests couldn't exercise it.
insights.root_cause: Existing vitest config didn't enable browser mode with Playwright provider.
insights.solution: Added vitest.browser.config.ts enabling @vitest/browser-playwright with a chromium instance, headless, extra launch args for SwiftShader; included assetsInclude for .webm.

playwright.config.ts.short_description: Playwright test runner configuration for end-to-end tests
playwright.config.ts.description:
This file declares the Playwright Test configuration used by the project's end-to-end test suite. It exists so that the Playwright test runner picks up centralized settings (test directory, per-test timeout, retry policy, and reporter) that apply to all e2e tests under the repository. The single config object is created with defineConfig from @playwright/test so TypeScript-friendly validation and editor completions are available.

The configuration sets testDir to ./tests/e2e, increases the per-test timeout to 120_000 ms (with an inline comment explaining this is needed because GIF encoding is CPU-bound), disables retries (retries: 0), and sets the reporter to "list". These choices enforce a test runtime expectation (longer timeouts for heavy CPU tasks) and a deterministic retry policy; they affect CI and local developer runs of Playwright tests. The file is intentionally minimal and solely focused on runner-level options rather than test-level fixtures or project matrix settings.

key_constructs.name: defineConfig
key_constructs.purpose: Wraps and type-checks the Playwright configuration object for TypeScript-aware Playwright usage
key_constructs.reasoning: Using defineConfig yields an exported config that Playwright recognizes and provides TypeScript validation in-editor. An agent changing this file must respect that the defineConfig wrapper is the canonical factory for Playwright configs and that its argument structure maps directly to Playwright run-time options.

key_behaviors: points Playwright to the tests/e2e directory
sets a per-test timeout of 120000 ms
disables retries for tests
selects the reporter format as 'list'

pitfalls.mistake: Reducing the timeout value without accounting for CPU-bound work (e.g., GIF encoding)
pitfalls.consequence: E2E tests that perform heavy encoding or CPU work may time out and appear flaky or failing in CI
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve or carefully evaluate the timeout value; if changed, ensure heavy CPU-bound tests complete under the new limit

pitfalls.mistake: Changing testDir to a different path without updating test runner commands or CI
pitfalls.consequence: Playwright will not discover tests, causing CI job to pass with zero tests or to fail depending on CI settings
pitfalls.prevention: If relocating tests, update package.json scripts and CI workflow definitions that assume ./tests/e2e

pitfalls.mistake: Enabling retries globally (increasing retries) to mask intermittent failures
pitfalls.consequence: Flaky tests may hide real regressions and inflate test times in CI
pitfalls.prevention: Understand why a test is flaky before increasing retries; retries are a mitigation, not a fix

key_sections: testDir: indicates the folder Playwright will scan for test files
timeout: per-test timeout (ms) — increased for CPU-bound tasks (GIF encoding)
retries: global retry policy for flaky tests
reporter: controls output format used locally and in CI
skip_unless_needed: import line — trivial single import
wrapping mechanics — defineConfig is standard, no custom logic

src/components/video-editor/types.ts.short_description: Type definitions, defaults, and utility clamps for editor features: webcam, zoom, annotations, crop and playback.
src/components/video-editor/types.ts.description:
This file centralizes TypeScript types, default values, and small utility functions used by the video editor UI and related export/preview pipelines. It exists to provide a single source of truth for domain concepts used throughout the editor: webcam layout/size/positioning, zoom regions and focus, annotation regions and styles, crop regions, playback speed configuration, and small helper clamps. The shapes and defaults here are referenced by UI components (editor panels, overlays), exporter code and any serialization of editor projects.

Design-wise the module keeps thin POJO-style interfaces and literal unions for constrained enums (ZoomDepth, WebcamMaskShape, AnnotationType, ArrowDirection). Defaults are exported near their associated types so other modules can reliably initialize UI state and persist project files consistent with the editor. Utility functions (clampPlaybackSpeed, clampFocusToDepth, an internal clamp) encapsulate validation behavior and small nondestructive corrections (e.g., rounding playback speeds to 2 decimals, returning a midpoint when clamp receives NaN).

The file reflects recent API evolution visible in the commit insights: WebcamSizePreset was migrated from categorical labels to a numeric percentage (10–50) and the annotation model was extended to support figures and stacking (zIndex) while preserving a legacy content field. Because these types are consumed across the renderer and sometimes persisted to disk/project files, changes here have an API impact and must be coordinated with all call sites (serialization, editor UI, exporter, and any tests).

insights.title: WebcamSizePreset API changed (string enum -> numeric percent)
insights.problem: Two consecutive commits introduced webcam size presets: first as small/medium/large, then refactored to a numeric percent range (10–50).
insights.root_cause: Feature evolved: initial design used categorical presets, later replaced by percentage for finer control; both changes touched the same type.
insights.solution: Final change defines WebcamSizePreset as number and DEFAULT_WEBCAM_SIZE_PRESET = 25. Codebase updated to use numeric percent and clamp 10–50.
insights.Lesson Learned: API-level type changes are breaking; when migrating, update all call sites and tests and prefer a migration commit that includes adaptors or clear release notes.

insights.title: Extend annotation model to support figures and stacking
insights.problem: Annotation model lacked figure-specific data and z-index stacking control; content field was overloaded.
insights.root_cause: Early annotation model only handled simple text/image notes and didn't accommodate structured figure annotations.
insights.solution: Added AnnotationType 'figure', FigureType/ArrowDirection/ShapeType types, FigureData interface, per-type content fields (textContent, imageContent), zIndex field on AnnotationRegion, and DEFAULT_FIGURE_DATA.
insights.lesson_learned: Design models for extensibility: when supporting multiple content types, keep type-specific fields to avoid loss of data when switching types. Include stacking metadata (zIndex) for UI/editor operations.

src/lib/exporter/gifExporter.ts.short_description: Client-side GIF export pipeline: compute output size, stream-decode video(s), render frames and encode to GIF using gif.js workers.
src/lib/exporter/gifExporter.ts.description:
This module provides two related responsibilities: a utility for calculating GIF output dimensions (calculateOutputDimensions) and a GifExporter class that performs the end-to-end client-side GIF export. The exporter reuses the project's StreamingVideoDecoder to demux/decode frames without seeking, the FrameRenderer to composite video + webcam + annotations into a canvas, and gif.js (worker-based) to encode frames into a Blob. It supports timeline features (trimRegions, speedRegions), webcam compositing via a separate decoder and AsyncVideoFrameQueue, progress reporting, cancellation, and a capped worker count derived from navigator.hardwareConcurrency.

The file exists to provide parity of GIF output with the editor's preview and other export formats (MP4), so FrameRenderer receives the same configuration used by the editor (wallpaper, zoomRegions, cursor telemetry, webcam sizing presets, etc.). The design favors streaming (decodeAll) over per-frame seeking to improve performance and to correctly handle trimmed/speed-altered timelines. Resource lifecycle management is a core focus: the exporter offers cancel() and cleanup() to ensure decoders, frame queues, the renderer and gif.js state are destroyed or aborted, and VideoFrame objects are always closed in finally blocks.

Several non-obvious behaviors are important: calculateOutputDimensions rounds to even numbers and enforces a minimum of 2 in each dimension; the 'original' preset will fit within the source bounds while adopting a requested aspect ratio; gif.js repeat semantics are inverted (0 = infinite loop, 1 = no loop) and navigator.hardwareConcurrency is clamped into [1,8] worker count logic. The exporter also contains logging and explicit progress phases (normal frame progress and 'finalizing' with renderProgress). The code carefully coordinates webcam decode via an AsyncVideoFrameQueue and stopWebcamDecode flag and ensures queue.close/fail/destroy are invoked in all control flows (see commit history insights).

key_constructs.name: GIF_WORKER_URL
key_constructs.purpose: URL string pointing to gif.js worker script used to configure gif.js workerScript.
key_constructs.reasoning: Worker script URL must be kept correct for gif.js to spawn workers; packaging/build paths rely on import.meta.url resolution.

key_constructs.name: calculateOutputDimensions
key_constructs.purpose: Compute output width/height for GIF exports given source size, preset and an optional target aspect ratio.
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by UI/tests to determine export canvas size; enforces even dimensions and respects the 'original' preset semantics (fit within source bounds while adopting aspect ratio). Changes here affect visible output dimensions and tests.

key_constructs.name: GifExporter
key_constructs.purpose: Encapsulates GIF export lifecycle: initializes decoders and renderer, streams frames, adds frames to gif.js, reports progress, and supports cancellation and cleanup.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the primary export API used by the renderer/export UI. Any changes must respect decoding/queueing/cancellation contracts and maintain resource cleanup semantics to avoid leaks or deadlocks.

key_constructs.name: export
key_constructs.purpose: Async method that performs the entire export operation, returning an ExportResult with a Blob on success or error on failure.
key_constructs.reasoning: Contains the streaming decode loop and interacts with external modules (StreamingVideoDecoder, FrameRenderer, AsyncVideoFrameQueue, and gif.js). Edits here must maintain try/finally resource handling and the handshake with webcamFrameQueue.

key_constructs.name: cancel
key_constructs.purpose: Marks the exporter cancelled and attempts to abort active decoders and the gif.js encoder, then calls cleanup.
key_constructs.reasoning: Exposes cancellation to the UI/tray; must remain robust to avoid leaving decoders/queues/frames alive.

key_constructs.name: cleanup
key_constructs.purpose: Safely destroy/dereference streaming decoders, renderer and gif encoder references with guarded try/catch to avoid throwing during cleanup.
key_constructs.reasoning: Centralizes resource teardown used by both normal completion and cancellation/error paths; important to keep consistent error swallowing to avoid masking export errors while ensuring resources are freed.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing workerScript/worker URL resolution or packaging approach for GIF_WORKER_URL without updating build packaging.
pitfalls.consequence: gif.js won't be able to spawn workers at runtime causing encoding failures or falling back to main-thread encoding.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep import.meta.url resolution intact and verify built asset path; run the exporter in a dev/prod environment after edits.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering calculateOutputDimensions rounding logic (toEven) to allow odd sizes or values < 2.
pitfalls.consequence: Some downstream rendering or gif.js assumptions may break; tests expect even dimensions and a minimum size.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect even-dimension enforcement and minimum bound behavior present in current function.

pitfalls.mistake: Modifying streaming decode/queue interplay (webcamFrameQueue, stopWebcamDecode) without preserving the fail/close/destroy semantics.
pitfalls.consequence: Exports can deadlock waiting on webcam frames, leak VideoFrame objects, or leave consumers blocked in long-running exports.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep queue.close/fail calls and ensure webcamFrameQueue is destroyed in finally; preserve stopWebcamDecode semantics and ensure webcamDecoder.cancel() is invoked on cancellation.

pitfalls.mistake: Removing try/finally closures that always close VideoFrame objects.
pitfalls.consequence: VideoFrame leaks and memory pressure; potential exceptions thrown from frame close paths.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the finally block that closes videoFrame and webcamFrame regardless of success or errors.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing worker count determination to an unbounded or large value.
pitfalls.consequence: Could spawn too many workers causing resource exhaustion on low-end systems or degrade performance.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the existing clamp to at most 8 workers and at least 1, derived from navigator.hardwareConcurrency.

insights.title: GifExporter accepts webcamSizePreset and forwards to FrameRenderer
insights.problem: GifExporter needed to know webcam size to render frames matching editor preview.
insights.root_cause: Webcam size model change required exporters to propagate the new parameter.
insights.solution: Added webcamSizePreset to GifExporter config and included it in frameRenderer configuration.
insights.Lesson Learned: Keep exporter config aligned with editor state; adding new UI options requires exporter/API updates.

insights.title: Pass cursorTelemetry into GIF exporter for visual parity
insights.problem: GIF exports could diverge from playback if cursor-auto-follow behavior wasn't applied during rendering.
insights.root_cause: GIF exporter invoked FrameRenderer without cursorTelemetry.
insights.solution: Add cursorTelemetry to GifExporter config and pass it to FrameRenderer initialization.
insights.lesson_learned: Ensure feature parity between playback and all export formats by propagating the same runtime inputs through each exporter.

insights.title: Ensure exported frames are released and webcam decode can stop cleanly
insights.problem: GIF export could deadlock waiting on webcam frame queues or leak VideoFrame objects if an error occurred.
insights.root_cause: No final release of frames in all code paths; webcam decode queue consumer could be blocked if producer stopped without signaling.
insights.solution: Wrap frame processing in try/finally to always close frames, introduce stopWebcamDecode flag to prevent the webcam queue consumer from waiting indefinitely, destroy frame queues and cancel webcamDecoder in cleanup.

insights.title: Ensure webcam decode queues are always torn down
insights.problem: Export pipelines created auxiliary async queues for webcam frames but didn't reliably close/fail/destroy them on all code paths, leading to leaked frames, hanging consumers, or unclosed resources during failure paths.
insights.root_cause: webcamFrameQueue was declared locally in a nested block and closed only in a then() handler; exceptions could bypass the close, leaving queue consumers waiting or resources leaked.
insights.solution: Lift webcamFrameQueue to outer scope, track webcamDecodeError, use .catch to capture errors and .finally to either fail() or close(), and ensure destroy() is called in the export's finally block.
insights.lesson_learned: Any queued async producer/consumer structure must be cleaned up in all control flow paths (success/error/finally). Allocate resources in a scope that allows final cleanup and ensure destroy/close/ fail is called in finally.

insights.title: Adjust GIF encoder worker count to match hardware
insights.problem: GIF encoder previously used a fixed number (4) of web workers which could be suboptimal on low- or high-core machines.
insights.root_cause: Hard-coded worker count did not take host CPU capacity into account and could either under-utilize or overwhelm the system.
insights.solution: Use navigator.hardwareConcurrency (fallbacks) to compute WORKER_COUNT = clamp(cores - 1, 1, 8) and pass that to GIF worker config.
insights.lesson_learned: Avoid hard-coded concurrency; bound worker counts and respect navigator.hardwareConcurrency with sensible caps and fallbacks.

insights.title: GIF exporter coupled to streaming decoder API (speedRegions)
insights.problem: GifExporter calls streamingDecoder.getEffectiveDuration and decode callback with speedRegions — signature changed in streamingDecoder.
insights.root_cause: Adding speed/trim support in streamingDecoder required updates to callers; exporter and decoder are tightly coupled.
insights.solution: Propagate speedRegions from GifExporter into streamingDecoder.getEffectiveDuration and decoding call sites.
insights.lesson_learned: When adding timeline features (speed/trim) to the decoder, update all exporters — consider a small adapter layer or strongly-typed config object to avoid missed call sites.

insights.title: Migrate GIF exporter to streaming decoder and deliver frames without seeks
insights.problem: GIF exporter used per-frame seeking and an HTMLVideoElement which was slow and inaccurate for trimmed timelines.
insights.root_cause: Same as video exporter: seeking an HTMLVideoElement per frame is a poor model for efficient exporting of many frames.
insights.solution: Switch to StreamingVideoDecoder, use getEffectiveDuration from decoder, and stream frames into FrameRenderer and GIF worker.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep exporters consistent: use a single streaming decode approach for both GIF and MP4 to share demux/resample logic, and ensure resources are canceled/destroyed on abort.

insights.title: GifExporter implementation added (client-side gif.js encoding)
insights.problem: New feature to export edited video as GIF required frame extraction, transformations, and encoding with progress reporting and cancellation.
insights.root_cause: Lack of GIF export pipeline in the existing exporter set.
insights.solution: Added GifExporter class which reuses FrameRenderer and VideoDecoder to render frames, adds frames to gif.js encoder in a worker with progress callbacks, supports loop and size presets, and exposes export/cancel APIs.
insights.lesson_learned: Adding heavy client-side encoders requires careful attention to memory and progress reporting; provide cancellation and use worker-based encoders (gif.js) to avoid blocking UI. Reuse existing frame-rendering utilities to maintain parity with MP4 exports.

insights.title: Promise rejection parameter adjusted to avoid linter build error
insights.problem: A Promise created in gifExporter used a reject param that was never used, causing unused variable/lint issues that broke strict build or tsconfig settings.
insights.root_cause: Unused variable name _reject existed in Promise constructor.
insights.solution: Renamed the reject argument to _reject (or removed usage) to silence unused variable warnings or updated code to avoid referencing it.
insights.lesson_learned: Unreferenced promise rejection variables can cause build failures in strict TS setups; either use named _reject or handle rejection paths properly.

src/lib/exporter/gifExporter.test.ts.short_description: Unit tests for GIF output sizing: verifies calculateOutputDimensions behavior for presets and aspect ratios.
src/lib/exporter/gifExporter.test.ts.description:
This is a small Vitest unit test file that validates the calculateOutputDimensions utility exported from gifExporter.ts. The suite asserts two behaviors: that a scaled preset ("medium") will produce dimensions matching a supplied aspect ratio (16:9 in the test), and that the 'original' preset will fit the computed aspect ratio within the original source bounds while rounding to even dimensions. The tests import GIF_SIZE_PRESETS from types.ts so they remain aligned with the canonical preset definitions.

The file's purpose is regression protection for sizing logic; changes to GIF_SIZE_PRESETS, to calculateOutputDimensions, or to rounding semantics should be reflected here. Historically, the tests were updated when preset sets changed (commit insights indicate presets and FPS enums were adjusted), so the tests are relatively small but important to avoid drift between UI expectations and encoder dimensions.

src/components/video-editor/timeline/Ite.short_description: React timeline item component used by the video editor to render zoom/trim/speed/annotation items with drag/resize handles and a compact time label.
src/components/video-editor/timeline/Ite.description:
This file defines a single, reusable timeline Item component used in the video editor timeline. It exists to render a draggable/resizable item visual (the colored "glass" pill) with appropriate icons and labels depending on the variant (zoom | trim | speed | annotation). The component integrates with a drag-and-drop/timeline library via the useItem hook from "dnd-timeline", which supplies DOM refs, drag attributes/listeners, and computed inline styles (itemStyle, itemContentStyle). The Item is responsible for: attaching the node ref, applying the provided drag listeners/attributes, enforcing a minimum clickable width, rendering left/right end caps (resize affordances), showing the main icon+label for the variant, and showing a compact, memoized time label underneath the main content.

The component was designed to be compact in tight timeline views: a small MIN_ITEM_PX ensures items remain visually at near-true positions while still offering a tiny hit target for interaction; the comments explain the UX decision to keep that small so users must zoom to interact with sub-second items. The time label is memoized with useMemo to avoid recomputation on re-renders. Visual styling depends on a CSS module (ItemGlass.module.css) with several named classes for different variant colors and a selected state. The file also contains a ZOOM_LABELS map for zoom multiplier labels and a formatMs helper to render start/end times as human-readable minute:second or second.s formatting.

src/components/video-editor/videoPlaybac.short_description: Compute and apply PIXI layout for video + webcam overlay, cropping and masking.
src/components/video-editor/videoPlaybac.description:
This module centralizes the logic that sizes, positions and masks the main video content (and optional webcam overlay) inside a PIXI Application used by the video editor playback layer. It exists to encapsulate the math and PIXI calls that take a source video element, viewport container, optional crop region, webcam sizing/preset information and produce the PIXI sprite transform, mask shape and metadata needed by the rest of the playback UI. The function both computes values (scale, offsets, bounds) and mutates PIXI objects (sprite.scale/position and maskGraphics shapes) so the PIXI scene matches the expected composed layout.

The implementation delegates the high-level positioning of screen and webcam regions to computeCompositeLayout from src/lib/compositeLayout (imported here). That function returns screenRect, webcamRect and flags like screenCover which drive whether the video should be scaled to cover or fit. layoutVideoContent then computes the effective padding mapping to a scale multiplier, converts crop percentages into pixel coordinates, calculates the scale to apply (cover vs fit behavior), sets the PIXI sprite transform, and clears/draws a rounded-rectangle mask to clip the video to the visible screenRect. The function returns a LayoutResult describing stage size, cropped video size, base scale and offsets, mask rectangle, webcam rectangle and explicit crop bounds so other parts of the UI can use the same computed numbers.

This file is focused on rendering layout for the editor's playback canvas and is tightly coupled to PIXI objects (Application, Sprite, Graphics) and the composite layout abstraction, so edits must preserve the mutating contract (it resizes app.renderer, sets app.canvas CSS sizing, modifies sprite.scale/position, and redraws maskGraphics). It also handles edge cases: early returns when the video dimensions or container dimensions are not available, special-casing padding for the "vertical-stack" webcam layout, and disabling border radius when the composite layout indicates screenCover (to avoid rounded corners when scaling to cover).

key_constructs.name: LayoutParams
key_constructs.purpose: Type/interface describing inputs required to compute and apply the layout (container, pixi app, sprite, mask graphics, video element and optional cropping/webcam parameters).
key_constructs.reasoning: Provides a single aggregated input structure so callers can pass DOM + PIXI objects and layout options together; an agent must preserve field names and optionality when constructing or reading LayoutParams.

key_constructs.name: LayoutResult
key_constructs.purpose: Type/interface describing the computed layout values returned from layoutVideoContent (stage & video sizes, scale/offset, mask & webcam rects, crop bounds).
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the contract used by consumers to position UI overlays or compute export transforms. Editors must not change shape or meaning of the returned fields without updating all consumers.

key_constructs.name: layoutVideoContent
key_constructs.purpose: Main function that computes layout and applies transforms/masks to PIXI objects; returns computed layout or null on early-exit.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the primary entry point used by playback and editor code; changes to its signature, return values, or side effects (resizing renderer, mutating sprite/mask) will impact rendering and must be carefully coordinated with callers and tests.

key_behaviors: computes scale and offsets to fit or cover the cropped video area
applies PIXI sprite scale and position to display the cropped region
draws and fills a rounded-rectangle mask to clip video to the screen rect
returns a LayoutResult with precise bounds for overlays and export

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming videoElement.videoWidth/videoHeight are always non-zero.
pitfalls.consequence: The function will early-return null and no layout will be applied; consumers expecting a LayoutResult may crash or not render overlays.
pitfalls.prevention: Check for and handle null/undefined returns from layoutVideoContent; avoid calling before video metadata is loaded. Respect lockedVideoDimensions when provided.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing how padding maps to paddingScale (the magic factor 0.4 and percentage mapping).
pitfalls.consequence: Visual sizes will change nonlinearly; other code (e.g., computeCompositeLayout expectations) and UX will break because callers expect the current mapping.
pitfalls.prevention: If modifying padding behavior, update any calling code and tests that assume the current mapping. Preserve the vertical-stack override where padding is ignored.

pitfalls.mistake: Mutating or replacing maskGraphics without retaining API expectations (clear()/roundRect()/fill()).
pitfalls.consequence: Masking may no longer clip the video correctly, rounded corners might be lost or applied incorrectly, or PIXI might throw if methods differ.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep maskGraphics API usage consistent; if swapping to a different graphic implementation, ensure it provides equivalent drawing/clearing/filling behavior.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering scale computation logic for compositeLayout.screenCover vs fit without updating downstream consumers.
pitfalls.consequence: Crop centering and exported frames may be misaligned, because baseScale and baseOffset are used elsewhere to compute pixel coordinates.
pitfalls.prevention: When changing scaling behavior, also update other code (export, overlay positions) that rely on baseScale/baseOffset and run visual verification and automated tests.

pitfalls.mistake: Ignoring lockedVideoDimensions or treating it as always present.
pitfalls.consequence: Incorrect layout may be computed if a locked dimension is meant to override video element metadata; or early-return might be triggered unexpectedly.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect lockedVideoDimensions semantics: it overrides videoElement dimensions when provided; callers must set or unset it intentionally.

paddingScale calculation: maps percentage padding into usable scale factor
scale calculation: cover vs fit and how it uses cropped vs full video dimensions
PIXI mutations: app.renderer.resize, sprite.scale/position and maskGraphics drawing

early-return checks for width/height — straightforward guards

src/components/video-editor/KeyboardShor.short_description: React component that renders a hover-help popup showing keyboard shortcuts and a link to customize them
src/components/video-editor/KeyboardShor.description:
KeyboardShortcutsHelp is a presentational React component used in the video editor UI to show a compact, hover-activated tooltip listing both configurable and fixed keyboard shortcuts. It exists to give users a quick reference for action bindings and a direct way to open the shortcut configuration UI (openConfig). The component relies on ShortcutsContext for runtime shortcut bindings and platform info (isMac) and on i18n via useScopedT("shortcuts") to render localized labels. It also imports canonical shortcut data (FIXED_SHORTCUTS, SHORTCUT_ACTIONS) and a formatting helper (formatBinding) from lib/shortcuts to keep displayed bindings consistent across the app.

The UI is designed as a small help icon (HelpCircle). On hover it reveals a tooltip that contains: a localized title, a small button which triggers openConfig, a list of dynamic actions (SHORTCUT_ACTIONS) where each action label is looked up via i18n and the actual binding is rendered using formatBinding(shortcuts[action], isMac), and a second section listing FIXED_SHORTCUTS rendered from a central source of truth. The FIXED_SHORTCUTS entries are localized via the i18n key fixedActions.<i18nKey> with a fallback defaultValue of fixed.label. The component also includes platform-specific display adjustments for the fixed shortcuts (replacing Ctrl/Shift/Alt glyphs with Mac symbols when isMac is true). The visual behavior (visibility, opacity transitions, z-index) is implemented with utility CSS classes and tailwind-like classnames using group-hover to control tooltip visibility.

key_constructs.name: KeyboardShortcutsHelp
key_constructs.purpose: Exported React component that displays a tooltip listing keyboard shortcuts and a button to open shortcut configuration.
key_constructs.reasoning: When editing this component, preserve its reliance on ShortcutsContext (shortcuts, isMac, openConfig), the i18n scope (useScopedT("shortcuts")), and the use of canonical shortcut lists (SHORTCUT_ACTIONS, FIXED_SHORTCUTS). The component maps over those lists to render localized labels and platform-aware bindings; changes must keep the same binding between keys in the lists and translation keys.

shows localized labels for shortcut actions
opens shortcut configuration via openConfig

pitfalls.prevention: When editing markup or classes, verify hover behaviour and z-index remain consistent; confirm tooltip shows on hover and does not block other controls.

pitfalls.consequence: If a binding is undefined and formatBinding doesn't handle undefined, rendering may throw or show incorrect text.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep formatBinding able to accept undefined/null bindings or ensure the ShortcutsContext always provides keys for SHORTCUT_ACTIONS.

insights.lesson_learned: When a formatting utility becomes async, components must fetch the values and avoid calling async directly in render. Use placeholders or initial defaults to avoid layout shift.

src/components/video-editor/projectPersi.short_description: Normalize, validate and serialize editor project data and helper utilities for file URLs and id generation
src/components/video-editor/projectPersi.description:
This module centralizes the logic for interpreting, normalizing and serializing the video editor's on-disk project representation. It exists to provide a stable canonical shape for project data (EditorProjectData) in memory and on disk so the editor UI and persistence layers can rely on consistent fields despite legacy/partial inputs. The file contains conversion helpers for file paths <-> file:// URLs (cross-platform, with Windows drive and UNC handling), safe numeric clamping and validation helpers, schema version (PROJECT_VERSION) and wallpaper paths used by the editor UI.

Key responsibilities are: resolving project media from either the new media object or legacy videoPath, normalizing partial or user-provided editor state into a fully-populated ProjectEditorState (normalizeProjectEditor), producing a serialized project snapshot suitable for unsaved-changes diffs (createProjectSnapshot), validating incoming project blobs (validateProjectData) and a few small helpers such as deriveNextId and unsaved-change detection. The design favors defensive normalization: the editor accepts partial/legacy shapes and enforces ranges/defaults for numeric and enumerated fields. Several normalization decisions are non-obvious (e.g. legacy boolean motionBlurEnabled mapping to a motionBlurAmount, clamped webcam size, validated aspectRatio membership using ASPECT_RATIOS set), and these are intentional to preserve compatibility across project file versions and guard runtime consumers from malformed input.

key_constructs.name: WALLPAPER_PATHS
key_constructs.purpose: Array of wallpaper asset paths used as default wallpaper options in the editor UI
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the single source-of-truth for wallpaper file paths; code that displays wallpaper choices or defaults to a wallpaper should reference this array.

key_constructs.name: PROJECT_VERSION
key_constructs.purpose: Numeric version for the project on-disk schema
key_constructs.reasoning: Used when creating project files (createProjectData). Incrementing this indicates a breaking/intentional change to the on-disk format; other code that reads/writes project files or migration logic must respect this version.

key_constructs.name: toFileUrl
key_constructs.purpose: Convert a filesystem path into a file:// URL in a cross-platform way (handles Windows drive and UNC paths)
key_constructs.reasoning: Paths used inside project data may be persisted as file URLs. The function encodes path segments safely and preserves Windows drive letters (optionally). Consumers should use this to produce portable file:// URIs.

key_constructs.name: fromFileUrl
key_constructs.purpose: Convert a file:// URL back to a platform path string, preserving Windows drive and UNC semantics
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the inverse of toFileUrl and must be used to interpret file URLs found in loaded project data. It includes robust fallback logic for malformed URLs and percent-decoding errors.

key_constructs.name: deriveNextId
key_constructs.purpose: Generate the next numeric id using an existing set of prefixed ids (prefix-N)
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by editor code that needs to pick unique incremental ids for regions/elements; it only inspects existing id strings and returns the next integer, ensuring no accidental collisions with non-matching ids.

key_constructs.name: validateProjectData
key_constructs.purpose: Quick structural validation that a deserialized object is a usable EditorProjectData
key_constructs.reasoning: A shallow guard used before attempting to open a project: it verifies version is a number, that media can be resolved and editor is present and an object. Callers should still rely on normalizeProjectEditor for full normalization.

key_constructs.name: resolveProjectMedia
key_constructs.purpose: Resolve and normalize the project's media information, accepting both the new media object and the legacy videoPath string
key_constructs.reasoning: This function provides compatibility between schema versions by delegating normalization to normalizeProjectMedia (from recordingSession) and by accepting legacy videoPath entries that older projects may still have.

key_constructs.name: normalizeProjectEditor
key_constructs.purpose: Normalize a potentially-partial ProjectEditorState into a full, validated ProjectEditorState with safe defaults and clamped numeric fields
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the critical transformation that ensures the editor has consistent data to render and manipulate. It enforces ranges for crop/zoom/padding/border/motion blur, validates enumerated values (aspect ratios, webcam presets, gif options), normalizes region lists (zoom, trim, speed, annotation) and maps legacy fields (e.g. motionBlurEnabled boolean to motionBlurAmount numeric). All serialization and unsaved-change logic depends on its deterministic output.

key_constructs.name: createProjectSnapshot
key_constructs.purpose: Serialize project data to a normalized JSON string for saving or unsaved-change detection
key_constructs.reasoning: Always calls normalizeProjectEditor before serializing (signature accepts Partial<ProjectEditorState>) so snapshots are stable and comparable. This stability is relied upon by hasProjectUnsavedChanges to detect user edits.

key_constructs.name: hasProjectUnsavedChanges
key_constructs.purpose: Compare two JSON snapshots (current and baseline) to determine if the project has unsaved changes
key_constructs.reasoning: A simple string comparison of normalized snapshots; because createProjectSnapshot always normalizes, this comparison is robust, but callers must ensure both snapshots were generated the same way.

key_behaviors: normalize editor state from partial/legacy inputs
serialize normalized project snapshot for saving and diffing
resolve media paths from new and legacy formats
convert between file paths and file:// URLs
derive incremental ids from existing prefixed ids

pitfalls.mistake: Assume project files always contain media.media.screenVideoPath or only the new media object
pitfalls.consequence: Older projects that contain a legacy videoPath would fail to be recognized as containing media if resolveProjectMedia isn't used; validation/normalization may produce null media unexpectedly.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect resolveProjectMedia's logic — it explicitly accepts candidate.videoPath as a legacy fallback.

pitfalls.mistake: Modifying the shape or ordering of normalizeProjectEditor output without updating createProjectSnapshot usage
pitfalls.consequence: Snapshots would change format and hasProjectUnsavedChanges comparisons could flip unexpectedly, causing UI to show unsaved changes erroneously or miss them.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep normalizeProjectEditor deterministic and ensure createProjectSnapshot continues to call it before serializing; any intentional schema change should update PROJECT_VERSION and associated tests.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering toFileUrl/fromFileUrl encoding semantics (especially Windows drive and UNC handling)
pitfalls.consequence: Saved project file paths may become non-portable or loading older projects may produce incorrect local paths. Percent-encoding/decoding errors can also produce invalid paths.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the existing encoding rules: keepWindowsDrive handling, special UNC handling (host + pathParts), and robust fallback in fromFileUrl that tolerates decodeURIComponent failures.

pitfalls.mistake: Using createProjectSnapshot with already-normalized editor state under the old function signature assumption
pitfalls.consequence: Duplicate or inconsistent normalization could be performed, or tests relying on snapshot stability could break if callers stop passing Partial types.
pitfalls.prevention: Use createProjectSnapshot as defined (accepts Partial<ProjectEditorState>) and rely on it to perform normalization prior to serialization.

pitfalls.mistake: Not clamping numeric values (e.g. playback speed, crop region) or trusting user-provided values
pitfalls.consequence: Downstream code may receive out-of-range values leading to rendering errors or export failures.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the clamping and allowed-value checks implemented in normalizeProjectEditor (e.g. clamp ranges, valid enums and lists).

key_sections: normalizeProjectEditor: main normalization logic and defaults (critical for understanding saved snapshot shape)
resolveProjectMedia: compatibility with legacy projects and linkage to recordingSession.normalizeProjectMedia
toFileUrl / fromFileUrl: platform-specific path encoding/decoding edge cases
createProjectSnapshot & hasProjectUnsavedChanges: how snapshots are generated and compared
skip_unless_needed: isFiniteNumber / clamp helpers (small utilities)
WALLPAPER_PATHS generation (static asset list generation)

creates version 2 projects with explicit media

insights.title: Normalize editor state before snapshot/serialization
insights.problem: createProjectSnapshot used ProjectEditorState in signature and passed raw editor to createProjectData causing type/validation issues; unsaved changes detection was fragile.
insights.root_cause: Serialization was performed without normalizing optional/partial editor fields leading to inconsistent snapshots.
insights.solution: Changed createProjectSnapshot to accept Partial<ProjectEditorState> and call normalizeProjectEditor(editor) before createProjectData to ensure consistent serialized snapshots.
insights.Lesson Learned: Normalize and validate optional editor state before serializing to keep snapshots stable for change detection.

insights.title: Project version bump and media object schema
