src/main.tsx.short_description: Renderer app bootstrap: mounts the React App into the DOM and provides i18n context
src/main.tsx.description:
This file is the single-entry client bootstrap for the renderer (React) side of the Electron app. Its purpose is to import global CSS and mount the top-level React component tree into the DOM element with id "root". It exists so the renderer process has a minimal, predictable place to start the React app, wrap the app in cross-cutting providers, and enable React StrictMode during development.

Design-wise it keeps the bootstrap minimal: a CSS import for global styles (index.css), a provider wrapper (I18nProvider) that supplies translation/localization context to the entire app, and the App component (the application's primary UI). It uses ReactDOM.createRoot(...).render(...) and React.StrictMode to mount the app, and it uses a non-null assertion on document.getElementById("root") to assert the DOM structure expected by the Vite/Electron renderer. This file therefore tightly couples to the DOM structure produced by the app's HTML template and to the I18nContext contract.

key_constructs.name: ReactDOM
key_constructs.purpose: Holds React DOM rendering APIs used to create the root and render the React tree.
key_constructs.reasoning: Any changes to how the app is mounted (hydration, SSR, root id) will interact with ReactDOM. Keeping createRoot usage consistent is important for React 18 rendering semantics.

key_constructs.name: createRoot
key_constructs.purpose: The React 18 API used to create a concurrent root for rendering the app into a DOM node.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the actual call that attaches React to the DOM; altering it (for example to hydrate) changes lifecycle and rendering behavior and must be done deliberately.

key_constructs.name: I18nProvider
key_constructs.purpose: Context provider component imported from contexts/I18nContext that supplies i18n/localization to the app.
key_constructs.reasoning: The provider order matters: components inside App will expect translations and locale state from this provider. Removing or reordering it affects localization runtime behavior across the renderer.

key_constructs.name: App
key_constructs.purpose: Top-level React component representing the application's UI.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the principal UI composition point. Any change in how the app is mounted (wrapping providers, StrictMode) will affect App and all its children.

key_behaviors: mounts the React application into the DOM root element
wraps the App with the I18nProvider so translations/locales are available
applies global CSS from index.css
enables React.StrictMode for development-time checks

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or changing the non-null assertion on document.getElementById("root") without ensuring the HTML contains the expected element
pitfalls.consequence: If the DOM root is missing at runtime the app will throw at startup and fail to mount.
pitfalls.prevention:
Ensure the app HTML template includes
or adjust this bootstrap to handle absent element gracefully and update all consumers.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering or removing React.StrictMode in development without recognizing its effects
pitfalls.consequence: React.StrictMode doubles-invokes some lifecycle/effect code in development. Changing it will change dev-time behavior and may mask effects-related bugs.
pitfalls.prevention: If removing StrictMode, run the existing test/dev flows to verify no hidden side-effect assumptions relied on the double-invocation behavior.

pitfalls.mistake: Reordering or removing I18nProvider relative to App
pitfalls.consequence: Components inside App that depend on i18n context will break (undefined translations or runtime errors).
pitfalls.prevention: Keep provider wrapping intact or update dependent components and tests accordingly when changing provider placement.

pitfalls.mistake: Moving index.css import or changing global CSS handling without checking cascade/order
pitfalls.consequence: Global styles may change unexpectedly across the app, causing UI regressions.
pitfalls.prevention: When adjusting CSS imports run the renderer dev server and visually verify major screens (launch, editor) for regressions.

key_sections: index.css import: establishes global stylesheet ordering
I18nProvider: ensures locale/translation context for all descendants
App: the top-level UI component to which the provider applies
skip_unless_needed: the import lines (boilerplate) if you only need to modify provider or mount behavior

related_files.relationship: App is the top-level UI component mounted by this bootstrap file; changes to mounting or providers here affect App and its children.
related_files.reason_to_check: If you change provider order, StrictMode, or root mounting behavior, verify App's expectations (contexts, CSS selectors).

related_files.relationship: Defines I18nProvider used in this file; provides translations and locale management.
related_files.reason_to_check: If provider API or contract changes, update this bootstrap to provide required props or rewrap appropriately.

related_files.relationship: Global CSS imported by this file; affects base styling across the renderer.
related_files.reason_to_check: If CSS variables or resets are moved/renamed, verify global styles and component appearances after edits.

related_files.relationship: Contains the <div id="root"> that this file mounts into (Vite/Electron dev/prod HTML template).
related_files.reason_to_check: If root id changes or the HTML template is altered, update this file to match the new mount point.

src/components/video-editor/ExportDialog.short_description: React component that displays export progress, errors, and success for MP4/GIF exports
src/components/video-editor/ExportDialog.description:
ExportDialog.tsx is a UI component used by the video editor to surface the state of an export operation to the user. It accepts a rich set of props describing the current export (ExportProgress, isExporting, exportFormat, error, exportedFilePath, etc.) and renders multiple states: active exporting with progress, a multi-phase compiling state (special handling for GIF compilation), error display, and a success state that briefly shows a confirmation and auto-closes the dialog. The component encapsulates UX behavior around resetting transient success state, timing an auto-close when the export completes, and offering a "Show in Folder" action when an exported file path is available.

This file exists to isolate all export-related modal UI and logic (including small decision helpers and side effects) in one place, so the rest of the editor can drive it via props. The component is intentionally format-aware (mp4 vs gif) because GIF exports can be multi-phase (render frames, then compile) and provide additional meta like renderProgress; the component maps those phases to different messages, gauges, and visuals. The component relies on the ExportProgress type from the exporter layer and expects that exporters will provide a percentage, optional renderProgress, and a phase string (e.g., "finalizing").

Design decisions visible in the file: (1) showSuccess is a local transient UI state with explicit resets triggered by useEffect hooks when an export starts or the dialog re-opens; (2) multi-phase handling (isCompiling/isFinalizing) to present different progress metrics and animations; (3) the file assumes that the consumer will provide an onShowInFolder handler for platform-specific 'reveal in folder' behavior and just calls it when the button is clicked. The component is pure presentation + small UI lifecycle concerns; it does not perform export work itself but must be kept in sync with the exporter contract (phases and progress fields).

key_constructs.purpose: TypeScript interface defining the component's props: state flags, progress, error, callbacks and optional exported file info
key_constructs.reasoning: All callers must conform to this shape; changes to these fields affect how the dialog displays and which actions are enabled (e.g., presence of exportedFilePath shows 'Show in Folder').

key_constructs.name: ExportDialog
key_constructs.purpose: Default exported React functional component that renders the export modal and its states
key_constructs.reasoning: Primary UI entry point. The agent should preserve its prop-driven behavior and side effects (success timer, resets) when modifying or moving logic.

key_constructs.name: getStatusMessage
key_constructs.purpose: Internal helper returning the localized status message string based on current phase/error/format
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to centralize messaging for the different export phases. It depends on renderProgress, isCompiling/isFinalizing and error presence.

key_constructs.name: getTitle
key_constructs.purpose: Internal helper returning title text for the dialog based on phase/format/error
key_constructs.reasoning: Encapsulates title selection logic so UI markup remains declarative; changes here affect the dialog headline across all states.

key_behaviors: renders export progress and progress bar visuals
displays multi-phase status (rendering vs compiling vs finalizing)
displays error panel when export fails
shows success confirmation and auto-closes after completion
exposes a "Show in Folder" action when exportedFilePath is provided
allows user-initiated cancel via onCancel callback when provided

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming exported file paths use POSIX separators and splitting on '/'
pitfalls.consequence: On Windows paths with backslashes, filename extraction will fail or return the whole path string; UI may display an incorrect name
pitfalls.prevention: Respect that filename extraction is doing a platform-sensitive operation; preserve exportedFilePath and use platform-aware logic in the consumer or pass a basename string rather than relying on split('/') in the component

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or changing the showSuccess reset effects or the auto-close timer logic without keeping lifecycle invariants
pitfalls.consequence: showSuccess may persist incorrectly across exports or the dialog may not auto-close after successful export, causing confusing UX
pitfalls.prevention: When editing the useEffect hooks that set/reset showSuccess and that start the auto-close timer, ensure the same dependencies (isExporting, isOpen, progress, error, onClose) are respected and timers are cleaned up on unmount

pitfalls.mistake: Altering callback props (onClose, onShowInFolder, onCancel) to be optional/unstable without preserving identity guarantees
pitfalls.consequence: The useEffect hook that depends on onClose may capture a stale reference or cause unexpected behavior when the timer calls onClose; cancel logic may not run if handlers are changed mid-export
pitfalls.prevention: Treat these callbacks as externally-managed; if replacing them, ensure stable references or update dependency arrays accordingly

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming progress fields (percentage, renderProgress, phase) are always present or within expected ranges
pitfalls.consequence: UI could render NaN or negative widths, or show misleading percentages (progress > 100) which could break layout or mislead users
pitfalls.prevention: Respect that progress.* fields are optional and guard usage (the component already guards some cases); ensure exporter upstream continues to provide the documented contract

key_sections: ExportDialogProps: understand which props the component expects and which callbacks must be supplied
useEffect hooks near the top: logic that resets showSuccess and handles the success auto-close timer (important lifecycle behavior)
getStatusMessage and getTitle: central decision points mapping exporter state to user-facing text
JSX render branches: showSuccess vs isExporting vs error — this is how UI states map to props
skip_unless_needed: Inline CSS <style> block defining @keyframes indeterminate (visual-only animation detail)
Small presentational classes and markup details unless touch-up is required

related_files.reason_to_check: If exporter progress shape (percentage, renderProgress, phase, currentFrame, totalFrames) changes, this component's conditional logic must stay in sync

related_files.relationship: Parent/editor drives export state and mounts ExportDialog; coordinates starting/stopping exports and supplies callbacks (onCancel/onShowInFolder/onClose)
related_files.reason_to_check: Changes in how the editor invokes reveal-in-folder, or how it passes exportedFilePath, should be validated here

related_files.relationship: Preload/contextBridge exposes platform APIs (e.g., revealInFolder) that onShowInFolder will call; component relies on the consumer to wire platform reveal actions correctly
related_files.reason_to_check: If the revealInFolder IPC changes signature or behavior, ensure the consumer handles errors and that the dialog continues to show exportedFilePath until user interacts

insights.title: Add 'Show in Folder' button and toast action using reveal-in-folder IPC
insights.problem: After export users wanted a quick way to reveal the exported file; earlier code reset path too early.
insights.root_cause: No IPC for revealing file and exported path wasn't reliably preserved for dialog action.
insights.solution: Added exportedFilePath prop, Show in Folder button, and handler that calls window.electronAPI.revealInFolder with error handling and toast notifications.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep exported path available to UI until dialog closed; calls to platform APIs should surface any errors to users.

insights.title: Export dialog updated to support GIF-specific progress and compiling phase
insights.problem: GIF exports have a multi-phase process (render frames then compile via gif.js) and the old export UI only supported a single percentage-progress model used for MP4.
insights.root_cause: Different exporters produce progress info differently (frame-based vs compile-phase). ExportDialog needed to surface both types of progress and the final compiling step.
insights.solution: Add exportFormat prop, detect isCompiling/isFinalizing, show renderProgress if present, show different progress bar visuals and messages for 'Compiling GIF', include format label in messages and adapt layout (two-column grid showing format and frames). Also reset showSuccess on new exports and when re-opening dialog.
insights.lesson_learned: Exporter implementations must define a consistent progress contract (phases and optional renderProgress) to let UI show meaningful state for different formats. Export UI should handle multi-phase exports and be resilient to missing progress fields.

src/lib/exporter/streamingDecoder.ts.short_description: Stream-decoding video files via web-demuxer + WebCodecs and resampling VFR→CFR for export.
src/lib/exporter/streamingDecoder.ts.description:
This module implements a forward-pass, streaming video decode pipeline that uses the WebDemuxer WASM demuxer and the WebCodecs VideoDecoder. It exists to extract high-quality, frame-accurate VideoFrame objects for the exporter pipeline (video/gif muxers) without repeatedly seeking an HTMLVideoElement. The streaming approach minimizes memory usage by holding only a single decoded frame and emitting clones at target timestamps (CFR), while still decoding trimmed regions to keep codec state intact for P/B frames.

Key design decisions: (1) Use web-demuxer to produce chunks to feed directly to VideoDecoder so decoding is fast and deterministic; (2) Accept both local (file:// / filesystem) and remote sources — when running in Electron, local reads use window.electronAPI.readBinaryFile to avoid fetch/file:// issues; (3) Detect and normalize AV1 codec descriptions (buildAV1CodecString) because web-demuxer can return a bare "av01" which WebCodecs cannot accept; (4) Perform streaming resampling from variable frame rate (VFR) source frames to constant target frame rate (CFR) output using a single held frame and a midpoint handoff rule to choose which decoded frame to clone. The module also includes robust timeout guards (withTimeout wrapper used internally) around source loading and demuxer operations to avoid indefinite hangs.

How it fits: other exporter modules (videoExporter.ts, gifExporter.ts, muxer and audio pipeline) use this decoder to obtain per-frame VideoFrame payloads and metadata such as frame rate, dimensions, codec, duration, and whether audio exists. The decoder exposes metadata via loadMetadata and performs the heavy lifting in decodeAll. It is cancelable and performs explicit cleanup (closing VideoFrames, closing VideoDecoder, canceling demuxer reader). The code contains many pragmatic guards for real-world container/codec edge cases (truncated containers, AV1 quirks, demuxer streamDuration vs mediaInfo.duration, backpressure thresholds, and tolerances for perceived early decode end).

key_constructs.name: SOURCE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS
key_constructs.purpose: Timeout (ms) used around source file read, fetch, demuxer load, and metadata read operations.
key_constructs.reasoning: When editing code that calls or changes I/O behavior, respect this constant as it prevents indefinite hangs; changing it affects user-visible timeouts and test timing.

key_constructs.name: buildAV1CodecString
key_constructs.purpose: Construct a WebCodecs-compatible AV1 codec string from an AV1CodecConfigurationRecord BufferSource or return a safe fallback.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function normalizes AV1 codec descriptions returned by web-demuxer (which can be bare 'av01') into a fully parameterized string required by WebCodecs; maintain correct byte-view handling for BufferSource inputs.

key_constructs.name: DecodedVideoInfo
key_constructs.purpose: Type alias/interface describing decoded video metadata (width, height, duration, frameRate, codec, audio presence).
key_constructs.reasoning: This data structure is the authoritative metadata the decoder exposes to the rest of the export pipeline; changes will affect consumers that rely on duration, streamDuration, and hasAudio.

key_constructs.name: shouldFailDecodeEndedEarly
key_constructs.purpose: Decides whether an apparently premature end-of-decode should be treated as an error based on last decoded frame, required end, and streamDuration.
key_constructs.reasoning: This encapsulates heuristics that distinguish benign metadata tails from real truncation; callers use it to decide whether to throw when decode finished before required end.

key_constructs.name: OnFrameCallback
key_constructs.purpose: Type alias for the async callback invoked per output frame: (frame, exportTimestampUs, sourceTimestampMs) => Promise<void>.
key_constructs.reasoning: The decodeAll streaming loop calls this for every emitted (cloned) VideoFrame; implementers must close frames and respect async behavior and backpressure.

key_constructs.name: StreamingVideoDecoder
key_constructs.purpose: Main class that handles loading source bytes, creating a WebDemuxer, extracting media info, and streaming decoded frames via VideoDecoder with VFR→CFR resampling.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the primary public API used by exporter modules to get frames and metadata. It owns lifecycle (demuxer, decoder), exposes loadMetadata and decodeAll, and implements cancellation and cleanup. Edits must preserve resource management, backpressure, AV1/codec normalization, and timeout behavior.

key_constructs.name: loadSourceFile
key_constructs.purpose: Private helper (method) that loads the source from a URL or local path, returning { file, blob } and preferring electronAPI.readBinaryFile for non-remote URLs.
key_constructs.reasoning: This method handles both remote fetch and local file reads via preload — changing it affects how packaged Electron apps operate and must respect electronAPI presence and failure modes.

key_constructs.name: loadMetadata
key_constructs.purpose: Creates a WebDemuxer instance, loads the file, and returns DecodedVideoInfo (width, height, duration, frameRate, codec, hasAudio, streamDuration).
key_constructs.reasoning: This method primes the demuxer and sets this.metadata; it also computes frame rate from avg_frame_rate and ensures streamDuration is normalized. Other components depend on metadata fields.

key_constructs.name: decodeAll
key_constructs.purpose: Streams demuxed chunks into a VideoDecoder, resamples VFR to the target frame rate across trim & speed regions, and calls the provided onFrame callback with cloned VideoFrames.
key_constructs.reasoning: This method implements the forward-decoding algorithm with backpressure, held-frame logic, mid-point handoff, segment output frame counting, reader cancellation, decoder.configure fallback behavior, and final cleanup. Any edits must preserve cloning/closing semantics and cancellation invariants.

key_behaviors: loads video source bytes from remote or local paths
extracts media metadata via web-demuxer
streams demuxed chunks into WebCodecs VideoDecoder
resamples variable framerate source to constant target framerate
emits per-frame callbacks with cloned VideoFrames and timestamps
handles cancellation and cleans up decoder/demuxer resources

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming web-demuxer returns a WebCodecs-ready codec string for AV1 (e.g., 'av01' is sufficient).
pitfalls.consequence: VideoDecoder.configure will fail or produce decoder errors for AV1 content; exports will fail for AV1 sources.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve buildAV1CodecString normalization when decoderConfig.codec is a bare 'av01' and maintain correct BufferSource byte view handling.

pitfalls.mistake: Reading BufferSource extradata naively using .buffer without respecting byteOffset/byteLength.
pitfalls.consequence: Parsing wrong bytes leads to incorrect AV1 codec string synthesis and potential decode failures.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the view-aware Uint8Array creation (handling ArrayBuffer vs ArrayBufferView) as implemented.

pitfalls.mistake: Removing or weakening timeouts (SOURCE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS / withTimeout) around IO and demuxer calls.
pitfalls.consequence: Long-running or hung fetch/demuxer operations can stall exports and block the UI; CI/browser tests may timeout unpredictably.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep or adjust timeouts carefully and ensure tests account for them.

pitfalls.mistake: Closing or destroying the decoder/demuxer improperly (e.g., failing to close VideoFrames or not handling demuxer.destroy exceptions).
pitfalls.consequence: Resource leaks and inconsistent memory usage; potential errors in subsequent exports or tests.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve the explicit close/cleanup and the intentional catch { /* ignore */ } semantics around demuxer.destroy/reader.cancel and always close VideoFrame objects handed off.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing backpressure thresholds or holding strategy without coordinating decodeQueueSize and pendingFrames logic.
pitfalls.consequence: Can cause unbounded memory growth, stalls, or incorrect frame sequencing during VFR→CFR resampling.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect existing decodeQueueSize and pendingFrames thresholds and the held-frame mid-point handoff approach implemented in decodeAll.

key_sections: buildAV1CodecString: normalizes AV1 codec strings for WebCodecs — important for AV1 sources
loadSourceFile: shows how local vs remote sources are read (electronAPI.readBinaryFile fallback)
loadMetadata: demuxer instantiation and metadata extraction (frameRate, streamDuration)
decodeAll: main streaming decode loop, backpressure, held-frame resampling, cleanup, and early-end detection via shouldFailDecodeEndedEarly
skip_unless_needed: small constants (tolerances) unless adjusting timing/heuristics
type aliases (OnFrameCallback, DecodedVideoInfo) unless altering the API surface

related_files.reason_to_check: If decodeAll API, emitted timestamps, or metadata fields change, videoExporter must be updated to match.

related_files.relationship: Consumer — gif exporter uses per-frame data produced by StreamingVideoDecoder; framerate/timestamp semantics are critical.
related_files.reason_to_check: GIF timing relies on exported timestamps; any change to frameDurationUs or timestamp units must be coordinated.

related_files.relationship: Integration — loadSourceFile uses window.electronAPI.readBinaryFile when present to read local files in packaged Electron apps.
related_files.reason_to_check: If preload API signature or return shape changes, loadSourceFile must be updated accordingly.

related_files.relationship: Consumer/Partner — muxer may need demuxer-provided audio or streamDuration and uses frames produced here.
related_files.reason_to_check: Changes to metadata.streamDuration or getDemuxer exposure could affect audio muxing and timeline alignment.

related_files.reason_to_check: If the wasm path or packaging changes, loadMetadata's wasm URL resolution must be verified.

tests_to_run: npm run test:browser (for any browser-facing exporter tests)
npm run build (to ensure bundling of wasm path and no dev-only references)

insights.title: Handle bare av01 codec descriptions for AV1 in WebCodecs
insights.problem: web-demuxer may return a bare codec string like "av01" (no parameter string). Passing this to WebCodecs causes VideoDecoder failures because WebCodecs expects a fully parameterized AV1 codec string (e.g. av01.0.05M.08).
insights.root_cause: Extradata/description for AV1 may be missing or in an unexpected container format (WebM raw OBU), leading the demuxer to return only 'av01'. WebCodecs requires the parameterized form.
insights.solution: Added buildAV1CodecString(description) to parse an AV1CodecConfigurationRecord BufferSource (if present) and synthesize a full codec string; when decoderConfig.codec is a bare av01, replace it with the built codec string before choosing software decode or starting the decoder.
insights.lesson_learned: When bridging demuxers/parsers and WebCodecs, normalize codec strings and defensively parse extradata; don't assume the demuxer will always produce a WebCodecs-ready codec value.

insights.title: Use view-aware byte extraction for BufferSource inputs
insights.problem: Parsing extradata previously used new Uint8Array(description instanceof ArrayBuffer ? description : description.buffer) which ignored typed-array views' byteOffset/byteLength, leading to incorrect parsing when description is an ArrayBufferView or DataView.
insights.root_cause: BufferSource can be an ArrayBuffer or an ArrayBufferView/DataView. Using .buffer without respecting the view's offset/length can result in reading the wrong bytes.
insights.solution: Construct a Uint8Array properly for each BufferSource: if it's an ArrayBuffer use new Uint8Array(description), otherwise use new Uint8Array(description.buffer, description.byteOffset, description.byteLength).
insights.lesson_learned: Always handle BufferSource inputs in a view-aware manner — respect byteOffset/byteLength when given ArrayBufferView/DataView.

insights.title: Add timeouts when loading/parsing remote or local source to avoid hangs
insights.problem: Loading remote blobs, reading local files via electronAPI, or demuxer parsing could hang indefinitely and stall exports (especially on Windows).
insights.root_cause: No timeouts were applied to async I/O and demuxer parsing operations; underlying platform/hardware edge cases could block.
insights.solution: Added SOURCE_LOAD_TIMEOUT_MS and a withTimeout helper used around readBinaryFile, fetch, response.blob(), demuxer.load, and getMediaInfo calls so operations fail fast with clear messages.

insights.title: Load local video sources via main process when necessary
insights.problem: Fetching local file URLs via fetch() could fail in packaged Electron apps; exporter needed to support local file inputs for decoding.
insights.root_cause: Renderer fetch is not reliable for non-HTTP file:// paths in packaged electron contexts and cross-origin restrictions may apply.
insights.solution: Add loadSourceFile helper that uses window.electronAPI.readBinaryFile for non-remote URLs; construct File/Blob from returned ArrayBuffer and continue decoding pipeline. On remote URLs fallback to fetch with response.ok checks.
insights.lesson_learned: Export/decoding pipelines that accept both remote and local sources should probe and read local files via main-process fs helpers exposed through preload for consistent, packaged app behavior.

insights.title: Decoder truncated by missing read end range and AV1 hardware issues
insights.problem: Some containers were truncated when demuxer.read() was called without an explicit end; AV1 codecs could fail with hardware acceleration.
insights.root_cause: Implicit streaming reads and default hardware acceleration caused failures/early termination for some files and some codecs (AV1/av01).
insights.solution: Pass an explicit end range to demuxer.read(..., start, end) using streamDuration/metadata; prefer software decode for AV1 via decoder.configure({ hardwareAcceleration: 'prefer-software' }) with fallback; add metadata.streamDuration field.
insights.lesson_learned: Demuxing streaming media needs explicit end ranges for truncated containers; codec-specific behavior (AV1) may require preferring software decoders with graceful fallback.

insights.title: Backpressure and VFR→CFR resampling overhaul
insights.problem: Original approach buffered full segment frames and resampled at the end causing unbounded memory growth, poor latency, and incorrect VFR handling with speed regions.
insights.root_cause: Resampling strategy assumed buffering entire VFR segment; decoder decodeQueue/backpressure not coordinated with consumer backlog leading to stalls and memory pressure.
insights.solution: Rewrote streaming resampling to a streaming pass: compute segment output frame counts, hold the last decoded frame, emit clones for target timestamps up to a midpoint handoff, limit backlog/pendingFrames, and use tighter backpressure thresholds. Throw an explicit error if decode ends early.
insights.lesson_learned: For streaming VFR -> CFR conversion, prefer streaming resampling (emit on the fly using held frames) to avoid buffering entire segments; coordinate backpressure across decoder queue and consumer backlog.

insights.title: Expose demuxer for audio processing and annotate audio presence
insights.problem: Video exporter later needed access to demuxer for audio processing (muxing audio), but decoder didn't expose demuxer and metadata lacked audio info.
insights.root_cause: Tight encapsulation of demuxer prevented reuse for audio post-processing.
insights.solution: Add getDemuxer() accessor, include hasAudio and audioCodec in metadata, and expose streamDuration in metadata.
insights.lesson_learned: When components (video/audio pipelines) share demuxer resources, provide safe accessors and expanded metadata fields to avoid re-demuxing or duplication.

insights.title: Robust demuxer destroy error handling
insights.problem: demuxer.destroy() could throw; earlier code swallowed with catch {} which TypeScript flagged/crash risk.
insights.root_cause: Empty catch blocks are unsafe and omitted errors; also could cause linter/TS issues.
insights.solution: Replace empty catch with catch { /* ignore */ } to be explicit and avoid swallowing with no block.
insights.lesson_learned: Handle destructor errors intentionally and explicitly; use clear comments for ignored exceptions.

insights.title: New StreamingVideoDecoder uses web-demuxer + VideoDecoder for forward-pass decode
insights.problem: Exporting by repeatedly seeking an HTMLVideoElement was slow and caused frame-accuracy issues.
insights.root_cause: VFR to CFR conversion and trim handling required a decoder that can produce frames in a forward pass; HTMLVideoElement seeking is not designed for heavy, sequential decoding workloads.
insights.solution: Introduced StreamingVideoDecoder that uses WebDemuxer WASM to demux the file, feeds chunks to a VideoDecoder, buffers frames per segment, resamples VFR → CFR, and invokes a callback per output frame. Implements cancellation, cleanup, and deliverSegment resampling.
insights.lesson_learned: Use demux+VideoDecoder for batch frame extraction. Handle backpressure (decodeQueueSize), provide cancellation hooks, and close VideoFrames. Compute segments based on trims to skip trimmed ranges while maintaining decoder state.

electron/i18n.ts.short_description: A minimal synchronous i18n helper for the Electron main process using the renderer's JSON locale files
electron/i18n.ts.description:
This file provides a lightweight, synchronous internationalization utility intended for use inside the Electron main process. It imports the same JSON locale files used by the renderer (common.json and dialogs.json for each supported locale) and exposes a small API to set/get the current locale and to retrieve translated strings by namespace and dot-path key. The module exists because the main process cannot (or should not) depend on the renderer's full i18n runtime; instead it needs a compact, synchronous way to read the same translation bundles for menus, dialogs and other main-process UI flows.

Design choices favor simplicity and reliability: JSON files are imported at module-load time into a static messages map keyed by a tight Locale union type. mainT(namespace, key, vars?) is the primary consumer-facing function; it resolves the value via a dot-path traversal, falls back to English if a key is missing in the current locale, returns a namespace.key string if no translation exists, and performs a minimal interpolation of {{var}} placeholders. setMainLocale enforces that only the supported locale strings ("en", "zh-CN", "es", "fr") can become the current locale. The module is intentionally synchronous and compact to avoid I/O, dynamic loading, or heavy dependencies in the main process.

When editing, respect that this is the authoritative main-process translation accessor. It must stay aligned with the JSON files imported here and with the renderer's supported locales. The module’s behavior around fallback-to-English, the exact formatting of the dot-path traversal, and placeholder interpolation semantics are relied upon by main-process code that shows translated text (menus, dialogs, system prompts). Changes to the Locale union, imported JSON paths, or fallback/placeholder semantics can silently change runtime behavior across platforms and during packaging, so those areas require careful verification.

key_constructs.name: messages
key_constructs.purpose: Holds the statically imported translation bundles for each supported locale and namespace
key_constructs.reasoning: This single in-memory map is the authoritative source of translations for the Electron main process and must stay in sync with the renderer JSON bundles and any changes to supported locales.

key_constructs.name: setMainLocale
key_constructs.purpose: Sets the currentLocale to one of the accepted locale strings
key_constructs.reasoning: This enforces a small whitelist of allowed locales and prevents arbitrary or mistyped locale strings from being set at runtime.

key_constructs.name: getMainLocale
key_constructs.purpose: Returns the current locale value
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by main-process code needing to query the active locale; typed to the Locale union to reflect allowed values.

key_constructs.name: getMessageValue
key_constructs.purpose: Traverses a nested object using a dot-separated key path and returns a string leaf if present
key_constructs.reasoning: Implements dot-path lookup across nested JSON translation objects without pulling in a full i18n runtime.

key_constructs.name: interpolate
key_constructs.purpose: Performs basic replacement of {{var}} placeholders with provided vars
key_constructs.reasoning: Simple templating is sufficient for many main-process strings (menu labels, dialog messages); placeholder syntax and missing-var behavior are explicit and must be preserved.

key_constructs.name: mainT
key_constructs.purpose: Public function to fetch a localized string for a namespace/key with optional interpolation and English fallback
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the primary API consumed by main-process code; it encapsulates lookup, fallback, interpolation, and missing-key formatting.

key_behaviors: returns localized string for namespace and dot-path key
falls back to English when a key is missing in the active locale
interpolates {{var}} placeholders with provided vars
restricts runtime locale to a small whitelist via setMainLocale

pitfalls.mistake: Changing the Locale union or messages mapping without updating the JSON imports
pitfalls.consequence: Missing or mismatched import paths will cause compile/runtime errors or absent translations in the main process
pitfalls.prevention: Ensure JSON locale files are present and the messages map is updated to include new locales or removed locales are also removed from imports and the union

pitfalls.mistake: Altering fallback behavior (e.g., removing English fallback) or the returned missing-key format

pitfalls.mistake: Modifying interpolate's regex or semantics without checking placeholder naming conventions
pitfalls.consequence: Placeholders with characters not matched by \w (e.g., hyphens or dots) will not be interpolated, potentially leaving raw {{placeholders}} visible
pitfalls.prevention: If placeholder syntax needs to change, ensure templates in JSON files and all callers follow the new convention and verify with runtime checks

pitfalls.mistake: Converting imports to dynamic or asynchronous loading without accounting for main-process timing
pitfalls.consequence: Main process code that runs early (menus, dialogs during startup) may miss translations or cause race conditions
pitfalls.prevention: Keep translations synchronous or ensure any change is compatible with main-process startup sequencing

setMainLocale: whitelist enforcement for allowed locale strings

interpolate: placeholder matching rules and fallback behavior for missing vars

src/hooks/useEditorHistory.ts.short_description: React hook that implements undo/redo history and live-update checkpointing for the video editor state
src/hooks/useEditorHistory.ts.description:
This file defines a reusable React hook, useEditorHistory, that manages an undo/redo history for the editor's mutable state (zoom, trim, speed, annotations, crop, webcam layout, visual settings, etc.). It exists to provide a predictable, user-friendly undo/redo experience in the video editor UI: discrete changes are captured as history checkpoints (pushState) while continuous live interactions (e.g., slider drags) are coalesced into a single checkpoint via updateState + commitState to avoid noisy histories. The hook keeps an immutable history (past/present/future) and enforces a maximum history length (MAX_HISTORY) to bound memory use.

The design intentionally excludes selection IDs from the undoable EditorState (see top-file comment) so that ephemeral UI selection changes don't become part of the user's undo stack. The hook exposes boolean capabilities (canUndo/canRedo) and methods to mutate history (pushState, updateState, commitState, undo, redo) plus the current state. Internally it uses a dirtyRef flag (useRef) to detect the start of a live-update series and only create the pre-interaction checkpoint once. Utilities resolve and withCheckpoint implement the merge semantics and the bounded past array behavior respectively.

This hook is a central state-management primitive used by editor components (video editor UI) to provide consistent undo/redo and live interaction behavior. Consumers must treat the returned state as immutable and call the appropriate methods during interactions (for example, use updateState while dragging a slider, then commitState when the drag ends; use pushState for discrete atomic changes). Because it's exported from a hooks directory and typed with EditorState, it is part of the editor's public hook API used across components.

key_constructs.name: EditorState
key_constructs.purpose: Type describing the shape of the editor state that is stored in history (zoomRegions, trimRegions, webcam settings, visual settings, etc.).
key_constructs.reasoning: Understanding the EditorState shape is essential because changes to this type change what is undoable and can impact serialization, equality assumptions, and consumer components that read/write fields.

key_constructs.name: INITIAL_EDITOR_STATE
key_constructs.purpose: Provides the initial EditorState used when the hook is first created (default crop, wallpaper, padding, webcam defaults, etc.).
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the authoritative default state for new editor instances; edits to these defaults will change the initial behavior and appearance of the editor and may require updates in tests and serialization.

key_constructs.name: MAX_HISTORY
key_constructs.purpose: Caps the number of historical entries retained in memory (80).
key_constructs.reasoning: Any change to this constant affects memory/undo depth and how withCheckpoint prunes past entries; tests and UX assumptions may rely on this bound.

key_constructs.name: resolve
key_constructs.purpose: Merges a StateUpdate (partial EditorState or updater function) into the current present state to produce the next present state.
key_constructs.reasoning: resolve ensures updates are applied by shallow merging and supports updater functions; maintain its merge semantics (shallow merge) so callers that pass partial state behave as expected.

key_constructs.name: withCheckpoint
key_constructs.purpose: Creates a new History by appending the current present into past (bounded by MAX_HISTORY) and setting a new present while clearing future.
key_constructs.reasoning: This function encapsulates the checkpoint semantics used by both pushState and initial live-update checkpointing; its slice logic enforces the history cap and should not be altered without considering undo stack behavior.

key_constructs.name: useEditorHistory
key_constructs.purpose: Main exported React hook that provides state, pushState, updateState, commitState, undo, redo and canUndo/canRedo flags.
key_constructs.reasoning: All consumer components import and rely on this hook for history behavior. Any API/behavior changes (method names, side-effects) are breaking and will require updates across the editor UI.

key_constructs.name: pushState
key_constructs.purpose: Creates a discrete checkpoint in history by applying an update and adding the prior present to the past; resets the live-update (dirty) flag.
key_constructs.reasoning: Use when a user action is a single atomic change (e.g., toggling an option). It clears future entries (as per usual undo semantics) and resets dirtyRef so subsequent live updates start fresh.

key_constructs.name: updateState
key_constructs.purpose: Used for live/coalesced updates: marks start of a live interaction and creates a single checkpoint at the first update; subsequent calls during the same interaction update present without pushing new past entries.
key_constructs.reasoning: Critical to avoid noisy undo stacks during continuous interactions (like slider drags). It relies on dirtyRef to detect first-call semantics; consumers must call commitState when interaction ends.

key_constructs.name: commitState
key_constructs.purpose: Marks the end of a live update series by resetting the dirtyRef flag; does not modify history directly.
key_constructs.reasoning: Semantics require this to be called after an update series to allow subsequent updateState to make a fresh checkpoint. Omitting commitState in typical usage will keep dirtyRef true and cause updateState calls to keep mutating present rather than creating a new checkpoint when desired.

key_constructs.name: undo
key_constructs.purpose: Moves one step backward in the history: moves last item from past into present and pushes previous present onto future.
key_constructs.reasoning: Must respect empty-past behavior and ensure dirtyRef is reset (it is). Undo behavior is central to user expectations and must preserve immutability of history arrays.

key_constructs.name: redo
key_constructs.purpose: Moves one step forward in the history: takes first item from future into present and appends current present into past.
key_constructs.reasoning: Must respect empty-future behavior and reset dirtyRef; redo reuses normal undo/redo semantics and clearing future when new checkpoints are added is expected.

key_behaviors: provides undo/redo of EditorState changes
coalesces live updates (slider drags) into a single checkpoint
limits history length to MAX_HISTORY
exposes immutable present state plus canUndo/canRedo flags

pitfalls.mistake: Mutating the present state object in place instead of returning a new object.
pitfalls.consequence: React consumers may not re-render and history invariants (immutability) will break leading to incorrect undo/redo behavior.
pitfalls.prevention: Always create new objects for present updates; respect resolve's shallow-merge approach.

pitfalls.mistake: Not calling commitState after a live interaction (e.g., slider drag) or calling updateState without committing.
pitfalls.consequence: dirtyRef remains true, causing subsequent interactions to be merged into the previous checkpoint and producing unexpected undo behavior.
pitfalls.prevention: Ensure UI components call updateState during interactions and call commitState on interaction end (mouseup/touchend).

pitfalls.mistake: Changing MAX_HISTORY or withCheckpoint slice logic without checking consumers/tests.
pitfalls.consequence: Altering history retention could break UX assumptions and tests that depend on a certain undo depth.
pitfalls.prevention: If MAX_HISTORY must change, update tests and review places that may assume a specific undo depth.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering the EditorState shape or removing fields used by components.
pitfalls.consequence: Breaks serialization, persistence, and components that read/write those fields; may cause runtime type errors or incorrect UI behavior.
pitfalls.prevention: Coordinate any EditorState shape changes with editor components, project persistence code, and tests.

pitfalls.mistake: Treating selection IDs as undoable state.
pitfalls.consequence: User expectations would be violated: selecting/deselecting would produce undo steps (the code explicitly excludes selection IDs).
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the file's comment: selection IDs are intentionally excluded from EditorState used here.

key_sections: INITIAL_EDITOR_STATE: understand default values and fields
MAX_HISTORY: history cap and withCheckpoint slice semantics
resolve: how updates (partial or function) are applied
withCheckpoint: how a new checkpoint is created and future cleared
pushState/updateState/commitState: the public API for discrete vs live updates
skip_unless_needed: import list at top (types and default constants) — only check if modifying EditorState fields

related_files.relationship: Defines types (ZoomRegion, TrimRegion, Webcam presets, DEFAULT_* constants) that shape EditorState; changes there affect EditorState fields and defaults used by INITIAL_EDITOR_STATE.
related_files.reason_to_check: If EditorState fields are added/removed/renamed or default constants change, update this hook and all consumers.

related_files.relationship: Consumer of useEditorHistory — orchestrates editor UI that relies on pushState/updateState/commitState for user interactions.
related_files.reason_to_check: UI components must call updateState/commitState correctly for live interactions; API changes to the hook require corresponding updates here.

related_files.relationship: Part of the editor/recording flow; while not directly tied to history, changes to editor state semantics could impact how recordings are loaded/edited.
related_files.reason_to_check: When altering EditorState shape or serialization behavior, check interactions where recordings are loaded into the editor.

tests_to_run: npm run test:browser:install && npm run test:browser

insights.title: History abstraction with push/update/commit and checkpointing
insights.problem: Editor needed undo/redo with sensible checkpointing for live interactions.
insights.root_cause: Without checkpointing, slider drags would create many undo entries; selection and ephemeral state should not be made undoable.
insights.solution: Implement useEditorHistory with past/present/future, MAX_HISTORY limit, pushState (creates checkpoint), updateState (live updates creating first checkpoint), commitState (end of interaction), undo/redo. Use dirtyRef to mark live-update sessions.
insights.lesson_learned: History API should distinguish discrete changes (push) vs live updates (update + commit) to avoid noisy undo stacks; keep selection IDs out of undoable state.

src/lib/shortcuts.ts.short_description: Typed shortcut binding registry and utilities for matching, formatting, merging, and conflict detection
src/lib/shortcuts.ts.description:
This module centralizes keyboard shortcut metadata, platform-aware matching, display formatting, and conflict detection for the editor UI. It defines a typed list of configurable actions (SHORTCUT_ACTIONS) and a compact representation for a binding (ShortcutBinding). The file exists so UI code and recording/editor logic can share a single source of truth for default shortcuts, localized fixed shortcuts, and the utilities required to compare and format bindings consistently across platforms (macOS vs Windows/Linux).

Design choices visible in the code: fixed (non-configurable) shortcuts are enumerated separately in FIXED_SHORTCUTS with an i18nKey, label, display string and possibly multiple bindings; configurable shortcuts appear in DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS keyed by action. Conflict detection is two-tiered: fixed shortcuts are checked first and then configurable-to-configurable conflicts are resolved by comparing the provided config against other actions. Platform differences are intentionally surfaced (matchesShortcut maps the binding.ctrl flag to Cmd on mac via the isMacPlatform parameter). Formatting uses a small KEY_LABELS map and an isMac boolean to render localized glyphs or text for modifier keys.

This module is referenced by UI components that: (1) present shortcut help and editing UI (to format display strings and enumerate fixed shortcuts using i18nKey/label/display), (2) check whether a pressed keyboard event matches a configured action (matchesShortcut), and (3) validate user edits to configurable shortcuts (findConflict, bindingsEqual, mergeWithDefaults). Historical commit notes indicate FIXED_SHORTCUTS was extended to include i18nKey to support localization and that conflict detection utilities were added to prevent assignment of reserved keys such as Tab/Delete.

When changing this file, respect the stable shapes of exported types and constants because other modules read DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS, FIXED_SHORTCUTS, and rely on matchesShortcut semantics. The findConflict implementation intentionally checks fixed shortcuts first and then configurable ones — changing that order alters user-visible validation behavior. Also, matchesShortcut maps binding.ctrl to the platform primary modifier (Cmd on macOS); any edits must preserve or explicitly rework that cross-platform mapping to avoid behavioral regressions on macOS.

key_constructs.name: SHORTCUT_ACTIONS
key_constructs.purpose: Canonical list (tuple) of configurable shortcut action identifiers
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to enumerate and type ShortcutAction and to iterate actions in merge/validation flows; keep stable order and entries because code depends on the string literal union and iteration order.

key_constructs.name: ShortcutAction
key_constructs.purpose: Type union of all configurable action names derived from SHORTCUT_ACTIONS
key_constructs.reasoning: Provides a narrow typed API for functions that accept an action key and ensures exhaustive mapping in ShortcutsConfig and SHORTCUT_LABELS.

key_constructs.name: ShortcutBinding
key_constructs.purpose: Represents a single keyboard binding (key + modifier booleans)
key_constructs.reasoning: Central representation used everywhere to match events, format UI labels, and persist user-configured shortcuts; fields must be preserved for compatibility.

key_constructs.name: ShortcutsConfig
key_constructs.purpose: Mapping from ShortcutAction to its binding
key_constructs.reasoning: Standard persistent/config shape for user-configured shortcuts consumed by UI and matching logic.

key_constructs.name: FixedShortcut
key_constructs.purpose: Metadata shape for non-configurable shortcuts (used by help UI and conflict detection)
key_constructs.reasoning: Includes i18nKey to support translation, label/display for UI fallback, and bindings[] since multiple keys can map to a single fixed action.

key_constructs.name: FIXED_SHORTCUTS
key_constructs.purpose: Array of reserved (non-configurable) shortcuts with UI metadata
key_constructs.reasoning: Central registry of keys that UI/validation must treat as reserved. The array order is not critical but entries (and their binding lists) must remain accurate so conflict detection and help UI display match each other.

key_constructs.name: ShortcutConflict
key_constructs.purpose: Union type representing the two kinds of conflicts: hitting a fixed shortcut or colliding with another configurable action
key_constructs.reasoning: Return shape for findConflict to let callers present appropriate messaging or swap semantics depending on the conflict type.

key_constructs.name: bindingsEqual
key_constructs.purpose: Value equality check for two ShortcutBinding objects
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by conflict detection and by FIXED_SHORTCUTS matching. Uses case-insensitive key compare and coerces modifiers to booleans so missing flags behave like false.

key_constructs.name: findConflict
key_constructs.purpose: Checks whether a given binding conflicts with a fixed shortcut or any other configurable action in provided config
key_constructs.reasoning: Important validation helper for UI when users assign or change configurable shortcuts. It checks fixed shortcuts first (so reserved keys are reported as fixed conflicts) then configurable ones.

key_constructs.name: DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS
key_constructs.purpose: Default mapping of configurable actions to their default ShortcutBinding
key_constructs.reasoning: Serves as the baseline config used when no user config is present and as the source for mergeWithDefaults.

callers.context: import { DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS, mergeWithDefaults, type ShortcutsConfig } from "@/lib/shortcuts";

key_constructs.name: SHORTCUT_LABELS
key_constructs.purpose: Human-readable labels for configurable actions (non-i18n display mapping)
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by parts of the UI that need a stable English label for each action; note that FIXED_SHORTCUTS provides i18nKey for translations instead of this map.

key_constructs.name: matchesShortcut
key_constructs.purpose: Checks if a KeyboardEvent corresponds to a ShortcutBinding, respecting the platform primary modifier
key_constructs.reasoning: Encapsulates event matching logic so UI and input handlers don't duplicate platform-specific modifier mapping (Cmd vs Ctrl). It expects callers to supply isMacPlatform to control mapping behavior.

key_constructs.name: KEY_LABELS
key_constructs.purpose: Lookup table mapping special key idents to nicer display labels
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by formatBinding to produce human friendly key names (e.g., Space, arrow glyphs, Del). Adding entries affects displayed strings across the UI.

key_constructs.name: formatBinding
key_constructs.purpose: Render a ShortcutBinding into a human-readable string suitable for UI, respecting macOS glyphs when requested
key_constructs.reasoning: UI must use this single function to keep visual representation consistent; it relies on binding flags and the KEY_LABELS map and expects callers to pass isMac to choose glyphs.

key_constructs.name: mergeWithDefaults
key_constructs.purpose: Create a complete ShortcutsConfig by merging provided partial config onto DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS
key_constructs.reasoning: Used when loading user preferences that may omit some actions; it iterates SHORTCUT_ACTIONS to ensure all keys exist, preserving DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS as the base.

callers.context: import { DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS, mergeWithDefaults, type ShortcutsConfig } from "@/lib/shortcuts";

key_behaviors: matches keyboard events to configured shortcuts
formats bindings for display in help and settings
detects conflicts against fixed and configurable shortcuts
merges partial user configs with defaults

pitfalls.mistake: Treating binding.ctrl as 'always Ctrl key' instead of 'primary modifier' that maps to Cmd on macOS
pitfalls.consequence: Shortcut matching will break on macOS (users expecting Cmd-based shortcuts won't match), leading to wrong behavior for modifiers.
pitfalls.prevention: Preserve matchesShortcut's mapping of binding.ctrl to metaKey on macOS (isMacPlatform parameter) or update every caller consistently if changing semantics.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering the FIXED_SHORTCUTS entries shape (removing i18nKey, renaming label/display fields, or changing bindings[])
pitfalls.consequence: UI that uses these fields for translation and display will break; findConflict may fail to detect reserved keys correctly.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep FixedShortcut interface and FIXED_SHORTCUTS entries stable; update any consuming UI code when modifying the shape.

pitfalls.mistake: Changing findConflict ordering (checking configurable conflicts before fixed ones)
pitfalls.consequence: Reserved keys might be reported as configurable collisions, producing confusing messages and possibly allowing assignment of reserved keys.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect current order: fixed shortcuts are checked first, then other configurable actions.

pitfalls.mistake: Relying on binding.key case-sensitivity or mutating KEY_LABELS keys without updating formatBinding expectations
pitfalls.consequence: bindingsEqual/matchesShortcut comparisons or UI labels can become inconsistent; ' ' (space) and arrow keys are special-cased in KEY_LABELS.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep key strings normalized (lowercase) in persisted configs and ensure KEY_LABELS is updated alongside any key name changes.

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS contains all SHORTCUT_ACTIONS without using mergeWithDefaults
pitfalls.consequence: New actions added to SHORTCUT_ACTIONS may be omitted from user configs leading to undefined entries and runtime errors when accessed by code expecting a value.
pitfalls.prevention: Use mergeWithDefaults or verify DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS when adding new actions.

key_sections: DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS: baseline mappings used by mergeWithDefaults and initial state
FIXED_SHORTCUTS: non-configurable shortcuts used by help UI and findConflict
findConflict: conflict detection logic (fixed first, then configurable)
matchesShortcut: platform-aware event matching and formatBinding: UI display formatting
skip_unless_needed: SHORTCUT_LABELS: simple labels map used in limited UI contexts
KEY_LABELS: display label map for special keys (only extend when adding new special keys)

related_files.relationship: UI/entrypoint that may call into electronAPI and reference shortcut display/help
related_files.reason_to_check: If fixed shortcuts or display formatting change, update any help text or UI that lists reserved keys.

related_files.relationship: Primary editor UI that depends on matching shortcuts and configurable action names
related_files.reason_to_check: If action names (SHORTCUT_ACTIONS) or default bindings change, editor keyboard handlers must be reviewed.

related_files.relationship: Hook that may respond to play/pause or other shortcut-triggered actions
related_files.reason_to_check: Changes to playPause binding or matchesShortcut semantics will affect recording control hotkeys.

tests_to_run: npm run test:browser (if making UI/format changes)

insights.title: Add i18nKey and enumerate fixed shortcuts for localization
insights.problem: Fixed shortcut labels were hardcoded and not localizable in help UI.
insights.root_cause: FixedShortcut lacked an i18n key and UI components used label strings directly.
insights.solution: Add i18nKey to FixedShortcut and add keys for existing shortcuts (undo, redo, frameBack/frameForward, etc.). Update UI components to use t(i18nKey, defaultValue: label).
insights.lesson_learned: Design shortcut metadata with localization in mind from the start; include stable keys for translations to avoid string-based lookups.

insights.title: Add FIXED_SHORTCUTS and conflict detection utility
insights.problem: Users could assign shortcuts that conflict with reserved fixed keys (Tab, Delete) or other configurable shortcuts.
insights.root_cause: No central registry of fixed shortcuts and no conflict detection logic existed.
insights.solution: Add FIXED_SHORTCUTS array describing reserved key bindings and findConflict/bindingsEqual helpers to detect conflicts with configurable shortcuts (returning type 'fixed' or 'configurable').
insights.lesson_learned: Reserve non-configurable shortcuts centrally and detect conflicts early in configuration UI; provide clear messaging and swap semantics for configurable conflicts.

insights.title: New shortcut binding types and matching/format utilities
insights.problem: Keyboard bindings needed a typed representation and platform-aware matching/formatting.
insights.root_cause: Ad-hoc inline checks made keyboard handling scattered and hard to localize.
insights.solution: Introduced ShortcutBinding and ShortcutsConfig types, DEFAULT_SHORTCUTS, matchesShortcut (which maps ctrl to Cmd on macOS), formatBinding for UI display, and mergeWithDefaults.
insights.lesson_learned: Centralize keyboard binding logic to simplify matching and formatting across the app; respect platform modifier differences (Cmd vs Ctrl).

src/components/video-editor/PlaybackCont.short_description: React playback control bar for editor: play/pause, seek, time display, optional fullscreen.
src/components/video-editor/PlaybackCont.description:
PlaybackControls is a compact React functional component that renders the media playback UI used inside the video editor. It exists to centralize the UI and interaction for play/pause toggling, seeking, time display, progress visualization, and an optional fullscreen toggle. The component is intentionally visually compact (dense spacing, small fonts) to fit into the editor's resizable panels and uses a custom-styled progress track and thumb while delegating the actual media control behavior to callbacks provided by the parent.

Design choices reflected here: the component is purely presentational/controlled — it receives isPlaying, currentTime, duration, and isFullscreen as inputs and exposes user interactions via onTogglePlayPause, onSeek, and an optional onToggleFullscreen. Time formatting is local to the component (formatTime). Accessibility/UX considerations are present in the form of aria-labels on the buttons (using i18n strings via useScopedT) and use of a native input[type=range] for keyboard and pointer seeking, with the visible track/thumb implemented separately for visual fidelity. Commit history notes indicate a fullscreen toggle was added and layout tokens were tightened to match resizable editor panels.

key_constructs.name: PlaybackControls
key_constructs.purpose: Render the playback control bar and translate user interactions into prop callbacks.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the primary exported component in the file and the only top-level symbol consumers import. Any change to its props, structure, or DOM layout affects how parent components (e.g., VideoEditor) control playback and fullscreen behavior.

key_constructs.name: PlaybackControlsProps
key_constructs.purpose: TypeScript interface declaring props the component expects.
key_constructs.reasoning: Defines the public contract for the component — particularly which callbacks are required vs optional (onToggleFullscreen is optional). Modifying this interface changes the compile-time contract with consumers.

key_constructs.name: formatTime
key_constructs.purpose: Convert a time in seconds to a 'M:SS' string with fallback for invalid inputs.
key_constructs.reasoning: Used to present currentTime/duration in a human-readable form and contains a guard for invalid numeric values that returns '0:00'. Any change here impacts how times are displayed throughout the UI and tests (if present).

key_constructs.name: handleSeekChange
key_constructs.purpose: Event handler that parses the range input value and calls onSeek with a numeric time.
key_constructs.reasoning: Bridges the native input event (string value) to the numeric onSeek API. It assumes onSeek expects a number and uses parseFloat; altering parsing or event wiring will change seek behavior.

src/components/launch/SourceSelector.tsx.short_description: React component that fetches desktop capture sources and renders a selectable source selector UI.
src/components/launch/SourceSelector.tsx.description:
SourceSelector.tsx is a React functional component responsible for listing available desktop capture sources (screens and windows), letting the user pick one, and sending the selection back to the main process via the electron contextBridge API. It exists to provide the user-facing flow that appears when the app asks which screen/window to share — it requests system-provided thumbnails and application icons, displays them as cards with selection badges, and exposes Cancel/Share actions. The component intentionally handles cross-platform differences: it counts screen vs window sources and defaults the visible tab to "windows" when no screen sources are present (an explicit UX decision based on Linux/PipeWire behavior).

The component uses a useEffect hook to call window.electronAPI.getSources with an options object (types: ["screen","window"], thumbnail size, and fetchWindowIcons: true), maps the returned raw sources to the local DesktopSource shape, and stores them in state. UI is composed with a Tabs control (screens/windows), grid layout for cards, and two buttons (Cancel calls window.close, Share calls electronAPI.selectSource). The component relies on i18n hooks (useScopedT) for translatable labels and imports a CSS module for card and scrollbar styling, which is important because the visual behavior (like custom scrollbars and card selection) is part of its intended UX.

This file fits into the larger Electron app by depending on the preload/contextBridge API (window.electronAPI) for desktopCapturer interactions and by being part of the launch/source selection flow (paired with other launch components). Because the renderer code sometimes runs in non-Electron dev/test modes, the component is defensive in its async fetch (try/catch) and handles null thumbnails or app icons. The commit history shows several UX-driven changes here (defaulting tab when screenSources is empty, custom scrollbar CSS, and increased content height) — edits must respect those cross-platform considerations and visual polish decisions.

src/utils/aspectRatioUtils.ts.short_description: Utility helpers for representing and converting supported aspect ratios.
src/utils/aspectRatioUtils.ts.description:
This module centralizes the canonical list of supported aspect ratios and provides helpers to convert those string values to numeric ratios, dimensions, labels, CSS-ready values, and portrait/landscape checks. It exists so the rest of the app (UI controls, editor layout, exporter, CSS/layout calculations, etc.) can rely on a single authoritative list of allowed aspect ratios and consistent logic for how each ratio is interpreted.

Key design decisions: there is a single const tuple ASPECT_RATIOS that is used to derive the AspectRatio union type to avoid duplicating allowed values across the codebase. getAspectRatioValue implements an exhaustive TypeScript switch over AspectRatio with a never default branch — this enforces compile-time coverage when a new ratio is added. The module purposely treats "native" as a special token: getAspectRatioValue maps "native" to a fixed fallback numeric ratio (16/9) and callers that have real source dimensions / crop regions are expected to call getNativeAspectRatioValue instead. Several helpers are small, single-responsibility functions (dimension calculation, label string, CSS formatting, portrait detection) so they can be composed by UI and layout code.

This file is small and widely referenced. Changing the list of ratios, the native fallback semantics, or the CSS formatting behavior can have broad effects (UI lists, editor aspect controls, exporter presets, layout math). The commit history indicates it was introduced/refactored to centralize allowed values and enable exhaustive switch checking; preserve that pattern if editing so that TypeScript continues to guard additions to the enum.

key_constructs.name: ASPECT_RATIOS
key_constructs.purpose: Canonical tuple of allowed aspect-ratio string values used across the app.
key_constructs.reasoning: Acts as the single source of truth for permissible ratios; the AspectRatio type is derived from it so adding/removing a value updates the type everywhere.

callers.context: import { ASPECT_RATIOS, type AspectRatio, getAspectRatioLabel } from "@/utils/aspectRatioUtils";

key_constructs.name: AspectRatio
key_constructs.purpose: TypeScript union type derived from ASPECT_RATIOS representing valid ratio keys.
key_constructs.reasoning: Ensures compile-time correctness and enables exhaustive switch checking when used in functions like getAspectRatioValue.

key_constructs.name: getAspectRatioValue
key_constructs.purpose: Convert an AspectRatio string into a numeric width/height ratio; returns a fixed fallback for "native".
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by UI/layout code that needs a numeric ratio for math or to derive dimensions. Uses an exhaustive switch to make TypeScript surface missing cases when AspectRatio changes.

key_constructs.name: getNativeAspectRatioValue
key_constructs.purpose: Compute the numeric native aspect ratio based on actual video width/height and optional crop region.
key_constructs.reasoning: Callers that have a real video source or a crop region should use this to determine the true aspect ratio (the function handles an optional cropRegion). It exists because getAspectRatioValue's "native" fallback is not appropriate for source-aware contexts.

key_constructs.name: getAspectRatioDimensions
key_constructs.purpose: Given an AspectRatio and a base width, return width and computed height.
key_constructs.reasoning: Convenience helper for UI/layout to quickly obtain scaled dimensions while preserving the chosen aspect ratio.

key_constructs.name: getAspectRatioLabel
key_constructs.purpose: Return a human-readable label for an AspectRatio value (maps "native" to "Native").
key_constructs.reasoning: Used by UI controls that render selector labels.

callers.context: import { ASPECT_RATIOS, type AspectRatio, getAspectRatioLabel } from "@/utils/aspectRatioUtils";

key_constructs.purpose: Return whether an AspectRatio represents a portrait orientation (numeric ratio < 1).
key_constructs.reasoning: Useful in UI/layout decisions to flip controls, pick orientations, or rotate previews.

key_constructs.name: formatAspectRatioForCSS
key_constructs.purpose: Format an AspectRatio into a value ready to be used in CSS (replacing ":" with "/" or emitting a numeric fallback for "native").
key_constructs.reasoning: Used when the aspect ratio must be supplied to CSS properties (e.g., aspect-ratio), and supports an optional nativeRatio override for the "native" token.

computes native ratio from source dimensions and optional crop
calculates scaled height for a base width
formats aspect-ratio strings for UI and CSS

pitfalls.mistake: Treating "native" the same as other aspect ratios and calling getAspectRatioValue when true native source dimensions are available.
pitfalls.consequence: You will get a static 16/9 fallback instead of the actual source/crop-based aspect ratio; UI/layout or exports that depend on true source ratio will be wrong.
pitfalls.prevention: Use getNativeAspectRatioValue when you have videoWidth/videoHeight (and cropRegion) rather than relying on getAspectRatioValue for "native".

pitfalls.mistake: Changing ASPECT_RATIOS values or removing an entry without updating all consumers.
pitfalls.consequence: Consumers that build UI lists, saver/loaders, or exporter presets may break or become inconsistent; TypeScript will help, but some runtime lists or serialized project files may be impacted.
pitfalls.prevention: Recognize ASPECT_RATIOS is the canonical list; check UI selectors (editor/source selector/export presets) and serialization code when altering it.

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming getNativeAspectRatioValue's cropRegion uses pixels vs normalized ratios.
pitfalls.consequence: Misinterpreting the semantics can lead to incorrect ratios. The function multiplies videoWidth by cropRegion.width and divides by (videoHeight * cropRegion.height) — if cropRegion.width/height are absolute pixels, the result will be scaled incorrectly unless callers expect that math.
pitfalls.prevention: Verify how cropRegion is generated/represented (normalized fraction vs pixel extents) in calling code before changing the function or its callers.

pitfalls.mistake: Altering formatAspectRatioForCSS to change the native fallback representation.
pitfalls.consequence: Consumers that expect a fraction string (e.g., "16/9") or a numeric string may break; CSS accepts both numbers and fraction strings, so changing the format changes how CSS receives the ratio.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect that formatAspectRatioForCSS returns a decimal string for native when nativeRatio is not provided and that callers may rely on this behavior.

pitfalls.mistake: Removing the exhaustive switch/default-never pattern in getAspectRatioValue.
pitfalls.consequence: TypeScript will no longer force updates when a new AspectRatio is added, increasing risk of unhandled cases and runtime errors.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the exhaustive switch (with never) to preserve compile-time coverage guarantees.

getAspectRatioValue: numeric mapping and exhaustive switch pattern (preserve this for type safety)
getNativeAspectRatioValue: how native ratio is computed from video/crop inputs (semantics of cropRegion matter)
formatAspectRatioForCSS: how values are prepared for CSS (note native fallback is a decimal string)

insights.title: Centralize AspectRatio values and enable exhaustive type-checking
insights.problem: Aspect ratio values were duplicated inline in UI components and the string union type could get out of sync with UI usage.
insights.root_cause: Allowed aspect ratios were declared as a string union in the type and repeated as inline arrays in UI code, making it easy to forget to update all places when adding a new ratio.
insights.solution: Introduce ASPECT_RATIOS as a single const tuple and derive the AspectRatio type from it; update getAspectRatioValue to use exhaustive switch with a never default to ensure compile-time coverage.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep canonical lists of allowed values in one place and derive types from them. Use an exhaustive switch pattern (never default) to make TypeScript surface missing case coverage when extending enums/tuples.

src/components/video-editor/CropControl..short_description: Interactive crop UI over a video canvas that exposes a normalized crop region.
src/components/video-editor/CropControl..description:
CropControl is a React functional component that renders an interactive cropping overlay over a video preview. It exists to let users visually adjust a normalized crop rectangle (x,y,width,height as values in [0,1]) on top of a live video frame. The component renders a canvas that continuously draws the current video frame (via requestAnimationFrame) and places an SVG-based dimming/mask and a set of absolutely-positioned div handles to allow moving and resizing the crop rectangle. Changes to the crop are reported upward via onCropChange with a CropRegion object in normalized coordinates.

Design-wise the component separates representation (CropRegion, normalized coordinates) from DOM layout (percent-based CSS positions, SVG mask). The canvas is sized to the actual video resolution (video.videoWidth/video.videoHeight) while the UI overlay positions are computed as percentages (cropRegion.* * 100). Drag interactions are performed in container-normalized coordinates (client coordinates divided by container width/height), so crop math works independent of pixel scaling. The component enforces invariants such as a minimum crop width/height of 10% (0.1), preventing inversion when dragging opposite edges, and constraining moves so the crop stays within 0..1 bounds.

This component fits into the video editor flow: a parent editor supplies the HTMLVideoElement reference and the cropRegion (likely from editor state). Parent components expect onCropChange to be called continuously as the user drags. The file still declares an aspectRatio prop in CropControlProps (AspectRatio type import present) but the function does not destructure or use it; commit history indicates aspectRatio was removed from the component's public API in a recent refactor, so call sites may still pass it but the component currently ignores it. Because the crop values are normalized, other parts of the export pipeline (exporter, muxer) will need to convert them to pixel-space against the original video resolution when applying the crop during export.

src/lib/compositeLayout.ts.short_description: Compute positions and sizes for composing a screen capture and webcam overlay on a canvas.
src/lib/compositeLayout.ts.description:
This module encapsulates the geometry logic for composing a screen recording area and an optional webcam overlay into a single canvas layout. It exists so the renderer (video editor UI, preview, exporter) can consistently position and size the webcam relative to the screen capture area across different canvas sizes, aspect ratios, and presets. The code centralizes visual rules (presets, margins, border radii, shadows) and numeric math for sizing so other parts of the app can rely on a single authoritative layout algorithm.

Design decisions visible here: numeric webcam size presets (10–50 percent) are converted to a fraction by webcamSizeToFraction and applied to a geometric-mean reference dimension (sqrt(canvasWidth * canvasHeight)) so that the webcam occupies a consistent perceptual area regardless of canvas orientation. Two preset transform types are supported: overlay (picture-in-picture) and stack (vertical-stack). Overlay computes a scaled webcam that preserves aspect ratio (with shape-specific adjustments for square/circle/squared masks) and clamps placement to canvas bounds; stack places a full-width webcam at the bottom and sets screen to cover mode. Rounding and clamping choices (Math.round, Math.max/Math.min) are used to keep integer pixel values predictable for rendering and tests.

This file is used by UI components (video editor preview and layout controls) and exporter code that needs exact pixel geometry. Tests in src/lib/compositeLayout.test.ts verify important invariants (anchoring, monotonic size growth with preset, clamping, square enforcement for circular masks, geometric-area consistency across portrait/landscape).
