src/lib/compositeLayout.test.ts.description:
This test file exercises computeCompositeLayout and asserts geometric and placement invariants that the UI and exporter rely upon. The tests are written with vitest and focus on behaviorally important guarantees rather than pixel-perfect positioning in every case. They check anchoring (lower-right default overlay), that overlay sizing respects the stage fraction and preserves aspect ratio, monotonic scaling when webcamSizePreset increases, clamping of presets to 10–50, special-case behavior for vertical stack preset (including no-webcam handling), and mask-shape-specific rules (square/circle forcing square dimensions, rounded masks producing larger radius).

Because the assertions include exact equalities in some cases (area equality between portrait and landscape) and tight inequalities in others, the implementation's numeric choices (geometric mean reference, rounding with Math.round/Math.floor, clamp bounds) are important. The tests were updated historically to reflect a refactor that moved sizing to a numeric percent model and geometric-mean reference dimension. The tests both document expected behavior and act as a guardrail for changes to compositeLayout.ts.

src/components/video-editor/AnnotationSe.short_description: React settings panel UI for viewing and editing a single annotation's type, content and style
src/components/video-editor/AnnotationSe.description:
A stateful React functional component that renders the annotation settings inspector used by the video editor. This panel lets the user switch annotation type (text, image, figure/arrow), edit text content, upload images, pick fonts (including custom fonts), set font size and formatting (bold/italic/underline/align), pick text/background colors, and configure figure-specific options (arrow direction, stroke width, shapes/emojis). It exists to centralize all annotation editing UI and to emit changes through callbacks so the parent/editor can update the annotation model and persist that change for rendering and export.

The component integrates with app-level systems: i18n (useScopedT) for localized labels, the custom fonts storage API (getCustomFonts) so user-added fonts appear in the font family selector, a dialog component for adding custom fonts (AddCustomFontDialog), and the Toast system (sonner) for user feedback on image upload success/failure. It uses numerous UI primitives from the project's design system (Select, Popover, Tabs, ToggleGroup, Slider, Button) and small helper modules (cn, getArrowComponent) so it plugs directly into the editor's look-and-feel and export model (FigureData).

Design decisions visible in the code: (1) separation of concerns via callback props (onContentChange, onTypeChange, onStyleChange, onFigureDataChange, onDelete) — the component does not mutate global state itself but informs parent; (2) in-panel management of custom fonts — the panel loads custom fonts on mount and refreshes the list when AddCustomFontDialog reports a new font; (3) file upload handled via an invisible input and FileReader to produce data URLs, with MIME type validation and explicit input value reset to allow re-uploading the same file; (4) Select controls convert between string values and typed style fields (e.g., fontSize: number is converted to/from string for Select value). The commit history indicates recent additions: exposing custom fonts and consolidating figure configuration into a single FigureData model so UI and exporter remain in sync.

src/components/video-editor/timeline/Tim.short_description: React wrapper that wires dnd-timeline interactions, clamping logic, and a live DOM tooltip for editing timeline spans.
src/components/video-editor/timeline/Tim.description:
This component wraps the third-party TimelineContext from the dnd-timeline package and adapts it to the editor's domain rules. It exists to centralize timeline interaction policies (range clamping, item span clamping, neighbour-aware snapping) and to supply live UI affordances (a direct-DOM tooltip) without inducing React re-renders during high-frequency drag/resize events. The wrapper converts videoDuration into a totalMs timeline domain, enforces minimum durations and visible range constraints, and resolves collisions with neighbouring regions when the user moves or resizes items.

Design decisions visible in the code: clamping functions (clampSpanToBounds, clampRange) normalize spans and ranges relative to totalMs and minimums; clampToNeighbours attempts to snap an active span to neighbour boundaries and expands/contracts it so that minimum duration rules are still satisfied; tooltip display is performed with direct DOM updates (tooltipRef) for performance reasons rather than state updates. Event handlers (onDragStart/onDragMove/onDragEnd, onResizeMove/onResizeEnd) extract spans from event.active.data.current.getSpanFromDragEvent or getSpanFromResizeEvent, show/hide the tooltip during interactions, apply clamping rules on end events, and call onItemSpanChange when final positions are accepted.

Integration context: TimelineWrapper is intended to sit around timeline child components in the Video Editor UI. It depends on external props and callbacks supplied by the parent: range, onRangeChange, videoDuration, hasOverlap (collision detection), onItemSpanChange, and arrays of region spans for neighbour-aware snapping. The component does not own authoritative persistence; it emits changes via callbacks. The commit history notes that tooltip and neighbour clamping were added to improve UX — those features are tightly integrated into the event lifecycle and should be respected when editing.

Non-obvious behaviors and edge cases: a zero-duration source (totalMs === 0) is specially handled in clamping functions to allow non-zero minimum durations and avoid divisions/negative bounds. The neighbour snapping attempts to preserve minimum durations by extending or contracting where possible; if an overlap cannot be resolved it rejects the modification (returns early). The tooltip positioning constrains left position inside the parent bounding rect and caps the x position to avoid overflow. Event handlers assume event.active.data.current provides helper methods to compute spans from native drag/resize events; changes to that contract will break this wrapper.

insights.root_cause: Timeline interactions did not expose live tooltip or neighbor-aware clamping; clamp logic sometimes rejected user gestures outright.
insights.solution: Added DOM tooltip with showTooltip/hideTooltip, hooked onDragStart/onDragMove/onResizeMove to update tooltip, implemented clampToNeighbours to snap edges to neighbor boundaries and attempt to extend to minimum duration when possible; integrated these in onDragEnd/onResizeEnd.
insights.lesson_learned: For timeline UX, provide live visual feedback (tooltips) using direct DOM updates to avoid expensive re-renders; prefer clamping/snap-to-neighbor over rejecting moves to reduce frustration.

src/hooks/useAudioLevelMeter.ts.short_description: React hook that opens a microphone MediaStream, creates an AudioContext + AnalyserNode and exposes a smoothed RMS audio level.
src/hooks/useAudioLevelMeter.ts.description:
This module provides a React hook (useAudioLevelMeter) used to measure and expose a live microphone input level for UI components (for example the HUD/microphone level indicator). It encapsulates the Web Audio steps required to obtain a MediaStream via navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia, create an AudioContext, connect a MediaStreamSource to an AnalyserNode, poll frequency-bin data via requestAnimationFrame, compute an RMS-like level, and set a normalized numeric level state that React components can consume.

The hook exists to centralize audio metering responsibilities so UI components do not need to duplicate getUserMedia/WebAudio lifecycle logic. It handles lifecycle concerns: resuming suspended AudioContext, stopping MediaStream tracks and closing the AudioContext on disable/unmount, cancelling the animation frame loop, and guarding against race conditions with a mounted flag. Options are provided to enable/disable metering, select a specific deviceId (passed in as an exact constraint), and tweak the analyser.smoothingTimeConstant.

Key considerations: the hook uses analyser.getByteFrequencyData (frequency-domain bins) and computes RMS over the frequency bins (squared sum -> sqrt average) then maps that to a 0-100 scaled value with a clamp. The analyser fftSize is configured to 256 and smoothingTimeConstant defaults to 0.8 unless overridden. Errors from getUserMedia or creating/using audio APIs are caught and logged; when an error occurs the level is set to 0. The hook returns a simple object { level } where level is a number in (nominally) 0-100.

key_constructs.name: AudioLevelMeterOptions
key_constructs.purpose: TypeScript interface describing options accepted by the hook: enabled, deviceId, smoothingFactor.
key_constructs.reasoning: This single exported type documents expected inputs and drives the hook's behavior (enablement, device selection, smoothing). Consumers of the hook rely on these option fields to toggle metering and select microphone sources.

key_constructs.name: useAudioLevelMeter
key_constructs.purpose: React hook that returns a numeric audio level and manages WebAudio + MediaStream lifecycles.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the primary public API provided by the file; other UI hooks/components will import and call it. It is stateful and manages async browser APIs and must be treated as a side-effecting hook that opens microphone streams when enabled.

key_behaviors: requests microphone MediaStream when enabled
creates and resumes an AudioContext then connects a MediaStreamSource to an AnalyserNode
polls analyser data via requestAnimationFrame to compute and set a numeric level
stops tracks, cancels animation frames, and closes AudioContext on disable or unmount

pitfalls.mistake: Assume getUserMedia will always succeed or return immediately
pitfalls.consequence: If user denies permission or the device is unavailable, errors will be thrown; the hook catches and logs errors but will keep level at 0. Components should be prepared for level remaining 0.
pitfalls.prevention: Do not rely on level > 0 to imply permission; handle error states in the UI separately if needed.

pitfalls.mistake: Passing an invalid deviceId or changing deviceId while starting
pitfalls.consequence: navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia with an exact deviceId can throw OverconstrainedError; this can cause the hook to bail out and leave UI showing 0.
pitfalls.prevention: When programmatically changing deviceId, ensure callers validate device presence or handle errors; the hook will log and set level to 0 on failure.

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming AudioContext.close() is synchronous
pitfalls.consequence: close() returns a promise but the cleanup function does not await it; callers that rely on immediate closure may observe the context still closing in background or throw if re-created too quickly.
pitfalls.prevention: Avoid concurrent create/close race conditions from outside the hook; respect that cleanup triggers asynchronous close work inside the browser.

pitfalls.mistake: Relying on the level value being an exact dB-like measurement
pitfalls.consequence: The hook computes an RMS-like value over frequency-domain bins and applies a scaling and clamp; it is a UI-friendly relative metric, not an absolute calibrated amplitude/dB measurement.
pitfalls.prevention: Treat level as a relative UI indicator; don’t use it where precise audio-level calibration is required.

pitfalls.mistake: Not cancelling the animation frame or stopping tracks on unmount/disable
pitfalls.consequence: Leaving requestAnimationFrame or MediaStream tracks running will leak audio hardware access and keep the microphone active.
pitfalls.prevention: Respect the hook’s cleanup; any modifications to updateLoop or cleanup must preserve cancelling animationFrameRef and stopping all stream tracks.

key_sections: startMonitoring: async flow that requests getUserMedia, creates AudioContext/AnalyserNode and starts the update loop
updateLevel: the requestAnimationFrame loop computing RMS and setting state
cleanup: logic for cancelling animation frames, stopping tracks, and closing the AudioContext
skip_unless_needed: the small math block that computes RMS from the dataArray if only API-level behavior is of interest

related_files.relationship: likely consumer: screen recorder or HUD components will use this hook to show mic levels during recording
related_files.reason_to_check: Changes to the hook's public API (options or return shape) or lifecycle semantics should be validated against recorder logic and any components that call useAudioLevelMeter.

related_files.relationship: likely UI component that consumes the numeric level from this hook to render a visual meter
related_files.reason_to_check: Presentation expects a numeric 0-100 style value and smoothing; if scale or semantics change, the indicator must be adjusted.

insights.title: Add audio level meter using WebAudio AnalyserNode
insights.problem: Need to display microphone input level in the HUD while mic is enabled.
insights.root_cause: No existing UI-level hook for reading microphone amplitude in real-time.
insights.solution: New useAudioLevelMeter hook: open getUserMedia audio stream, create AudioContext + AnalyserNode, compute RMS of frequency data, update UI at rAF; cleans up AudioContext and stops tracks when disabled.
insights.lesson_learned: For audio metering, use small fftSize and smoothingTimeConstant; ensure robust cleanup to avoid leaking microphone permission streams; use requestAnimationFrame for smooth updates.

src/lib/assetPath.ts.short_description: Resolve a safe URL for an app asset, handling dev server, Electron base path, and fallbacks
src/lib/assetPath.ts.description:
This module centralizes how the renderer resolves paths to static assets (images, wallpapers, etc.) in different runtime environments: dev server (http/https), packaged Electron (where an asset base path is supplied via the preload/electron API), and a generic fallback. It encodes each path segment with encodeURIComponent to avoid invalid URL characters, trims leading slashes, and composes a final URL. The implementation attempts a best-effort strategy: prefer a web-served path when window.location indicates an HTTP(S) dev server; otherwise, if an Electron-provided asset base path is available via window.electronAPI.getAssetBasePath, use that base to construct an absolute URL; if anything fails or the environment is not a browser-like window, fall back to a simple root-relative path.

This file exists to provide a single, consistent mechanism to get asset URLs for UI components across dev and packaged app environments. It is designed to be safe in environments where window and window.electronAPI may be undefined (for example unit tests running in Node or server-side code), and it swallows exceptions during the resolution attempt in order to return a usable fallback path. The module exports a Promise-returning getAssetPath (default export) so callers can await asynchronous retrieval of an Electron-provided base path.

Important design decisions: path segments are encoded individually (encodeRelativeAssetPath) to preserve path delimiters while escaping special characters. ensureTrailingSlash is used before passing the base into new URL to avoid path concatenation pitfalls. A try/catch wraps the browser/electron branch so that any runtime issues (missing APIs, bad base value) revert to a safe fallback '/encodedRelativePath'.

key_constructs.name: encodeRelativeAssetPath
key_constructs.purpose: Normalize and encode a relative asset path by trimming leading slashes, splitting into segments, encoding each segment, and rejoining with '/'.
key_constructs.reasoning: Callers should treat this as the canonical sanitizer for incoming relative paths; it preserves segment boundaries so that encoded '/' characters are not produced and path composition with base URLs remains correct.

key_constructs.name: ensureTrailingSlash
key_constructs.purpose: Return the input with a trailing slash if it doesn't already end with one.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is used to ensure the base URL passed to new URL acts as a directory base rather than replacing the last path segment; important when composing with encodedRelativePath.

key_constructs.name: getAssetPath
key_constructs.purpose: Return a Promise<string> for the resolved asset URL, preferring dev server paths, then Electron base path, then a fallback root-relative path.
key_constructs.reasoning: This is the public API consumers should call to obtain asset URLs. It is async because it may await window.electronAPI.getAssetBasePath() in Electron; callers should await it and handle the returned string as an absolute or root-relative URL.

key_behaviors: returns encoded URL string for a requested asset
prefers web-served asset path when running on an HTTP(S) dev server
uses Electron-supplied base path when available
falls back to root-relative path when resolution fails

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming window.electronAPI.getAssetBasePath returns a filesystem path or URL without a scheme
pitfalls.consequence: new URL(base) will throw for non-absolute bases (e.g., plain filesystem paths without file://) causing fallback behavior; the exception is caught but you may lose intended base resolution.
pitfalls.prevention: When changing logic, preserve the try/catch and ensure base is normalized to an absolute URL before constructing new URL; do not remove ensureTrailingSlash unless you're confident about base formats.

pitfalls.mistake: Removing per-segment encoding (encodeURIComponent on each segment) or encoding the whole path as a single string
pitfalls.consequence: Slashes may be encoded incorrectly or special characters may be left unescaped, producing broken or unsafe URLs.
pitfalls.prevention: Keep the approach of splitting on '/' and encoding individual path segments to maintain correct path structure.

pitfalls.mistake: Assuming window or window.location is always present
pitfalls.consequence: In Node test environments or SSR-like contexts, accessing window without guards can throw; the existing code guards against it but removing guards would break tests or non-browser usage.
pitfalls.prevention: Retain checks for typeof window !== 'undefined' and guards around window.electronAPI.

key_sections: encodeRelativeAssetPath: how incoming paths are normalized and encoded
window.location protocol check: how dev server detection is performed
window.electronAPI.getAssetBasePath branch: how Electron base path is used with ensureTrailingSlash and new URL
fallback return: final root-relative string when other strategies are unavailable
skip_unless_needed: the simple ensureTrailingSlash helper (one-liner)
the try/catch wrapper if just reading behavior at a glance

related_files.relationship: Reads getAssetBasePath from window.electronAPI; the preload implementation is the provider of the Electron base path used here
related_files.reason_to_check: If the shape or semantics of getAssetBasePath change (signature, return value format), this module must be updated to handle the new format.

related_files.relationship: UI code that requests asset URLs (e.g., wallpapers) to render images; will call getAssetPath indirectly
related_files.reason_to_check: Visual regressions may occur if asset resolution behavior changes; check UI components that consume asset URLs.

tests_to_run: npm run test:browser (if changes interact with Electron API)

insights.title: CI now runs browser-mode Vitest tests
insights.problem: Browser-mode exporter tests were not executed in CI.
insights.root_cause: CI workflow lacked job to install Playwright deps and run test:browser.
insights.solution: Added a Test job that checks out, sets Node 22, npm ci, installs Playwright chromium dependencies, and runs npm run test:browser.
insights.Lesson Learned: Browser tests require additional CI steps (Playwright install with deps) and may change CI runtime requirements (chromium, swiftshader).

insights.title: Pin Node version via .nvmrc
insights.problem: Developers on varying Node versions could experience build/test inconsistencies.
insights.root_cause: No project-wide Node version pin prior to this change.
insights.solution: Add .nvmrc with Node 22.22.1 to align developer environments with CI.

insights.title: Add amber glass styles for speed items and increase hover opacity
insights.problem: New speed items needed a distinct visual style and glass overlay opacity felt low.
insights.root_cause: CSS didn't include variant styling for speed regions.
insights.solution: Added .glassAmber class for speed regions, updated hover/selected states and increased default overlay opacity.
insights.lesson_learned: Keep CSS modular and add new variant classes when introducing UI region types; small opacity tweaks can materially improve perceived affordance.

insights.title: Add red 'trim' glass style
insights.problem: Trim items needed distinct visual affordance from zoom items.
insights.root_cause: Single glass style only for zoomed items.
insights.solution: Introduced .glassRed styles for trim items (background, border, hover, selected).
insights.lesson_learned: Visual differentiation reduces user errors when multiple item types coexist on the same timeline.

insights.title: Add Linux build job to CI build workflow
insights.problem: Build workflow only produced macOS and Windows artifacts; Linux builds were missing.
insights.root_cause: Linux platform support was not included in CI build.yml.
insights.solution: Added build-linux job that checks out code, sets up node, installs deps, runs electron-builder install-app-deps and builds AppImage; uploads artifact (commit 78fbd30).
insights.lesson_learned: When expanding supported platforms, ensure CI has corresponding build jobs and environment (npx electron-builder install-app-deps) and that electron-builder settings include linux artifact configuration.
